body.text: 1.1 evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
body.translated_text: 1.1 Thus have I heard.

body.text: 1.2 ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā(n) rājagṛhe vihara(ti) gṛdhrakūṭe parvate || tena kha(lu samayena rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīpu)tro vṛjibhiḥ sārdhaṃ prativiruddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 1.2 At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain. At that time, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, was in conflict with the <s>Vṛjis</s>.

body.text: 1.3 sa evaṃ pariṣadi vācaṃ (bhāṣate) || aham imān vṛjīn ṛddhāṃś ca sphī(tāṃś ca kṣemāṃś ca subhikṣāṃś cākīrṇabahujanama)nuṣyāṃś cotsādayiṣyāmi vināśayiṣyāmy anayena vyasanam āpādayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 1.3 He spoke this word in his assembly: 'I shall overthrow these <s>Vṛjis</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people — I shall destroy them and bring them to ruin and calamity.'

body.text: 1.4 atha rājā mā(gadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputro varṣākāraṃ br)āhmaṇamagadhamahāmātram āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 1.4 Then the king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, addressed <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>:

body.text:
1.5 ehi tvaṃ varṣākāra yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrama || upetyāsmā(kaṃ vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandasvā)lpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchālpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca (su)khaṃ cānavadya(tāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca ||)
1.6 (evaṃ ca vada || rājā) māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputro vṛjibhiḥ sārdhaṃ prativiruddhaḥ || sa evaṃ pariṣadi vācaṃ bhāṣ(ate || aham imān vṛjīn ṛddhāṃś ca sphītāṃś ca kṣemāṃś ca) subhikṣāṃś cākīrṇabahujanamanu(ṣyāṃ)ś co(tsā)day(i)ṣyām(i) vināśayiṣyām(y) anayena vyasan(am āpādayiṣyāmi ||)
1.7 (kiṃ bhagavān āmantrayate || yathā varṣā)kāra sa bhagavāṃ vyākaroti tathaiv(odgṛhāṇa || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || a)vitathāvā(d)i(n)o hi bha(va)nti (tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ||)
1.8 (evaṃ deveti varṣākāro brāhma)ṇamagadhamahāmātro rājño mā(gadhasyājātaśatror vaidehīputrasya pratiśrutya) sarvaśvetaṃ vaḍab(ā)ratham abh(i)ruhy(a) ........

children.translated_text: ...surrounded by a retinue of young men, with a golden staff...

children.text:
........... (rājagṛhān niryāti bhagavato 'ntikenopadarśanāya bhagava)ntaṃ paryupāsanāyai || tasya yā(vad yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena gatvā yānād avatīrya padbhyām eva gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam abhiruhya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāmopetya) bhagavatā sārdhaṃ (saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃraṃjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte nyaṣīdat |)
1.9 (ekānte niṣaṇṇo varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamāhāmā)tr(o) bhagava(n)tam ida(m avocat ||)
1.10 (rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandaty alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchaty alpātaṅkatāṃ ca) pūrvavad yāv(at sparśa)vihāratāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text:
...he set forth from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having gone by chariot as far as the ground permitted for a chariot, he descended from the chariot and ascended <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain on foot. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached, he exchanged various friendly and cordial greetings with the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat down to one side.
1.9 Seated to one side, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
1.10 'The king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, bows his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and inquires about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction...' as before, up to '...and ease of living.'

body.translated_text:
1.5 'Come, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, go to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> is. Having approached, on our behalf bow your head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness in rising, his well-being, strength, happiness, blamelessness, and ease of living.'
1.6 'And say thus: "The king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, is in conflict with the <s>Vṛjis</s>. He speaks this word in his assembly: 'I shall overthrow these <s>Vṛjis</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people — I shall destroy them and bring them to ruin and calamity.'"'
1.7 '"What does the <s>Bhagavān</s> advise?" Whatever the <s>Bhagavān</s> declares, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, retain it just so. For what reason? <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones do not speak falsely.'
1.8 'So be it, Your Majesty,' replied <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, to the king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>. Mounting an all-white mare-chariot...

body.text:
1.11 su(khī bhavatu varṣākāra rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputras tvaṃ ca ||)
1.12 (rājā bhadanta māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputro vṛjibhiḥ sārdhaṃ) prativiru(ddhaḥ || sa evaṃ) pariṣadi vācaṃ bh(āṣate || aham imān vṛjīn ṛddhāṃś ca sphītāṃś ca kṣemāṃś ca subhikṣāṃś cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṃś cotsādayiṣyāmi vināśayi)ṣyāmy an(ayena vya)sanam āpādayiṣ(y)ā(mi ||)
1.13 (kiṃ bhagavāṅ gautama āmantrayate ||)
1.14 (ekam ahaṃ varṣākāra samayaṃ vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu viharāmi cāpāle c)aitye || tatra ma(yā vṛjīnāṃ) saptāparihā(ṇīyā dharmā deśitāḥ || yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛjaya imān saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān samādāya vartiṣyante vṛjiṣu ca saptāparihā)ṇīyā (dha)rmāḥ sandrakṣy(ante vṛddhir eva vṛjīnāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
1.15 (evam ahaṃ bhadantāsya bhagavato gautamasya saṃkṣiptena) bhā(ṣi)tasyāvi(bhaktasya vistareṇārthaṃ nājānāmi || bhagavān gautamo saṃkṣiptena bhāṣitasyārthaṃ vibhaktaṃ vistareṇa bhāṣeta || evam ahaṃ bhagavato gautama)sya saṃkṣiptena bhāṣitasyāvibh(aktaṃ vistareṇārthaṃ sādhu evājñāsyāmi ||)
1.16 (tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthito bha)gavantaṃ vījayamānaḥ || tatra bhaga(vān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
1.17 (kiṃ nu tvayānanda śrutaṃ vṛjayo 'bhīkṣṇasannipātā abhīkṣṇaṃ sannipātabahulā viharanti ||)
1.18 (śrutaṃ me bhadanta vṛjayo 'bhīkṣṇasannipātā abhīkṣṇaṃ sannipātabahulā viharanti ||)
1.19 (yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛjayo 'bhīkṣṇasannipātā abhīkṣṇaṃ sannipātabahulā vihariṣyanti vṛddhir eva vṛjīnāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
1.20 (kiṃ nu tvayānanda śrutaṃ vṛjayaḥ samagrāḥ sannipatanti samagrā vyuttiṣṭhanti samagrā vṛjikaraṇīyāni kurvanti ||)
1.21 (śrutaṃ me bha)danta vṛjayaḥ sama(grāḥ sannipatanti samagrā vyuttiṣṭhanti samagrā vṛjikaraṇīyāni kurvanti ||)
1.22 (yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛjayaḥ samagrāḥ sannipatiṣyanti sama)grā vyutthāsyanti (samagrā vṛjikaraṇīyāni kariṣyanti vṛddhir eva vṛjīnāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
1.23 (kiṃ nu tvayānanda śrutaṃ vṛjayo 'pra)ṇihitaṃ na praṇi(dadhati praṇihitaṃ ca na samucchindati yathāprajñaptaṃ vṛjidharmaṃ samādāya vartante ||)
1.24 (śrutaṃ me bhadanta vṛjayo 'praṇihitaṃ na praṇidadhati praṇihi)taṃ ca na samucchin(da)()n(ti yathāprajñaptaṃ vṛjidharmaṃ samādāya vartante ||)
1.25 (yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛjayo 'praṇihitaṃ na praṇidhāsyanti praṇihitaṃ ca na samucchetsyanti yathāprajñaptaṃ) vṛjidharmaṃ samādā(ya vartiṣyante vṛddhir eva vṛjīnāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)

body.translated_text:
1.11 'May the king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, be happy, and you as well, <s>Varṣākāra</s>.'
1.12 'The king, Venerable Sir, of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, is in conflict with the <s>Vṛjis</s>. He speaks this word in his assembly: "I shall overthrow these <s>Vṛjis</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people — I shall destroy them and bring them to ruin and calamity."'
1.13 'What does the Venerable <s>Gautama</s> advise?'
1.14 'At one time, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, I was dwelling among the <s>Vṛjis</s>, in their territory, at the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine. There I taught the <s>Vṛjis</s> seven conditions of non-decline (<s>saptāparihāṇīya dharma</s>). As long as, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>Vṛjis</s> shall take up and practice these seven conditions of non-decline, and as long as the seven conditions of non-decline shall be seen among the <s>Vṛjis</s>, only growth is to be expected for the <s>Vṛjis</s> in wholesome qualities, not decline.'
1.15 'Thus, Venerable Sir, I do not understand in detail the meaning of this brief statement of the Venerable <s>Gautama</s>. May the Venerable <s>Gautama</s> speak at length the meaning of this brief statement, so analyzed. Thus I shall rightly understand the meaning of the Venerable <s>Gautama</s>'s brief statement.'
1.16 At that time, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was standing behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, fanning him. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:
1.17 'Have you heard, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> hold frequent assemblies and dwell abundantly in frequent assemblies?'
1.18 'I have heard, Venerable Sir, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> hold frequent assemblies and dwell abundantly in frequent assemblies.'
1.19 'As long as, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>Vṛjis</s> shall hold frequent assemblies and dwell abundantly in frequent assemblies, only growth is to be expected for the <s>Vṛjis</s> in wholesome qualities, not decline.'
1.20 'Have you heard, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> assemble in harmony, rise in harmony, and carry out <s>Vṛji</s> affairs in harmony?'
1.21 'I have heard, Venerable Sir, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> assemble in harmony, rise in harmony, and carry out <s>Vṛji</s> affairs in harmony.'
1.22 'As long as, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>Vṛjis</s> shall assemble in harmony, rise in harmony, and carry out <s>Vṛji</s> affairs in harmony, only growth is to be expected for the <s>Vṛjis</s> in wholesome qualities, not decline.'
1.23 'Have you heard, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> do not establish what has not been established, do not abolish what has been established, and take up and practice the ancient <s>Vṛji</s> customs as they were prescribed?'
1.24 'I have heard, Venerable Sir, that the <s>Vṛjis</s> do not establish what has not been established, do not abolish what has been established, and take up and practice the ancient <s>Vṛji</s> customs as they were prescribed.'
1.25 'As long as, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>Vṛjis</s> shall not establish what has not been established, shall not abolish what has been established, and shall take up and practice the ancient <s>Vṛji</s> customs as prescribed, only growth is to be expected for the <s>Vṛjis</s> in wholesome qualities, not decline.'
1.26 'Have you heard, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Vṛji</s> matriarchs, the <s>Vṛji</s> maidens — those who are protected by their fathers, protected by their mothers, protected by their brothers, protected by their sisters, protected by their fathers-in-law, protected by their mothers-in-law, protected by their relatives, protected by their clans, who have guardians with authority to punish, who have husbands, who are maidens belonging to others, even those encircled merely by a garland — that in regard to such women they do not

body.text: 1.35 (kiṃ nu tvayānanda) śrutaṃ vṛjīnām arhatā(m anti)ke tīvracetasa ārakṣāsmṛtiḥ pratyupasthitā kaccid anāgatāś cārhanta āgaccheyur āgatāś cābhirameraṃs te ca na vihanyerañ cīvarapiṇḍapā(taśayanāsanaglā)napratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ ||

1.36 śrutaṃ me bhadanta vṛjīnām arhatām antike tīvracetasa ārakṣāsmṛtiḥ pratyupasthitā kaccid anāgatāś cārhanta āga(ccheyur āgatāś cā)bhirameraṃs te ca na vihanyerañ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ ||

1.37 yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛ(jī)nām arhatām antike tīvracetasa (ārakṣāsmṛtiḥ) pratyupasthitā bhaviṣyati kaccid anāgatāś cārhanta āgaccheyur āgatāś cābhiramera(ṃ)s te ca na vihanyerañ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkā(rair vṛddhir eva vṛjī)nāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||

1.38 yāvac ca varṣākāra vṛjaya imān saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān samādāya vartiṣyante vṛjiṣu ca saptāparihā(ṇīyā dharmāḥ sandrakṣyan)te vṛddhir eva vṛjīnāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||

1.40 ekaikena tāvad bho gautamāṅgena samanvāgatā vṛjayo 'gamanīyāḥ syū rājño māga(dhasyājātaśa)tror vaidehīputrasya kaḥ punar vādaḥ sarvaiḥ ||
1.41 hanta bho gautama gamiṣyāmo bahukṛtyāḥ smo bahukaraṇīyāḥ ||
1.42 yasyedānīṃ varṣākāra kāla(ṃ) manyase ||
1.43 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||

2.1 tatra bhagavān (āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate || yāvanto bhikṣavo gṛdhra)kūṭaparvatam upaniśritya viharanti tān sarvān upasthānaśālāyāṃ (sannipātaya ||)
2.2 (evaṃ bhadantety) āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yāvanto bhikṣavo gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvata(m upaniśritya) viharanti tān sarvān upasthānaśālāyāṃ sannipātayitvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma || upetya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt || ekānt(a)sthit(a) ā(yuṣmān ānando) bhagavantam idam avocat ||

2.3 yāvanto bhadanta bhikṣavo gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam upaniśritya viharanti te sarva upasthānaśālāyāṃ sannipatitāḥ || yasyedānīṃ bhagavāṅ kālaṃ man(yate ||)
2.4 (atha bhagavān ye)nopasthānaśālā tenopajagāma || upetya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣī(dat) || niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantra(ya)te sma ||

2.5 saptāhaṃ vo bhikṣavo 'parihā(ṇīyān dharmān deśayiṣyā)mi tāñ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || saptā(parihāṇīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.6 (yāvac ca bhikṣavo 'bhīkṣṇasannipātā a)bhīkṣṇaṃ sannipātabahulā vihariṣyanti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃ(kṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.7 (yāvac ca bhikṣavaḥ samagrāḥ) sannipatiṣyanti samagrā vyutthāsyanti samagrāḥ saṃghakaraṇīyā(ni kariṣyanti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.8 (yāva)c (ca) bhikṣavo 'praṇihitaṃ na praṇidhāsyanti praṇihitaṃ ca na (samucchetsyanti yathā)prajñap(t)i(kāṃ śi)kṣāṃ samādāy(a vartiṣyante vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā) k(u)śalānāṃ dharmā(ṇ)āṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||

2.9 yāvac ca bhik(ṣavas tṛṣṇāyāḥ paunarbhavi)kyā (nandirāga)sahagatāyās ta(tra tatrābhinandinyā vaśaṃ na gacchanti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.10 (yāvac ca bhikṣavo ye te bhikṣavaḥ) sthavirā rāt(r)ijñāś cirapravrajitā ............... (tān satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūja)yiṣyanti teṣāṃ vacanaṃ (ś)r(ota)v(y)aṃ ma(ṃsyante vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.11 (yāvac ca bhikṣavo 'raṇyavanaprasthāni) prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvasiṣyan(ti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.12 (yāvac ca bhikṣavaḥ sabrahmacāriṇām antike tī)vracetasa ārakṣāsmṛtiḥ pratyupasth(itā kaccid anāgatāś ca sabrahmacāriṇa āgaccheyur āgatāś cābhirameraṃs te ca na vihanyerañ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglā)napratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pr(atikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.13 (yāvac) ca bhikṣava i(mān saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān samādāya vartiṣyante bhikṣuṣu) ca saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ sandrakṣyante vṛd(dh)i(r eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśa)lānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihā(ṇiḥ ||)
2.14 (aparān api saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān deśayiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇuta) sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhā(ṣiṣye || saptāparihāṇīyā dha)rmāḥ katame ||

2.15 yāvac ca bhikṣavaḥ śā(stāraṃ satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti śāstā)raṃ satkṛtvā gurukṛtvā mānayitvā pū(jayitvopaśri)tya vihariṣyanti dharmaṃ śikṣām anuśā(sanam apramādaṃ pratisaṃstaraṃ samādhiṃ satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣya)nti pūjayiṣyanti samādhiṃ satkṛtvā (gurukṛtvā) māna(yitvā pūjayitvopaśritya vihariṣyanti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.16 Nur im Tib.
2.17 (aparā)n api saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān de(śa)yiṣyāmi (tāñ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.18 (yāvac ca bhikṣavo na karmārāmā bhaviṣyanti na bh)āṣyārāmā na nidrār(āmā) na sa(ṃ)gaṇi(kārāmā) ............... (vi)śeṣādhigamenā(nta)rāvasā(n) ....... (vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.19 Nur im Tib.
2.20 (aparān api saptāparihā)ṇīyān dharmān deśayiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇuta (sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.21 (yāvac ca bhikṣavaḥ śrāddhā bhaviṣyanti hrīmanto bhaviṣyanty) avatrāpiṇa ārabdhavīryā u(pasthitasmṛtayaḥ samāhitāḥ prajñāvanto bhaviṣyanti vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.22 Nur im Tib.
2.23 (aparā)n api saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān deśa(yiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.24 (yāvac ca bhikṣavo dharmajñā arthajñā)ḥ kālajñā mātraj(ñ)ā ātmajñāḥ pariṣa(jjñāḥ pudgalavarāvarajñā vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.25 Nur im Tib.
2.26 (aparān api saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān deśayiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.27 (yāvac ca bhikṣavaḥ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayiṣyanti vivekaniśritaṃ virāganiśritaṃ nirodhaniśritaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ dharmavicayavīryaprītiprasrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayiṣyanti vivekaniśritaṃ virāganiśritaṃ nirodhaniśritaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.28 (yāvac ca bhikṣava imān saptāparihāṇīyān dharmān samādāya vartiṣyante bhikṣuṣu ca saptāparihāṇīyā dharmāḥ sandrakṣyante vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.29 (ṣaḍ ahaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ saṃraṃjanīyān dharmān deśayiṣyāmi tāñ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || ṣaṭ saṃraṃjanīyā dharmāḥ katame ||)
2.30 maitraṃ me kāyakarma pratyupasthitaṃ bhaviṣyati śāstu(r a)ntike vijñ(ā)nāñ ca sabrahmacār(i)ṇām || ayaṃ dharmaḥ saṃraṃjanīyaḥ priyakaraṇo gurukaraṇo manāpakaraṇaḥ priyatvāya gurutvāya gauravāya bhāvanāya saṃgrahāya samādhaye 'vigrahāyāvivādāya ekotībhāvāya saṃvartate ||
body.translated_text:
2.15 As long as, O monks, they will honor the Teacher, respect, esteem, and worship him; having honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, they will dwell relying upon him — they will honor the <s>Dharma</s>, the training, the instruction, heedfulness, and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), respect, esteem, and worship <s>samādhi</s>; having honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped <s>samādhi</s>, they will dwell relying upon it — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.
2.16 [Preserved only in Tibetan.]
2.17 'I shall teach yet another seven conditions leading to non-decline (<s>aparihāṇīya dharmas</s>). Listen to them; well and thoroughly bear them in mind, I shall speak. What are the seven conditions of non-decline?'
2.18 'As long as, O monks, they will not be devoted to work, not devoted to talk, not devoted to sleep, not devoted to company ... [lacuna] ... with respect to attainment of distinction ... [lacuna] ... only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.'
2.19 [Preserved only in Tibetan.]
2.20 'I shall teach yet another seven conditions leading to non-decline. Listen to them; well and thoroughly bear them in mind, I shall speak. What are the seven conditions of non-decline?'
2.21 'As long as, O monks, they will be faithful, possessed of moral shame (<s>hrī</s>), possessed of moral dread (<s>apatrāpya</s>), of aroused energy, with mindfulness established, concentrated, and wise — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.'
2.22 [Preserved only in Tibetan.]
2.23 'I shall teach yet another seven conditions leading to non-decline. Listen to them; well and thoroughly bear them in mind, I shall speak. What are the seven conditions of non-decline?'
2.24 'As long as, O monks, they are knowers of the <s>Dharma</s>, knowers of meaning, knowers of the proper time, knowers of measure, knowers of the self, knowers of assemblies, and knowers of the superiority and inferiority of persons — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.'
2.25 [Preserved only in Tibetan.]
2.26 'I shall teach yet another seven conditions leading to non-decline. Listen to them; well and thoroughly bear them in mind, I shall speak. What are the seven conditions of non-decline?'
2.27 'As long as, O monks, they will cultivate the mindfulness factor of awakening (<s>smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga</s>) based on seclusion, dispassion, cessation, and ripening into relinquishment; they will cultivate the <s>Dharma</s>-investigation, energy, rapture, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity factors of awakening based on seclusion, dispassion, cessation, and ripening into relinquishment — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.'
2.28 'As long as, O monks, they will undertake and practice these seven conditions of non-decline, and as long as the seven conditions of non-decline will be seen among the monks — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.'
2.29 'I shall teach you, O monks, six principles of harmony (<s>saṃraṃjanīya dharmas</s>). Listen to them; well and thoroughly bear them in mind, I shall speak. What are the six principles of harmony?'
2.30 'My friendly bodily action (<s>maitraṃ kāyakarma</s>) will be established toward the Teacher and toward wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. This <s>dharma</s> is conducive to harmony, productive of affection, productive of respect, productive of esteem; it conduces to friendliness, to respect, to reverence, to cultivation, to solidarity, to concord, to non-conflict, to non-dispute, and to unity.'

children.translated_text: 2.31 Friendly verbal action (<s>maitraṃ vākkarma</s>).
2.32 Friendly mental action (<s>maitraṃ manaskarma</s>).

children.text: 2.33 ye te lābhā dhārmikā dharmalabdhā antataḥ pātragatāḥ pātraparyāpannās tadrūpeṣu lābheṣu sādhāraṇaparibhojino bhaviṣyāmo 'pratiguptabhojin(aḥ) sārdhaṃ vijñaiḥ sabrahmacāribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 2.33 Whatever righteous gains are obtained in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, even down to what has gone into the bowl and is contained in the bowl — with respect to such gains, we will be sharers in common use, without hidden eating, together with our wise fellow practitioners of the holy life.

body.text: ayaṃ dharmaḥ saṃraṃjanī(yaḥ) pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> is conducive to harmony, as before.

body.text: 2.34 yāni tāni śīlāny akhaṇḍāny acchidrāṇy aśabalāny akalmāṣāṇi bhujiṣyāṇy aparāmṛṣṭāni susamāptāni susamādattāni vijñapraśastāny agarhitāni vijñais tadrūpaiḥ śīlaiḥ śīlasāmānyagatā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sārdhaṃ vijñaiḥ sa(b)r(a)hmac(ā)ribhiḥ || ayaṃ dharmaḥ saṃraṃjanīyaḥ pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: 2.34 Whatever precepts (<s>śīla</s>) are unbroken, uncorrupted, unspotted, unblemished, liberating, not grasped at, well-accomplished, well-undertaken, praised by the wise, blameless among the wise — with respect to such precepts, we will be united in moral conduct with our wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. This <s>dharma</s> is conducive to harmony, as before.

body.text: 2.35 yeyaṃ dṛṣṭir āryā nairyāṇikā nairvedhikā niryāti tatkarasamyagduḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai tadrūpayā dṛṣṭyā dṛṣṭisāmānyagatā bhaviṣyāmaḥ sārdhaṃ vijñaiḥ sabrahmacāribhiḥ || ayaṃ dharmaḥ saṃraṃjanīyaḥ pūrvavad yāvad ekotībhāvā(ya saṃ)vartate ||
body.translated_text: 2.35 That noble view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) which is emancipating (<s>nairyāṇikā</s>), penetrating (<s>nairvedhikā</s>), which leads one who acts accordingly to the complete destruction of suffering, to making an end of suffering — with respect to such a view, we will be united in view with our wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. This <s>dharma</s> is conducive to harmony, as before, up to 'conduces to unity.'

body.text:
2.36 (yāvac ca bhikṣava imān ṣaṭ saṃraṃjanīyān dharmān samādāya vartiṣyante bhikṣuṣu ca ṣaṭ saṃraṃjanīyā dharmāḥ sandrakṣyante vṛddhir eva bhikṣūṇāṃ pratikāṃkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na parihāṇiḥ ||)
2.37 <Nur Chin.>
<Hier im Tib. Uddāna>
body.translated_text:
2.36 As long as, O monks, they will undertake and practice these six principles of harmony, and as long as the six principles of harmony will be seen among the monks — only growth is to be expected for the monks in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, not decline.
2.37 [Preserved only in Chinese.]
[Here in the Tibetan, an <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse).]

body.text:
3.1 (tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate || āgamayānanda yena pāṭaligrāmakaḥ ||)
3.2 (evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt || atha bhagavān sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena magadheṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran antarā ca pāṭaligrāmakam antarā ca rājagṛhaṃ rājāgārake rātrīṃ viharati veṇuyaṣṭikām upaniśritya ||)
3.3 (atha bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma || caturṇāṃ bhikṣava āryasatyānām ajñānād adarśanād anavabodhād aprativedhād idaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ saṃdhāvitaṃ saṃsṛtaṃ mayā yuṣmābhir eva ca || katameṣāṃ caturṇām ||)
3.4 (duḥkhasya duḥkhasamudayasya duḥkhanirodhasya duḥkhanirodhagāminyāḥ pratipado 'jñānād adarśanād anavabodhād aprativedhād idaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ saṃdhāvitaṃ saṃsṛtaṃ mayā yuṣmā)bhir eva ca ||
body.translated_text:
3.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>.'
3.2 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Magadhan</s> territories with the community of monks, between <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> and <s>Rājagṛha</s>, dwelt for a night at the Royal House (<s>Rājāgāraka</s>), near <s>Veṇuyaṣṭikā</s>.
3.3 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Through ignorance of the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), O monks, through not seeing, not understanding, not penetrating them, this long course has been traversed and wandered through, by me and by you as well. Of which four?'
3.4 'Through ignorance of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the origin of suffering (<s>duḥkhasamudaya</s>), the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodha</s>), and the path leading to the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad</s>) — through not seeing, not understanding, not penetrating them, this long course has been traversed and wandered through, by me and by you as well.'

body.text: 3.5 tad idaṃ duḥkha(m āryasatyam anuviddhaṃ p)r(ati)viddham ucch(i)nnā bhavanetrī vikṣīṇo jātisaṃsāro nāstīdānī(ṃ) punarbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 3.5 Now this noble truth of suffering has been thoroughly known and penetrated; the conduit to existence (<s>bhavanetrī</s>) has been cut off, the cycle of birth-and-death (<s>jātisaṃsāra</s>) has been exhausted — there is now no further rebirth.

body.text: 3.6 duḥkhasamudayo duḥkhanirodho duḥkhanirodhagāminī prati(pad āryasatyam anuviddhaṃ) p(ra)t(i)viddham ucchin(n)ā bhavanetrī vikṣīṇo jātisaṃsāro nāstīdānīṃ punarbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 3.6 The origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering — the noble truth — has been thoroughly known and penetrated; the conduit to existence has been cut off, the cycle of birth-and-death has been exhausted — there is now no further rebirth.

children.translated_text: 3.7 [Preserved only in Tibetan.]
3.8 Of the four noble truths,
from not seeing them as they truly are,

body.text: saṃsṛtaṃ (d)īrgha(m adhvānaṃ

children.translated_text: both I and you as well. (1)

3.9 Those truths have been seen,
the conduit to existence has been uprooted;

body.translated_text: we wandered this long course —

body.text: vikṣīṇo jātisaṃsāro

children.translated_text: there is now no further rebirth. (2)

body.translated_text: the cycle of birth-and-death is exhausted,

body.text: 4.1 tatra bha(gavān āyuṣmantam ānan)dam (ā)mantrayate || āgamayānanda yena pāṭaligrāmakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 4.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>.'

body.text: 4.2 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmā(n ā)nan(d)o bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt || atha bha(gavā)n (magadheṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran pāṭa)ligrāmakam anuprāptaḥ pāṭaligrāmake viharati pāṭalake caitye ||
body.translated_text: 4.2 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Magadhan</s> territories, arrived at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> dwelt at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>, at the <s>Pāṭalaka</s> shrine.

body.text: 4.3 aśrau(ṣu)ḥ pāṭa(ligrāmī)y(ak)ā brāhmaṇagṛhapata(y)o (bhagavān gautamo magadheṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran pāṭa)ligrāmakam anuprāptaḥ pāṭaligrāmake viharati pā(ṭa)lake caitye ||
body.translated_text: 4.3 The <s>Brahmin</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> heard: 'The <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Magadhan</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>. He is dwelling at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>, at the <s>Pāṭalaka</s> shrine.'

body.text:
4.4 (śrutvā ca punaḥ saṃ)ghāt saṃghaṃ pūgāt pūgaṃ saṃ(gamya samāgamya pāṭaligrāmakān niṣkramya yena) bhagavāṃs tenopajagmur upetya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikān(te nyaṣīdan ||)
4.5 ekānt(ani)ṣaṇṇān pāṭaligrāmīya(kān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn bhagavān i)dam a(vo)cat ||
body.translated_text:
4.4 Having heard, then from group to group, from assembly to assembly, having come together and met, departing from <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>, they approached to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat to one side.
4.5 To the <s>Brahmin</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this:

body.text: 4.6 pañceme brāhmaṇagṛhapataya ādīnavāḥ pramāde || katame pañca ||
body.translated_text: 4.6 'There are these five dangers, O <s>Brahmin</s> householders, in heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). What five?'

body.text:
4.7 iha br(āhma)ṇag(ṛha)patayaḥ pramattaḥ pramād(ādhikaraṇahetor) mahatīṃ bhogajyāniṃ nigacchati || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇah(eto)r mahatī(ṃ) bhogajyāniṃ nigacchati || ayaṃ prath(ama) ād(īnavaḥ pramāde ||)
4.8 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetor yāṃ yām eva pariṣadam upasaṃkrāmati yadi vā kṣatriyapa(r)i(ṣadaṃ yadi vā brāh)maṇapariṣadaṃ yadi vā gṛhapatipariṣadaṃ yadi vā śramaṇapariṣadaṃ tatra tatra madgur upasaṃkrāmaty anudagro 'viśāradaḥ || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapata(yaḥ) p(ra)mattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetor yāṃ yām eva pariṣadam upasaṃkrāmati pūrvavad yāvad aviśāradaḥ || ayaṃ dvitīya ādīnavaḥ pramāde ||
body.translated_text:
4.7 'Here, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, incurs great loss of wealth. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, incurs great loss of wealth — this is the first danger of heedlessness.'
4.8 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, whichever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, or an assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or an assembly of householders, or an assembly of <s>śramaṇas</s> — there he approaches timidly, dispirited and unconfident. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, whichever assembly he approaches... as before, up to ...unconfident — this is the second danger of heedlessness.'

body.text: 4.9 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattasya pramādādhikaraṇahetor digvidikṣu (pā)pako 'va(rṇo 'kīrtiśa)bdaśl(o)ko 'bhyudgacchati || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattasya pramādādhikaraṇahetor digvidikṣu pāpako 'varṇo 'kīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhy(ud)g(ac)chati || ayaṃ tṛtīya ādīnavaḥ pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.9 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, for a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, an evil reputation, a bad name, an ill report spreads in all directions. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, for a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, an evil reputation, a bad name, an ill report spreads in all directions — this is the third danger of heedlessness.'

body.text: 4.10 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetor vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetor vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti || ayaṃ caturtha ādīnavaḥ pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.10 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, dies full of remorse. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, dies full of remorse — this is the fourth danger of heedlessness.'

body.text: 4.11 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetoḥ kāyasya bhedān narakeṣūpapadyate || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pramattaḥ pramādādhikaraṇahetoḥ kāyasya bhedān narakeṣūpapadyate || ayaṃ pañcama ādīnavaḥ pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.11 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, upon the breaking up of the body, is reborn in the hells. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedless person, on account of heedlessness, upon the breaking up of the body, is reborn in the hells — this is the fifth danger of heedlessness.'

body.text: 4.12 pañca tv ime brāhmaṇagṛhapataya ānuśaṃsā apramāde || katame pañca ||
body.translated_text: 4.12 'But there are, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, five benefits of heedfulness. What five?'

body.text: 4.13 iha brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor na mahatīṃ bhogajyāniṃ nigacchati || yad br(ā)hmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor na mahatī(ṃ) bhogajyāniṃ nigacchati || ayaṃ prathama ānuś(aṃ)so 'pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.13 'Here, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, does not incur great loss of wealth. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, does not incur great loss of wealth — this is the first benefit of heedfulness.'

body.text: 4.14 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor yāṃ yām eva pariṣadam upasaṃkrāmati yadi vā kṣatriyapariṣadaṃ yadi vā brāhmaṇapariṣadaṃ yadi vā gṛhapatipariṣadaṃ yadi vā śramaṇapariṣadaṃ tatra tatrāmadgur upasaṃkrāmaty udagro viśāradaḥ || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor yāṃ yām eva pariṣadam upasaṃkrāmati pūrvavad yāvad viśāradaḥ || ayaṃ dvitīya ānuśaṃso 'pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.14 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, whichever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, or an assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or an assembly of householders, or an assembly of <s>śramaṇas</s> — there he approaches without timidity, spirited and confident. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, whichever assembly he approaches... as before, up to ...confident — this is the second benefit of heedfulness.'

body.text: 4.15 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramattasyāpramādādhikaraṇahetor digvidikṣūdāraḥ kalyāṇaḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgacchati || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramattasyāpramādādhikaraṇahetor digvidikṣūdāraḥ kalyāṇaḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgacchati || ayaṃ tṛtīya ānuśaṃso 'pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.15 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, for a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, a noble, auspicious reputation, a good name and report, spreads in all directions. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, for a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, a noble, auspicious reputation, a good name and report, spreads in all directions — this is the third benefit of heedfulness.'

body.text: 4.16 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor na vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetor na vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti || ayaṃ caturtha ānuśaṃso 'pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.16 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, does not die full of remorse. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, does not die full of remorse — this is the fourth benefit of heedfulness.'

body.text: 4.17 punar aparaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetoḥ kāyasya bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate || yad brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'pramatto 'pramādādhikaraṇahetoḥ k(āyasya) bhedāt sugatau sv(a)rgaloke deveṣūpapadyate || ayaṃ pañcama ānuśaṃso 'pramāde ||
body.translated_text: 4.17 'Furthermore, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, upon the breaking up of the body, is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the <s>devas</s>. That, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders, a heedful person, on account of heedfulness, upon the breaking up of the body, is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the <s>devas</s> — this is the fifth benefit of heedfulness.'

body.text:
4.18 (atha bhagavān pāṭaligrāmīyakān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati || anekaparyāyeṇa dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvā tūṣṇīm abhūt ||)
4.19 atha pāṭaligrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttar(āsa)ṅgaṃ kṛtvā ye(na) bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocan || adhivāsayatv asmākaṃ bhagavān āvasathe rātriṃvāsāya || adhivāsayati bhagavān pāṭaligrāmīyak(ā)nāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena ||
body.translated_text:
4.18 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s> with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them in many ways with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
4.19 Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes on one shoulder, extending their joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to stay the night in our rest-house.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s> by his silence.

body.text: 4.20 atha pāṭaligrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānt(āḥ) ||
body.translated_text: 4.20 Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent by his silence, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: 5.1 atha bhagavān aciraprakrāntān pāṭaligrāmīyakān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn viditvā bahir āvasathasya pādau prakṣālyāvasathaṃ praviśya nyaṣīdat ||
body.translated_text: 5.1 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s> had recently departed, washed his feet outside the rest-house, entered the rest-house, and sat down.

body.text:
5.2 (tena samayena varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātra udyuktaḥ pāṭaligrāmakaṃ nagaraṃ māpayituṃ vṛjīnāṃ pratighātārtham || tadā pāṭaligrāmake mahāśakyamahāśakyā devatā vastuni pratigṛhṇanti ||)
5.3 paryaṅkam ābhujyarjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtim upasthāpyādrākṣīd bhagavān āvasathe divāvihāropagato divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa pāṭaligrāmake mahāśakyamahāśakyā devatā vastūni pratigṛhṇanti || dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sāyāhne pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāyāvasathād avatīryāvasathapracchāyāyāṃ p(u)rastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat ||
body.translated_text:
5.2 At that time, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, was engaged in building a fortified city at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> to counter the <s>Vṛjis</s>. At that time, powerful and mighty deities were taking possession of sites in <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>.
5.3 Having crossed his legs, straightened his body, and established mindfulness before him, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, while engaged in daytime meditation in the rest-house, saw with his divine eye — purified and surpassing the human — that powerful and mighty deities were taking possession of sites in <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>. Having seen this, in the evening, having emerged from his seclusion, having descended from the rest-house, in the shade of the rest-house, before the assembly of monks, he sat down on a seat that had been prepared.

body.text: 5.4 niṣadya bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 5.4 Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: ka ānandodyuktaḥ pāṭaligrāmakaṃ n(agara)ṃ māpayitum ||
body.translated_text: 'Who, <s>Ānanda</s>, is engaged in building a fortified city at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>?'

body.text: 5.5 varṣākāro bhadanta brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātra udyuktaḥ pāṭaligrāmakaṃ nagaraṃ māpayituṃ vṛjīnāṃ pratighātārtham ||
body.translated_text: 5.5 '<s>Varṣākāra</s>, Venerable Sir, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, is engaged in building a fortified city at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> to counter the <s>Vṛjis</s>.'

body.text: 5.6 sādhu sādhv (ānanda + + varṣā)kāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro yathā (devais trāyastriṃśaiḥ sārdham) + + + + + + + ||
body.translated_text: 5.6 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Ānanda</s>! <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, as if consulting with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods...'

body.text:
5.7 (atrāham āna)ndādrākṣam āvasathe divāvihāropagat(aḥ pāṭaligrāmake mahāśakyamahāśa)kyā devatā vas(tū)ni p(rat)i(gṛhṇanti ||)
5.8 (yasminn ānanda pradeśe mahāśakyamahāśakyā de)vatā vastūni pratigṛhṇanti m(ahāśakyānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tasmin pradeśe) c(i)ttaṃ krāmati yaduta vā(sāya ||)
5.9 yasmin pradeśe madhyā devatā v(astū)ni pratigṛhṇanti madhyānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tasmin pradeśe cittaṃ krāmati yaduta vāsāya ||
body.translated_text:
5.7 'Here, <s>Ānanda</s>, I saw while engaged in daytime meditation in the rest-house — powerful and mighty deities were taking possession of sites in <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>.'
5.8 'In whichever site, <s>Ānanda</s>, powerful and mighty deities take possession, the minds of powerful and mighty humans are drawn to that site, namely, for habitation.'
5.9 'In whichever site middling deities take possession of sites, the minds of middling humans are drawn to that site, namely, for habitation.'

body.text: 5.10 yasmi(n pra)d(e)śe nīcā devatā vastūni pratigṛhṇanti nīcānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tas(min) pradeśe cittaṃ krāmati yaduta vāsāya ||
body.translated_text: 5.10 'In whichever site lowly deities take possession of sites, the minds of lowly humans are drawn to that site, namely, for habitation.'

body.text: 5.11 asminn ānanda pāṭaligrāmake mahāśakyamahā(śa)kyā devatā vastūni pratigṛhṇanti || asmin pradeśe mahāśakyānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cittaṃ kramiṣyati yaduta vāsāya ||
body.translated_text: 5.11 'In this <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, powerful and mighty deities are taking possession of sites. In this site, the minds of powerful and mighty humans will be drawn, namely, for habitation.'

body.text: 5.12 yāvad evānandāryā āvāsā ā(ryā) vyavahārā āryā vāṇir yathaitad agraṃ bhaviṣyati puṭabh(edanā)nāṃ yaduta pāṭaliputraṃ nagaraṃ ||
body.translated_text: 5.12 'As far as, <s>Ānanda</s>, there are noble dwelling places, noble commerce, and noble speech — so far this will be the foremost of trading centers, namely, the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.'

body.text: 5.13 tasya trayo 'ntarāyā veditavyā agnito 'py udakato ('py a)bhyantarato 'pi mithobhedāt ||
body.translated_text: 5.13 'Three dangers are to be expected for it: from fire, from water, and from internal dissension and mutual discord.'

body.text: 6.1 aśrauṣīd varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātraḥ || bhagavān gautamo magadheṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran pāṭaligrāmakam anuprāptaḥ pā(ṭa)ligrāmake viharati pāṭalake caitye || (paryu)pā(sate ta)ṃ pāṭaligr(āmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛha)patayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 6.1 <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, heard: 'The Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, while wandering on his journey through the <s>Magadha</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> and is dwelling at <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> in the <s>Pāṭalaka</s> shrine. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Pāṭaligrāma</s> are attending upon him.'

body.text: 6.2 śrutvā ca punaḥ pāṭaligrāmakān niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃs t(e)nopajagāma || upetya bhagavat(ā) sā(r)dh(aṃ) s(aṃ)mukh(aṃ saṃ)m(o)dan(īṃ) saṃra(ṃ)j(anīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisār)yaikānte nyaṣīdat ||
body.translated_text: 6.2 Having heard this, he set out from <s>Pāṭaligrāmaka</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he exchanged various friendly and cordial greetings with the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat down to one side.

body.text: 6.3 ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ varṣākāraṃ brāhmaṇamagadha(ma)hāmātraṃ bhagavān dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayati samādāpayati samutte(jayati saṃ)praharṣayati || anekaparyāyeṇa dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayitvā samādāpa(yi)tvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayi(t)vā tūṣṇīm abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 6.3 The <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.

body.text: 6.4 atha v(arṣākā)ro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātra utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā ye(na) bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 6.4 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 6.5 adhivāsayatu me bhavāṅ gautamaḥ śvo bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena || adhivāsayati bha(ga)vān varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena ||
body.translated_text: 6.5 'May the Venerable <s>Gautama</s> consent to accept tomorrow's meal together with the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks).' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, by his silence.

body.text: 6.6 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā (bhagava)to bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 6.6 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: 6.7 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātras tām eva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyam evotthāyāsanakāni prajñapyodakamaṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati || samayo bho gautamo sadyo bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhavāṅ gautamaḥ kālaṃ manyate ||
body.translated_text: 6.7 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, that very night prepared various pure and excellent foods, hard and soft. Rising early in the morning, having arranged the seats and set up the water-jar, he sent a messenger to inform the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the time: 'It is time, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>; the meal is ready. May the Venerable <s>Gautama</s> come at whatever time he sees fit.'

body.text: 6.8 atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivasya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasya bhaktābhisāras tenopajagāma || upetya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat ||
body.translated_text: 6.8 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by and at the head of the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>, went to the place where the meal of <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, was arranged. Having arrived, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: 6.9 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātraḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayati saṃpravārayati || śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ sauvarṇaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purato 'sthāt || āyācamāna evaṃ cāha ||
body.translated_text: 6.9 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, knowing that the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent foods, hard and soft. Having served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent foods, hard and soft, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating and had washed his hands and put away his bowl, he took a golden ewer and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, making a request and speaking thus:

body.text: 6.10 ito dānād yaḥ puṇyābhiṣyandaḥ kuśalābhiṣyandaḥ sa bhavatu pāṭaliputravāstavyānāṃ devatānāṃ dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya || teṣāñ ca nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādiśasva ||
body.translated_text: 6.10 'May the overflow of merit, the overflow of wholesome qualities from this gift, be for the long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness of the deities dwelling in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. And may you dedicate the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (merit-dedication) in their names.'

body.text: 6.11 atha bhagavān varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasya tad dānam anayā(bhyanu)modanayābhyanumodate ||
body.translated_text: 6.11 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> expressed his appreciation of the gift of <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, with this expression of gratitude:

body.text:

  śrāddhaḥ puruṣapudgalaḥ ||

body.text: 7.1 atha bhagavān varṣākāraṃ brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātraṃ dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 7.1 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text: 7.2 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro yat tatrotsīdanadharmaṃ tat sarvaṃ visarjanadharmam iti kṛtvā bhagavantaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 7.2 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, reflecting that 'all that is subject to arising is subject to cessation,' followed behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, step by step.

body.text: 7.3 atha varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasyaitad abhavat ||
body.translated_text: 7.3 Then this thought occurred to <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>:

body.text: yena dvāreṇa śramaṇo gautamaḥ prathamato niṣkramiṣyati tam ahaṃ gautamadvāraṃ māpayiṣyāmi yena (t)īrthena śramaṇo gautamaḥ prathamato nadīṃ gaṅgām uttariṣyati tam ahaṃ gautama(tī)rthaṃ māpayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 'Through whichever gate the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> first departs, that I shall have named the <s>Gautama</s> Gate. And at whichever ford the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> first crosses the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, that I shall have named the <s>Gautama</s> Ford.'

body.text: 7.4 atha bhagavān varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasya cetasā cittam ājñāya paścimena dvāreṇa niṣkramyottareṇānvāvṛtto yena nadī gaṅgā ||
body.translated_text: 7.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing with his mind the thought in the mind of <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, departed through the western gate and turned northward toward the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

body.text: 7.5 tena khalu samayena māgadhakā manuṣyā nadīṃ gaṅgām uttaranty api pratyuttaranty apy ekatyāḥ śalmaliphaleṣv ekatyā alābuniḥśrayaṇikābhir ekatyās tḥlabimbopanair ekatyāś chāgalakair dṛtibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 7.5 At that time, the people of <s>Magadha</s> were crossing back and forth over the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — some on <s>śalmalī</s>-fruit rafts, some on gourd floats, some on <s>tūlabimba</s> (cotton-bale) boats, and some on goatskin bladders.

body.text: 7.6 atha bhagavata etad abhavat || kiṃ nu nadīṃ gaṅgām asajyamānaḥ srotaso gacchāmy āho svid apārime tīre 'ntarhitaḥ pārime tīre pratitiṣṭh(āmi || ath)a bhagavāṃs tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte 'pārime tīre 'ntarhitaḥ pārime tīre pratyasthāt ||
body.translated_text: 7.6 Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Shall I go across the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> without being impeded by the current, or shall I disappear on this near bank and reappear on the far bank?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) that, with his mind concentrated, he disappeared on the near bank and reappeared standing on the far bank.

body.text: 7.7 atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇama(ga)dhamahāmātro yena dvār(eṇa bhagav)ā(n) niṣkrā(n)tas tad gautamadvāraṃ māpayati yena tīrthena bhagavān nadīṃ gaṅgām uttīrṇas tad gautamatīrthaṃ māpayati ||
body.translated_text: 7.7 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, had the gate through which the <s>Bhagavān</s> had departed named the <s>Gautama</s> Gate, and the ford at which the <s>Bhagavān</s> had crossed the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> named the <s>Gautama</s> Ford.

children.text: 7.8 athānyataro bhikṣus tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ babh(āṣe) |

having made a bridge, leaving aside the shallow pools —

body.text: 8.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: Having cut here the root of craving,

body.text: 8.2 āgamy(ānanda yena ku)ṭ(i)grāmakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: for what should one search? (3)'

body.text: 8.3 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 8.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 8.4 atha bhagavān yena (ku)ṭi(grā)makas tena caryāṃ prakrāntaḥ || anupūrveṇa caryāñ (caraṅ kuṭigrāmakam a)nuprāptaḥ kuṭigrāmake viharaty uttareṇa grāmasya śiṃśapāvane ||
body.translated_text: 8.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Kuṭigrāmaka</s>.'

body.text: 8.5 tatra bhagavā(n bhikṣūn) āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 8.5 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>:

body.text: 8.6 itīmāni bhikṣavaḥ śīlāny ayaṃ s(amādhir iyaṃ prajñā ||) śīlaparibhāvitaḥ samādhiś cirasthitiko bhavati || prajñāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ samyag eva vim(u)cyate rāgadveṣamohebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 8.6 'These, <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the precepts; this is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); this is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). <s>Samādhi</s> cultivated through <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) becomes long-lasting. The mind cultivated through <s>prajñā</s> is rightly liberated from <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion).'

body.text: 8.7 evaṃ samyaksuvimuktacitta āryaśrāvakaḥ samyag (eva) praj(ānāti ||) kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi ||
body.translated_text: 8.7 'Thus, an <s>āryaśrāvaka</s> (noble disciple) whose mind is rightly and well liberated rightly knows: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done; I know of no further existence beyond this."'

body.text: 9.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 9.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 9.2 āgamayānanda yena nādi(k)ā ||
body.translated_text: 9.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Nādikā</s>.'

body.text: 9.3 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 9.3 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
9.4 atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu caryāñ caran nā(dikām anuprāpto nādikāyāṃ viharati kuñjikāvasathe ||)
9.5 (tena samayena nādikāyā mahato janakāyasya māry utthitābhūt || tathā hi karkaṭaka upāsakaḥ kālagataḥ ||)
9.6 (nikaṭa upāsakaḥ kaḍaṅgaraḥ kātyarṣabhaś cārur upacārur ariṣṭa upāriṣṭo bhadraḥ subhadro yaśo yaśodatto yaśottaro 'pi kālagataḥ ||)
9.7 (atha saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivasya pātracīvaram ādāya nādikāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣan ||)
9.8 (aśrauṣuḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavo nādikāṃ piṇḍāya carantaḥ || asyāṃ nādikāyāṃ mahāñ janakāyo mṛtaḥ || tathā hi karkaṭaka upāsakaḥ kālagato nikaṭo kaḍaṅgaraḥ kātyarṣabhaś cārur upacārur ariṣṭa upāriṣṭo bhadraḥ subhadro yaśo yaśodatto yaśottaraḥ kālagataḥ ||)
9.9 (śrutvā ca punar nādikāṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyāḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātāḥ pratikrāntāḥ || pātracīvaraṃ pratiśāmya pādau prakṣālya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagmuḥ || upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdan ||)
9.10 (ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavo bhagavantam idam avocan ||)
9.11 (iha vayaṃ bhadanta saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivasya pātracīvaram ādāya) nādikāṃ piṇḍāya prāviśāma || aśrauṣma (vayam) asyāṃ nādikāyāṃ ka(rkaṭaka upāsakaḥ kālagataḥ) pūrvava(d yāvad yaśodatto yaśottaraḥ kālagataḥ) teṣāṃ bhadanta kā gatiḥ kopapattiḥ ko 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
9.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Nādikā</s> and dwelt at <s>Nādikā</s> in the <s>Kuñjika</s> rest-house.
9.5 At that time, a great multitude of people at <s>Nādikā</s> had been struck by death. Thus the lay-follower <s>Karkaṭaka</s> had passed away.
9.6 The lay-followers <s>Nikaṭa</s>, <s>Kaḍaṅgara</s>, <s>Kātyarṣabha</s>, <s>Cāru</s>, <s>Upacāru</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Upāriṣṭa</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Subhadra</s>, <s>Yaśas</s>, <s>Yaśodatta</s>, and <s>Yaśottara</s> had also passed away.
9.7 Then a number of monks, in the morning, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, entered <s>Nādikā</s> for alms.
9.8 Those monks, while going for alms in <s>Nādikā</s>, heard: 'A great multitude of people has died in this <s>Nādikā</s>. Thus the lay-follower <s>Karkaṭaka</s> has passed away; <s>Nikaṭa</s>, <s>Kaḍaṅgara</s>, <s>Kātyarṣabha</s>, <s>Cāru</s>, <s>Upacāru</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Upāriṣṭa</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Subhadra</s>, <s>Yaśas</s>, <s>Yaśodatta</s>, and <s>Yaśottara</s> have passed away.'
9.9 Having heard this, having gone for alms in <s>Nādikā</s>, having finished their meal, after their afternoon meal, they returned. Having put away their bowls and robes and washed their feet, they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, they sat down to one side.
9.10 Seated to one side, those monks said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
9.11 'Here, Venerable Sir, we monks, in the morning, having dressed and taken our bowls and robes, entered <s>Nādikā</s> for alms. We heard that in this <s>Nādikā</s> the lay-follower <s>Karkaṭaka</s> has passed away...' as before, up to '...<s>Yaśodatta</s> and <s>Yaśottara</s> have passed away. What, Venerable Sir, is their destiny? What is their rebirth? What is their future state?'

body.text: 9.12 karkaṭaka up(āsakaḥ pañcānām avarabhāgīyā)nāṃ saṃ(yojanānāṃ prahāṇād aupapādukās tatra parinirvāyy anāgāmy anāvṛttidharmā pu)nar imaṃ lokaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 9.12 'The lay-follower <s>Karkaṭaka</s>, through the abandonment of the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), is of spontaneous arising (<s>aupapāduka</s>); he will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there; he is a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), of the nature of not returning again to this world.'

body.text:
9.13 nikaṭaḥ kaḍaṅgaraḥ pūrvavad yāvad yaśottara upāsakaḥ pañ(cānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ pūrvavad) yāvat punar imaṃ lo(kam ||)
9.14 (santi bhikṣavo nādikā)yām ardhatṛtīyāny upāsakaśatāni kālagatāni yāni pañcānām a(varabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanān)āṃ prahāṇād aupapādukās tatra parinirvāyiṇo 'nāgāmino 'nāvṛttidharmāṇaḥ punar imaṃ lokam ||
body.translated_text:
9.13 '<s>Nikaṭa</s>, <s>Kaḍaṅgara</s>...' as before, up to '...the lay-follower <s>Yaśottara</s>, through the abandonment of the five lower fetters...' as before, up to '...not returning again to this world.'
9.14 'There are, monks, two hundred and fifty lay-followers at <s>Nādikā</s> who have passed away, who through the abandonment of the five lower fetters are of spontaneous arising, will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there, are non-returners, of the nature of not returning again to this world.'

body.text: 9.15 sāti(rekāṇi bhikṣavo nādikāyāṃ tryupāsa)kaśatāni abhyatītāni kālagatāni yāni trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād rāgadveṣamohānāṃ ca tanutvā(t kālaṃ kṛtvā sakṛdāgāminaḥ sakṛd imaṃ lokam āgamya duḥkhasyāntaṃ ka)riṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: 9.15 'There are, monks, more than three hundred lay-followers at <s>Nādikā</s> who have died and passed away, who through the abandonment of three fetters and the weakening of desire, hatred, and delusion, having passed away, are once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) who, coming once more to this world, will make an end of suffering.'

body.text:
9.16 sātirekāṇy asyāṃ nādikāyāṃ pañcopāsakaśatāny abhyatītān(i) kālagatāni yāni (trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāc chrotaāpannā avinipā)tadharmāṇo niyataṃ saṃbodhiparāyaṇāḥ saptakṛtvaḥparamāḥ sap(takṛtvo de)vāṃś ca manuṣyāṃ(ś ca saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyanti ||)
9.17 (kālagatāḥ kā)lagatā iti yūyaṃ bhikṣavas tathāgataṃ prakṣyatha viheṭhayiṣyatha tathāgataṃ (na puna)r anena tathā(gat). + + + + + + + + (jātasyāvaśyaṃ kālakr)iyā ||
body.translated_text:
9.16 'There are more than five hundred lay-followers in this <s>Nādikā</s> who have died and passed away, who through the abandonment of three fetters are stream-enterers (<s>śrotaāpanna</s>), of the nature of not falling into lower states, fixed in destiny, bound for awakening (<s>saṃbodhiparāyaṇa</s>), who at most seven more times, having transmigrated through <s>deva</s> and human states seven times, will make an end of suffering.'
9.17 'You monks will keep asking the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the dead — "They have passed away, they have passed away" — and you will trouble the <s>Tathāgata</s>. But this is not... for one who has been born, death is inevitable.'

body.text:
9.18 kim atr(ā)ścaryam || utpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā sthitaiveyaṃ dharmatā dharma(sthitaye dhātūṃs tāṃs tathāgataḥ) svayam abhijñāyābhisaṃ(buddhyā)khyāti prajñ(ā)payati pra(sth)āpay(ati vibha)jati vivaraty uttānīka(roti de)śayati saṃ(prakāśayati ||)
9.19 (yadutāsmin satīdaṃ bhavaty asyotpādād idam utpadyate yadutāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvat samudayo nirodha)ś ca bhavati ||
body.translated_text:
9.18 'What is astonishing in this? Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this nature of things stands firm, this fixed principle of <s>Dharma</s>: the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having directly known and fully awakened to those elements, declares them, makes them known, establishes them, analyzes them, opens them up, makes them clear, teaches them, and illuminates them.'
9.19 'Namely: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is: conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) are formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>)...' up to '...there is both arising and cessation.'

body.text:
9.20
9.21 api (dharmādarśaṃ nāma dharma)paryāyaṃ deśayiṣye || (taṃ śṛṇ)uta s(ā)dhu ca su(ṣṭhu) ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye || dharmāda(r)ś(o dharmapa)ryāyaḥ (katamaḥ || buddhe dharme saṃghe 'vetyaprasā)dena samanvā(gato bhavaty ā)ryakāntaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati || ayam ucyate dharmādarśo dharmaparyāyaḥ || dharmādarś(o dharmaparyāya i)ti me yad ukt(aṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavas tad uktam ||)
9.22
body.translated_text:
9.20-9.21 'I shall also teach a <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Mirror of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmādarśa</s>). Listen to it, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak. What is the Mirror of the <s>Dharma</s> discourse? One is endowed with unwavering confidence (<s>avêtyaprasāda</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and is endowed with virtues dear to the Noble Ones (<s>āryakānta śīla</s>). This is called the Mirror of the <s>Dharma</s> discourse. That the Mirror of the <s>Dharma</s> discourse was taught by me — this, monks, has been said to you.'
9.22

body.text: 10.1 (tatra bhagavān ā)yuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate || āgamayānanda yena vaiśālī ||
body.translated_text: 10.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.'

body.text:
10.2 (evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||)
10.3 (atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapade)ṣu caryāṃ caran vaiśālim anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharaty āmra(pālivane ||)
10.4 (aśrauṣīd āmrapālir gaṇikā || bhagavāṅ gautamo vaiśālīm anu)prāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharaty asmākam evāmravane ||
body.translated_text:
10.2 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
10.3 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and dwelt at <s>Vaiśālī</s> in <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s grove.
10.4 <s>Āmrapālī</s> the courtesan heard: 'The Venerable <s>Gautama</s> has arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and is dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s> in our very own mango grove.'

body.text: 10.5 śrutvā ca punaḥ sarvāl(aṃkārair alaṃkṛtā strīgaṇam anvāhiṇḍayitvā bhadraṃ yānam adhiruhya vaiśālyā niryāti bhagavato 'ntikenopadarśa)nāya bhagavantaṃ paryupāsanāyai ||
body.translated_text: 10.5 Having heard this, adorned with all her ornaments, having assembled her retinue of women, mounting an excellent chariot, she set forth from <s>Vaiśālī</s> to the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
10.6 tasyā yāvad yānabhūmis tāvad yānena g(atvā yānād avatīrya padbhyām eva yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntā ||)
10.7 (adrākṣīd bhagavān anekaśatabhikṣuparivāre sanniṣaṇṇa āmrapāliṃ dūrād āgacchantīṃ) dṛṣṭv(ā) ca puna(r) bh(i)kṣūn āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text:
10.6 Having gone by chariot as far as the ground permitted for a chariot, she descended from the chariot and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> on foot.
10.7 The <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated amid an assembly of several hundred monks, saw <s>Āmrapālī</s> coming from afar, and having seen her, addressed the monks:

body.text:
10.8 ātāpino bhikṣavo viha(rata saṃprajānāḥ pratismṛtāḥ || āmrapālir gaṇikātrāgatā ||)
10.9 (kathaṃ ca bhikṣur ātā)pī bhavati ||
body.translated_text:
10.8 'Dwell ardent, monks, fully aware, mindful. <s>Āmrapālī</s> the courtesan has come here.'
10.9 'And how is a monk ardent?'

body.text:
10.10 iha bhikṣur utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇ(āṃ prahāṇāya cchandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhāti ||)
(a)nutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpād(āya cchandaṃ janayati pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: 10.10 'Here a monk, for the abandonment of arisen evil, unwholesome states, generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, takes hold of the mind and applies it. For the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states, he generates desire...' as before.

body.text: anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya cchandaṃ jana)yati pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: 'For the arising of unarisen wholesome states, he generates desire...' as before.

body.text: utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye (bhūyobhāvatāyā asaṃpramoṣāya paripūraṇāya vaipulyāya cchandaṃ janayati pūrvavat || ayaṃ) bh(i)kṣur ātāpī bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'For the maintenance, non-loss, increase, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire...' as before. 'This is how a monk is ardent.'

body.text: 10.11 kathañ ca bhikṣuḥ saṃprajāno bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 10.11 'And how is a monk fully aware (<s>saṃprajāna</s>)?'

body.text: 10.12 iha bhi(kṣur abhikrānte pratikrānte saṃprajāno bhavaty ālokite vilokite saṃmiñjite prasāri)t(e) saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe gate sthite niṣaṇṇe śayite jāgarite (bhāṣite tūṣṇīṃbhāve supte śrame viśrame saṃprajāno bhavati || ayaṃ bhikṣur saṃprajā)no bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 10.12 'Here a monk acts with full awareness when going forward and returning, when looking ahead and looking aside, when bending and extending, when wearing robes and carrying bowl, when walking, standing, sitting, lying down, when awake, when speaking, when silent, when sleeping, when weary, when resting — he acts with full awareness. This is how a monk is fully aware.'

body.text: 10.13 kathañ ca bhikṣuḥ pratismṛto bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 10.13 'And how is a monk mindful (<s>pratismṛta</s>)?'

body.text: 10.14 iha bhikṣur adhyātmaṃ kā(ye kāyānupaśyī viharaty ātāpī saṃprajānaḥ smṛtimān vinīyābhidhyā loke daurmanasyam || bahirdhā kā)ye 'dhyātmabahirdhā kāye 'dhyātmaṃ vedanāsu bahirdhā vedanāsv (adhyātmabahirdhā vedanāsv adhyātmaṃ citte bahirdhā citte 'dhyātmabahirdhā citte 'dhyātmaṃ dharme)ṣu bahirdhā dharmeṣv adhyātmabahirdhā dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyī vi(haraty ātāpī saṃprajānaḥ smṛtimān vinīyābhidhyā loke daurmanasyam || ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ prati)smṛto bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 10.14 'Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body internally, ardent, fully aware, mindful, having removed covetousness and distress regarding the world. Externally in the body; internally-externally in the body; internally in feelings; externally in feelings; internally-externally in feelings; internally in mind; externally in mind; internally-externally in mind; internally in <s>dharmas</s>; externally in <s>dharmas</s>; he dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s> internally-externally, ardent, fully aware, mindful, having removed covetousness and distress regarding the world. This is how a monk is mindful.'

body.text: 10.15 ātāpino bhikṣavo viharata saṃprajānāḥ pra(tismṛtāḥ || āmrapālir gaṇikātrāgatety eva mayākhyāta)m ||
body.translated_text: 10.15 'Dwell ardent, monks, fully aware, mindful. <s>Āmrapālī</s> the courtesan has come here — thus it has been declared by me.'

body.text:
10.16 ath(ā)mrap(ā)lir yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma || upetya bhagavatpādau śi(rasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat ||)
10.17 (ekāntaniṣaṇṇām āmrapāliṃ bhagavān dhārmyā kathayā) pūrvavad yāvat saṃpraharṣayitvā tūṣṇīm abhūt ||
body.translated_text:
10.16 Then <s>Āmrapālī</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed her head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, she sat down to one side.
10.17 The <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened <s>Āmrapālī</s>, seated to one side, with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>... as before, up to ...and fell silent.

body.text:
10.18 atha āmrapāli(r utthāyāsanād yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
10.19 (adhivāsa)yatu me bhagavā(ñ) śvo bhaktena sārdh(aṃ) bhikṣu(saṃghena ||)
10.20 (adhivāsayati bhagavāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena || atha āmrapālir bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā) bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato ('ntikāt prakrāntā ||)
body.translated_text:
10.18 Then <s>Āmrapālī</s>, rising from her seat, extending her palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
10.19 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept my offering of food tomorrow, together with the community of monks.'
10.20 The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted ...

body.text: 11.1 (aśrauṣur vaiśālakā licchavayaḥ || bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprā)p(t)o vai(śā)lyāṃ viharaty āmrapālivane ||
body.translated_text: 11.1 The <s>Licchavīs</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> heard: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. He is dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the <s>Āmrapālī</s> grove.'

children.translated_text: 11.2 Having heard, each one mounting their splendid carriages ... [lacuna] ... adorned ...

children.translated_text: 11.5 Some had red horses, red chariots, red reins and goads, red turbans, red parasols, sword-sheaths, and fly-whisks with red jeweled handles, red garments, ornaments, and ointments, and red retinues.

children.text: 11.6 (ekatyāḥ śvetāśvāḥ ś)v(eta)r(a)thāḥ śvetapragrahapratodāḥ śv(e)toṣṇīṣ(āḥ śvetacchatrakhaḍgakośāḥ śvetamaṇidaṇḍakacāmarāḥ śvetavastrālaṃkāravilepanāḥ śvetaparivārā)
children.translated_text: 11.6 Some had white horses, white chariots, white reins and goads, white turbans, white parasols, sword-sheaths, and fly-whisks with white jeweled handles, white garments, ornaments, and ointments, and white retinues.

children.text: 11.7 (uccaśabdaṃ prakṣveḍayanto mahāśabdaṃ prakṣveḍayanto vaiśālyā niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagmur bhaga)vaddarśanāy(a bha)gavantaṃ paryupāsanāyai ||
children.translated_text: 11.7 With loud shouts and great cries, departing from <s>Vaiśālī</s>, they approached to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was, to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
11.8 (adrākṣīd bhagavān vaiśalakāl licchavīn dūrād evāgacchato dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||)
11.9 ............... vaiśālakā(l li)cchavīn paśyatha || anayard(dhyā) ........

11.12 (tena kha)lu samayena paiṅgiko māṇavas t(asmin samāje) sanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt sannipatitaḥ || a(tha paiṅgiko māṇava utthāyāsanād ekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat ||)

11.16 + + + + + + + + dhāriṇo
