body.text:
12.1 (athāmrapālis tām eva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyam evotthāya āsanakāni prajña)pyodakamaṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya bha(gavato dūtena kālam ārocayati ||)
12.2 (samayo bho gautamo sadyo bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhavāṅ gautamaḥ kālaṃ manyate ||)
12.3 (atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivasya pā)tracīvaram ādāya bhikṣusaṃghapa(rivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yenāmrapālyā gaṇikāyā bhaktābhisāras tenopajagāma || upetya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nya)ṣīdat ||
body.translated_text:
12.1 Then <s>Āmrapālī</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, and having risen at dawn, arranged the seats, set out the water vessel, and sent a messenger to inform the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the time:
12.2 'It is time, Venerable <s>Gautama</s> ...'

body.text:
12.4 athāmrapāliḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śu(cin)ā praṇīte(na khādanī)yabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayati saṃpravārayati || śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā
12.5 bhagavantaṃ bhuktav(an)t(aṃ) viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarakam āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya ||
body.translated_text: 12.4 Then <s>Āmrapālī</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with her own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft. With pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, with her own hands ...

children.text: 12.6 atha bhagavān āmrapālyās tad dānam anayābhyanumodanayābhyanumodate |
children.translated_text: 12.6 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> expressed his approval of <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s gift with this verse of appreciation:

children.text: 12.7 dadat priyo bhavati bhajanti taṃ janāḥ
children.translated_text: 12.7 The giver becomes beloved; people seek his company;
he attains fame and his renown increases.

body.text: ama(d)gu(bhū)taḥ pariṣadaṃ vigāhate

children.translated_text: a man who is free from miserliness becomes confident. (1)

children.text:
12.8 tasmād dhi dānāni dadati paṇḍitā
  vinīya mātsaryamalaṃ sukhaiṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
12.8 Therefore the wise, who seek happiness,
give gifts, having removed the stain of miserliness;

body.translated_text: Without timidity he enters any assembly;

body.text: te dīrgharātraṃ tridaśe pratiṣṭhitā

children.translated_text: and having attained the nature of gods, they delight there. (2)

children.text:
12.9 kṛtāyuṣāḥ kṛtakuśalā itaś cyutāḥ
  svayaṃprabhā anuvicaranti nandane ||
children.translated_text:
12.9 Having lived out their lifespan, having accumulated merit, departing from there,
self-luminous, they wander in <s>Nandana</s> (the garden of delight);

body.translated_text: they are established for a long time among the <s>Tridaśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods,

body.text:
(te) tatra krīḍanti ramanti cobhayaṃ
  samarpitāḥ kāmaguṇais tu pañcabhiḥ ||
body.translated_text:
there they play and rejoice in both ways,
endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure.

body.text: śrutveha vākyam asitasya tāyinaḥ

children.translated_text: the disciples of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) delight in heaven. (3)

children.text: 12.10 atha bhagavān āmrapāli(ṃ) dhārmy(ā) kathayā sandarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 12.10 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened <s>Āmrapālī</s> with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.translated_text: Having heard in this world the words of the dark-hued Protector,

body.text: 13.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āma(n)trayat(e) ||
body.translated_text: 13.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 13.2 āgamayānanda yena veṇugrāmakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 13.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Veṇugrāmaka</s>.'

body.text: 13.3 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavata(ḥ prat)y(a)śrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 13.3 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 13.4 atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran veṇugrāmakam anuprāpto veṇugrāmake viharaty uttareṇa grāmasya śiṃśapāvane ||
body.translated_text: 13.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Veṇugrāmaka</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> dwelt at <s>Veṇugrāmaka</s>, to the north of the village, in a <s>śiṃśapā</s> (Dalbergia sissoo) grove.

body.text: 13.5 tena khalu samayena durbhikṣam abhūt kṛcchraḥ kāntāro durlabhaḥ piṇḍako yācanakena ||
body.translated_text: 13.5 At that time there was a famine — a time of hardship, a wilderness, when alms-food was hard to obtain by begging.

body.text: 13.6 tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 13.6 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:

body.text: 13.7 etarhi bhikṣavo durbhikṣaṃ kṛcchraḥ kāntāro durlabho piṇḍako yācanakena ||
body.translated_text: 13.7 'At present, O monks, there is a famine — a time of hardship, a wilderness, when alms-food is hard to obtain by begging.

body.text: 13.8 eta yūyaṃ bhikṣavo yathāsaṃstutikayā yathāsaṃlaptikayā yathāsaṃpremikayā vaiśālīsama(n)takena vṛjigrāmakeṣu varṣām upagacchata ||
body.translated_text: 13.8 Go, monks, according to your acquaintances, according to your companions, according to your friends, to the <s>Vṛji</s> villages surrounding <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and enter the rains retreat there.

body.text: 13.9 aham apy asminn eva veṇugrāmake varṣām upagamiṣyāmy ānandena bhikṣuṇopasthāyakena || mā sarva eva piṇḍakena k(lāma)tha ||
body.translated_text: 13.9 I too shall enter the rains retreat here in this very <s>Veṇugrāmaka</s>, with the monk <s>Ānanda</s> as my attendant. Let not all of you suffer hardship for alms-food.'

body.text:
13.10 evaṃ bh(adanteti) te bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya
13.11 yathāsaṃstutikayā yathāsaṃlapt(i)ka(y)ā y(athāsaṃpremikayā vaiśālīsamantakena vṛjigrāmakeṣu varṣām upagatāḥ ||)
body.translated_text:
13.10 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' those monks, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
13.11 according to their acquaintances, according to their companions, according to their friends, entered the rains retreat in the <s>Vṛji</s> villages surrounding <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: 14.1 (bhagavān tatraiva veṇugrāmake varṣām upagata ānandena bhikṣuṇopasthāya)k(e)na ||
body.translated_text: 14.1 The <s>Bhagavān</s> entered the rains retreat right there in <s>Veṇugrāmaka</s>, with the monk <s>Ānanda</s> as his attendant.

body.text:
14.2 t(asya) kh(al)u (varṣopagatasyotpannaḥ khara ābādhaḥ pragāḍhā vedanā māraṇāntikā ||)
14.3 (atha bhagavata etad abhavat ||)
14.4 (utpanno me khara ābādhaḥ pragāḍhā ve)danā māraṇāntikā viprakrānta(ś ca bhikṣusaṃghaḥ ||)
14.5 (na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ viprakrānte bhikṣusaṃghe parinirvāyām || yan nv ahaṃ tata ekatyā vedanā vī)ryeṇa pr(a)tiprasrabhya sarvanimi(ttānām amanasikārād ānimittaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ kāyena sākṣīkṛtvopasaṃpadya vihareyam ||)
14.6 (atha bhagavān tata e)katyā vedanā vīryeṇa pratiprasra(bhya) sarvanimittā(nām amanasikārād animittaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ kāyena sākṣīkṛtvopasaṃpadya vyahārṣīt || tena tathāgatasya kṣemaṇī)yatarañ cābhūd yāpanīyatara(ñ ca ||)
14.7 (athāyuṣmān ā)nandaḥ s(ā)yāhn(e) pratis(aṃlayanād vyutthāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma || upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā va)nditvaikānte 'sthāt ||
body.translated_text: 14.2 While he was spending the rains retreat, a severe illness arose [for him] — sharp, acute sensations, close to death. 14.3 Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 14.4 'A severe illness has arisen in me — sharp, acute sensations, close to death, and the community of monks (<s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>) has dispersed.' 14.5 'It would not be fitting for me to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> while the community of monks is dispersed. What if I were to suppress this illness by the force of energy, and through non-attention to all signs (<s>sarvanimittānām amanasikārāt</s>), having realized with my own body the signless concentration of mind (<s>animittaṃ cetaḥsamādhim</s>), were to attain it and abide in it?' 14.6 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, suppressing that illness by the force of energy, through non-attention to all signs, having realized with his own body the signless concentration of mind, attained it and remained content. Thereby the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s condition became more comfortable and more bearable. 14.7 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, in the afternoon, having emerged from his seclusion, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side.

body.text: 14.8 ekāntasthit(a āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam a)vocat ||
body.translated_text: 14.8 Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
14.9 api me bhada(n)ta m. .............. lapante bhagavata imam evaṃ .r .......... (ā)śvāsamātram || na tāvad bhagav(ān parinirvā)syati yāvad bhagavān bhikṣusaṃ(gh). .............
14.10 (ya)syānandaivaṃ syāt || (mamāsti bhikṣu)saṃgha(ḥ || ahaṃ) bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pari(hariṣyāmīti) ......
14.11 (mama khalv ā)nanda naivaṃ bhava(ti || mamāsti bhikṣu)s(a)ṃghaḥ || a(ha)ṃ (bhikṣusaṃghaṃ parihariṣyāmīti) ................
14.12 ..............
14.13 (tadyathā catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni sapta bodhyaṅgāny āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ ||)
14.14 (na tatrānanda tathāgatasya dharmeṣv ācāryamu)ṣṭi(r) yaṃ tathāgataḥ praticchādayitavyaṃ manyeta || kaccin me pare na vi(dyur iti ||)
14.15 (utpannaḥ kadāpi tathāgatasya khara ābādhaḥ pragāḍhā vedanā māraṇā)ntik(ā ||)
14.16 tasya ma etad abhavat || utpanno me khara ābādhaḥ pragāḍhā veda(nā māraṇāntikā viprakrāntaś ca bhikṣusaṃghaḥ ||)
14.17 (na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ vi)prakrānte bhikṣusaṃghe parinirvāyām || yan nv ahaṃ tata ekatyā vedanā vīryeṇa pratipra(s)r(abhya sarvanimittānām amanasikārād animittaṃ cetaḥsamā)dhiṃ kāyena sākṣīkṛtvopasaṃpadya vihareyam ||
body.translated_text: 14.9 'Venerable Sir, my ... [lacuna] ... the <s>Bhagavān</s> ... [lacuna] ... at least some comfort. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> as long as the <s>Bhagavān</s> [has not addressed] the community of monks ... [lacuna].' 14.10 '<s>Ānanda</s>, if anyone should think thus: "The community of monks is mine; I shall govern the community of monks" — ... [lacuna].' 14.11 'But, <s>Ānanda</s>, I do not think thus: "The community of monks is mine; I shall govern the community of monks" — ... [lacuna].' 14.12 ... [lacuna] ... 14.13 [These are:] the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni</s>), the four right exertions (<s>catvāri samyakprahāṇāni</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ</s>), the five faculties (<s>pañcendriyāṇi</s>), the five powers (<s>pañca balāni</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>sapta bodhyaṅgāni</s>), and the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ</s>). 14.14 'Therein, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not have a teacher's closed fist regarding the <s>dharmas</s> — that the <s>Tathāgata</s> would think there is something to be concealed: "Let others not know this of mine."' 14.15 'There arose at some time for the <s>Tathāgata</s> a severe illness — sharp, acute sensations, close to death.' 14.16 This thought occurred to me: 'A severe illness has arisen in me — sharp, acute sensations, close to death, and the community of monks has dispersed.' 14.17 'It would not be fitting for me to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> while the community of monks is dispersed. What if I were to suppress this illness by the force of energy, and through non-attention to all signs, having realized with my own body the signless concentration of mind, were to attain it and abide in it?'

body.text:
14.18 so 'haṃ tata (ekatyā ve)danā vīryeṇa pratiprasr(abhya sarvanimittānām amanasikārād animittaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ kāyena) sākṣīkṛtvopasaṃpadya vyahārṣam || tena tathāgatasya (kṣemaṇīyatarañ cā)bhūd yāpanīyatarañ (ca ||)
14.19 (punar aparam ānanda tathāgato vṛddho jīrṇatāṃ prāpto 'śī)tike vayasi vartate dvaidhāniśrayeṇa yāpy(ate || tadyathā jīrṇaṃ śakaṭaṃ dvaidhāniśraye)ṇa y(ā)pyata evam eva (tathāgato vṛddho jīrnatāṃ prāpto) 'śītike vayasi vartate dvaidhāniśrayeṇa yā(pyate ||)
14.20 (mā tasmāt tvam ānanda śoca mā klāma || kasmā)d eva tat || kuta etal labhy(aṃ yat taj jātaṃ bhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vedayi)taṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ kṣayadharmaṃ vyayadharmaṃ vi(rodhadharmaṃ pralokadharmaṃ na prarujya)te || nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: 14.18 'And so I, suppressing that illness by the force of energy, through non-attention to all signs, having realized with my own body the signless concentration of mind, attained it and remained content. Thereby the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s condition became more comfortable and more bearable.' 14.19 'Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is old, aged, advanced in years; he is in his eightieth year and is sustained by a double support. Just as an old cart is kept going by a double support, even so the <s>Tathāgata</s>, old, aged, advanced in years, in his eightieth year, is sustained by a double support.' 14.20 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, do not grieve, do not be weary! For how could it be otherwise? It is impossible that what is born, come into being, made, conditioned, experienced, dependently arisen, and subject to decay, to destruction, to dissolution, to disintegration — that it should not break apart. This situation does not exist.'

body.text:
14.21 prāg (eva bhi)kṣavo mayākhyātaṃ sarvair iṣṭaiḥ kāntaiḥ priyair manāpai(r nānābhāvo bhaviṣyati vinābhāvo viprayogo visaṃyogaḥ ||)
14.22 (tasmād) ānandaitarhi mam(a vā)tyayād ātmadvīpair vihartavyam ātmaśaraṇair dharmadvīpair dha(rmaśaraṇair ananyadvīpair ananyaśaraṇaiḥ || tat kasmād dhetoḥ ||)
14.23 (ye kecid ānandaitarhi mama vāt)yayād ātmadvīpā ātmaśaraṇā dharmadvīpā dharmaśaraṇā ananyadvīpā a(nanyaśaraṇās te 'graṃ bhaviṣyanti yaduta mama śr)āvak(āṇāṃ śikṣākāmānāṃ ||)
14.24 (kathaṃ cānanda bhi)kṣ(u)r ātmadvīpo bhavaty ātmaśaraṇo dharmadvīpo dharmaśaraṇo 'nanyadvīpo 'nanyaśaraṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 14.21 'Previously, O monks, it has been declared by me: from all that is dear, pleasant, agreeable, and appealing there will be separation, parting, and dissociation.' 14.22 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, now or after my passing, you should dwell as islands unto yourselves (<s>ātmadvīpa</s>), as refuges unto yourselves (<s>ātmaśaraṇa</s>), as islands of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadvīpa</s>), as refuges of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaśaraṇa</s>), with no other island, with no other refuge. For what reason?' 14.23 'Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, now or after my passing, dwells as an island unto themselves, as a refuge unto themselves, as an island of the <s>Dharma</s>, as a refuge of the <s>Dharma</s>, with no other island, with no other refuge — they will be the foremost, that is, among my disciples who desire the training.' 14.24 'And how, <s>Ānanda</s>, does a monk dwell as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, as an island of the <s>Dharma</s>, as a refuge of the <s>Dharma</s>, with no other island, with no other refuge?'

body.text: 14.25 iha bhikṣur (a)dhy(ā)tm(aṃ) kāy(e) kāyānupaśyī viha(raty) ātāpī saṃprajānaḥ smṛtimā(n) vinīyābhidhyā loke daurmanasyam || bahirdhā kāye 'dhyātmabahirdhā kāye 'dhyātmaṃ vedanāsu bahirdhā vedanāsv adhyātmabahirdhā vedanāsv adhyātmaṃ citte bahirdhā citte 'dhyātmabahirdhā citte 'dhyātmaṃ dharmeṣu bahirdhā dharmeṣv adhyātmabahirdhā dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyī viharaty ātāpī saṃprajānaḥ smṛtimān vinīyābhidhyā loke daurmanasyam ||
body.translated_text: 14.25 'Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body (<s>kāye kāyānupaśyī</s>) internally, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. [He dwells contemplating] the body externally, the body both internally and externally; internally in feelings (<s>vedanāsu</s>), externally in feelings, both internally and externally in feelings; internally in mind (<s>citte</s>), externally in mind, both internally and externally in mind; internally in <s>dharmas</s>, externally in <s>dharmas</s>, both internally and externally in <s>dharmas</s> — he dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyī</s>), ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world.'

body.text: 14.26 evaṃ hi bhikṣur ātmadvīpo bhavaty ātmaśaraṇo dharmadvīpo dharmaśaraṇo 'nanyadvīpo 'nanyaśaraṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 14.26 'Thus indeed does a monk dwell as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, as an island of the <s>Dharma</s>, as a refuge of the <s>Dharma</s>, with no other island, with no other refuge.'

body.text: <Hier im Tib. Uddāna>
body.translated_text: [Here in the Tibetan: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse)]

body.text: 15.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 15.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 15.2 āgamayānanda yena vaiśālī ||
body.translated_text: 15.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.'

body.text: 15.3 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 15.3 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 15.4 atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahrad(atīre kū)ṭāgāraśālāyām ||
body.translated_text: 15.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s>. At <s>Vaiśālī</s> he dwelt at the Monkey Pond (<s>Markaṭahrada</s>), in the Peaked-Roof Hall (<s>Kūṭāgāraśālā</s>).

body.text: 15.5 atha bhagavān p(ū)rvāhṇe nivasya pātracīvaram ādāya vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśad āyuṣmatānandena paścācchramaṇena ||
body.translated_text: 15.5 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robes, entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms, with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> walking behind as attendant.

body.text: 15.6 a(tha bhagavān) vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātaḥpratikrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 15.6 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having walked through <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms, having completed his meal, after his alms-round, returned.

body.text: 15.7 (pātracīvaraṃ pratiśamayya) yena cāpālaṃ caityaṃ tenopajagāma || upetyānyataraṃ vṛkṣamū(laṃ niśritya niṣa)ṇṇo di(vā)vihārāya ||
body.translated_text: 15.7 Having put away his bowl and robes, he approached the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine. Having approached, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his daytime meditation.

body.text: 15.8 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 15.8 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 15.9 ramaṇīyānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiś cāpālaṃ caityaṃ saptāmrakaṃ bahupattrakaṃ g(autamanya)grodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhurānikṣepaṇaṃ mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam || citro jaṃbudvīpo madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 15.9 'Delightful, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>! Delightful is the <s>Vṛji</s> land! Delightful is the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, the <s>Saptāmraka</s> (Seven Mangoes), the <s>Bahupattraka</s> (Many Leaves), the <s>Gautama Nyagrodha</s> (Banyan of <s>Gautama</s>), the <s>Śālavana</s> (Sāl Forest), the Yoke-Dropping Place, the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>! Colorful is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! Sweet is the life of human beings!'

body.text: 15.10 yasya kasyacic catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā || tathāgatasyānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ || ākāṃkṣamāṇas tathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: 15.10 'Whoever has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power (<s>catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ</s>) — if he so wishes, he could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power. If he so wishes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.'

body.text: 15.11 evam ukta āyuṣmān ānandas tūṣṇīm abhūt || dvir api trir api bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 15.11 When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> remained silent. A second time and a third time the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
15.12 ramaṇīyānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiś cāpālaṃ cai(t)yaṃ saptāmrakaṃ bahupattrakaṃ gautamanyagrodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhurānikṣepaṇaṃ mallā(nāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam || citro jaṃbudvīpo madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām ||)
15.13 (yasya kasyacic catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā || tathāgatasyānanda ca)tvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ || ākāṃkṣamāṇas tathāgataḥ kal(paṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā ||)
15.14 (dvir api trir apy āyuṣmān ānandas tūṣṇīm ||)
15.15 (atha bhagavata etad a)bhavat || sph(u)ṭo batāyam ānando bhikṣur māreṇa pāpīyasā yatredānīṃ yāvat trir apy au(dārike avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkriyamāṇe na śaknoti tannimittam ājñātuṃ yathāpi tataḥ sphu)ṭo m(ā)reṇa pāpīyasā ||
body.translated_text: 15.12 'Delightful, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>! Delightful is the <s>Vṛji</s> land! Delightful is the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, the <s>Saptāmraka</s>, the <s>Bahupattraka</s>, the <s>Gautama Nyagrodha</s>, the <s>Śālavana</s>, the Yoke-Dropping Place, the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>! Colorful is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! Sweet is the life of human beings!' 15.13 'Whoever has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power — if he so wishes, he could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power. If he so wishes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.' 15.14 A second time and a third time, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> remained silent. 15.15 Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Surely this monk <s>Ānanda</s> has been possessed by <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, in that now, even though this conspicuous, broad sign and indication has been made manifest three times, he is unable to understand its meaning — thus he is possessed by <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One.'

body.text: 15.16 iti viditvāyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 15.16 Having understood this, he addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 15.17 gacchā(nandānyataravṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya vihara mā ubhāv apy ākīrṇa)vihāriṇau bhaviṣyāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 15.17 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and sit at the foot of some other tree for your day's abiding. Let us not both be dwelling in crowded quarters.'

body.text: 15.18 evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśru(tyānyatamavṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya ||)
body.translated_text: 15.18 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down at the foot of another tree for his day's abiding.

body.text:
16.1 (sa māraḥ pāpīyān yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||) upetya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt || ekāntasthito māra(ḥ pāpīyān bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
16.2 (parinirvāhi bhagavan parinirvāṇasamayaḥ sugatasya ||)
16.3
16.4 (kasmāt tvaṃ pāpīya)nn evaṃ vadasi || parinirvāhi bhagavan parinirvāṇasamayaḥ sugatasya ||
body.translated_text:
16.1 Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
16.2 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> now pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> ...'

body.text: 16.5 (eko 'yaṃ bhadanta samayaḥ || bhagavān uruvilvāyāṃ viharati nadyā nairañjanāyās tīre bodhimūle 'cirābhisaṃbuddhaḥ ||) so 'haṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 16.5 'There was one occasion, Venerable Sir: the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Uruvilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, shortly after his full awakening. I approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text:
16.6 upetya bhagavantam evaṃ vad(āmi || parinirvāhi bhagavan parinirvāṇasamayaḥ sugatasya ||)
16.7 (bhagavān evam āha ||)
16.8 (na tāvat pāpīyan parinirvā)sy(ā)mi yāvan na me śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā bhaviṣyanti vyaktā medhāvinaḥ || alam u(tpannotpannānāṃ parapravādināṃ saha dharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ || alaṃ svasya vādasya pa)ryavadātāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikā vaistārikaṃ ca me bra(hmacaryaṃ cariṣyanti bahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtaṃ yāvad devamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃpra)kāśitam ||
body.translated_text:
16.6 'Having approached, I said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! It is time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."
16.7 The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:
16.8 "I will not pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, Evil One, so long as my disciples ...'

body.text:
16.9 etarhi bhadanta bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā vyaktā medhāvinaḥ || a(lam utpannotpannānāṃ parapravādināṃ saha dharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ svasya vādasya pa)ryavadātāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikā vaistārikaṃ ca te brahma(caryaṃ bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtaṃ yāvad devamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksaṃprakāśitam ||)
16.10 (tasmād aham e)vaṃ vadāmi parinirvāhi bhagavan parinirvāṇasamayaḥ sugatasya ||
body.translated_text: 16.9 'Now, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples are learned, skilled, wise. They are capable of refuting rival teachers who arise, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, and of establishing their own doctrine — monks and nuns ...'

body.text: 16.11 alpotsukas tvaṃ pāpīyan bhava na cirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasya trayāṇāṃ māsānām atyayād anupadhiśeṣe ni(r)v(ā)ṇadhātau parin(i)rvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 16.11 'Be of little concern, Evil One. Before long — after three months have passed — the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of clinging (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).'

body.text: 16.12 atha mārasya pāpīyasa etad abhavat || parinirvāsy(ate) śramaṇo gautama iti viditvā hṛṣṭas tuṣṭa udagraḥ prītisaumanasyajātas tatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 16.12 Then this thought occurred to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!' Knowing this, delighted, pleased, elated, filled with joy and happiness, he vanished right there on the spot.

body.text: 16.13 atha bhagavata etad abhavat || yan nv ah(aṃ) tadrūpān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān abhisa(ṃ)skuryāṃ (ya)thā samāhite citte jīvitasaṃskārān adhiṣṭhāyāyuḥsaṃskārān utsṛjeyam ||
body.translated_text: 16.13 Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What if I were to perform such feats of supernormal power (<s>ṛddhi-abhisaṃskāra</s>) that, with mind concentrated, having sustained the life-forces (<s>jīvitasaṃskāra</s>), I might relinquish the life-span forces (<s>āyuḥsaṃskāra</s>)?'

body.text: 16.14 atha bhagavāṃs tadrūpān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān abhisaṃskaroti yathā samāhite citte jīvita(saṃskārān adhi)ṣṭhāyāyuḥsaṃskārān utsṛjati || samananta(r)ots(ṛ)ṣṭāyuḥsaṃskāreṣv atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālaś cābhūd ulkāpā(tā) d(i)śodāhā (antarīkṣe devadun)dubhayo 'bhinadanti ||
body.translated_text: 16.14 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed such feats of supernormal power that, with mind concentrated, having sustained the life-forces, he relinquished the life-span forces. Immediately upon the relinquishing of the life-span forces, an exceedingly great ...

body.text: 16.15 atha bhagavāṃs tasmāt samādher vyutthā(ya ta)syā(ṃ) velāyāṃ (gā)thā(ṃ) babhāṣe ||
body.translated_text: 16.15 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), at that moment spoke this verse:

body.text:
tulyam atulyaṃ ca saṃbhavaṃ
  (bhavasaṃskāram apotsṛjan muniḥ ||
body.translated_text:
The equal and the unequal, and existence —
relinquishing the formations of becoming, the sage,

body.text:
adhyātmarataḥ samāhi)to
  h(y abhinat ko)śam ivāṇḍa(saṃbhavaḥ |)
body.translated_text:
delighting inwardly, concentrated,
broke through the shell like one born from an egg.

body.text: 17.1 (athāy)uṣmān ānando yena bh(agavāṃs tenopaja)gām(a ||) upetya bhagava(taḥ pādau) śirasā (vanditvaikānte 'sthāt || ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bha)ga(vantam ida)m avocat ||
body.translated_text: 17.1 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
17.2 ko bh(adanta hetuḥ kaḥ pra)tyayo yenaitarhy a(bhūn mahāpṛthivī)cāla ulkāpātā di(śodāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||)
17.3 (aṣṭāv ime) h(e)tavo 'ṣṭau pratyayā (ma)hataḥ pṛthiv(īc)ālasya || katame 'ṣṭau ||
body.translated_text:
17.2 'What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition, that just now there was a great earthquake, a fall of meteors, a burning of the directions, and divine drums resounding in the sky?'
17.3 'There are these eight causes, eight conditions for a great earthquake ...'

body.text: 17.4 (i)yaṃ mahāpṛ(thivy) apsu pratiṣṭhitā || āpo vā(yau) pratiṣṭhitā v(āy)u(r ākāśe pratiṣṭhitaḥ || bhavaty) ān(anda sama)yo yad ākāśe viṣamā vāyavo vānty āpaḥ (k)ṣ(o)bhayanti || āpaḥ kṣubdhāḥ pṛthivī(ṃ) cālayanti ||
body.translated_text: 17.4 'This great earth, <s>Ānanda</s>, is established upon water; water is established upon wind; wind is established upon space. There comes a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, when violent winds blow through space, agitating the waters; ...'

body.text: 17.5 ayaṃ prathamo hetuḥ prathamaḥ praty(ayo) mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
body.translated_text: 17.5 'This is the first cause, the first condition for a great earthquake.'

body.text: 17.6 punar aparaṃ bhikṣur maharddhiko bhavati mahānubhāvaḥ sa parīttāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñām adhitiṣṭhaty apramāṇāṃ cāpsaṃjñāṃ sa āk(āṃ)kṣamāṇaḥ pṛthivīṃ cālayati ||
body.translated_text: 17.6 'Furthermore, a monk of great supernormal power, of great authority, who establishes a limited earth-perception and an unlimited water-perception — he, when he wishes, causes the earth to shake.'

body.text: 17.7 bhikṣuṇī devatā vā maharddhikā bhavati mahānubhāvā sā parīttāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñām adhitiṣṭhaty apramāṇāṃ cāpsaṃjñām ākāṃkṣamāṇā pṛthivīṃ cālayati ||
body.translated_text: 17.7 'A nun, or a deity of great supernormal power, of great authority, who establishes a limited earth-perception and an unlimited water-perception — she, when she wishes, causes the earth to shake.'

body.text: 17.8 ayaṃ dvitīyo hetur dvitīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
body.translated_text: 17.8 'This is the second cause, the second condition for a great earthquake.'

body.text:
17.9 punar aparaṃ yasmin samaye bodhisatvas tuṣitād devanikāyāc cyutvā mātuḥ kukṣāv avakrāmaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālaś ca bhavati s(arvaś cāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavanti ||)
17.10 api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhatamā andhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandr(amasāv) evaṃmaharddhi(k)āv (evaṃmahānubhāvāv ābhayābhāṃ na pratyanubhavatas tā a)pi tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 17.9 'Furthermore, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, falling from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, descends into his mother's womb — at that time there is an exceedingly great earthquake, and all this world is illuminated with a surpassing radiance ...'

body.text: 17.11 tatra ye (satvā upa)pannās te tay(ā)bha(y)ān(yonyaṃ satvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānante || anye 'pi bhavantaḥ satvā ihopa)pannāḥ || anye 'pi bhavantaḥ satvā ihopapannāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 17.11 'There, those beings who have been reborn, seeing one another by that radiance, recognize: "Other beings, too, have been reborn here! Other beings, too, have been reborn here!"'

body.text:
17.12 ayaṃ tṛtīyo he(tus tṛtīyaḥ pratya)yo ma(hataḥ p)ṛ(thivīcālasya ||)
17.13 (punar aparaṃ yasmin samaye bodhisatvo mātuḥ ku)kṣer niṣkrāmaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālaś ca bhavati pūrvavad yāvad anye ('pi bha)vantaḥ satvā (ihopapannāḥ ||)
17.14 (ayaṃ caturtho hetuś caturthaḥ pratyayo ma)hataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
body.translated_text:
17.12 'This is the third cause, the third condition for a great earthquake.'
17.13 'Furthermore, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> issues forth from his mother's womb — at that time there is an exceedingly great earthquake ...'

body.text: 17.15 punar aparaṃ yasmin samaye bodhisatvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbo(dhim adhigacchaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivī)cālaś ca bhavati pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: 17.15 'Furthermore, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) — at that time there is an exceedingly great earthquake,' as before.

body.text:
17.16 ayaṃ pañcamo hetuḥ pañcamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthiv(īcālasya ||)
17.17 (punar aparam ānanda yasmin samaye tathāgatas tripariva)rtaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālaś ca bhava(ti pūrvavat ||)
17.18 (ayaṃ ṣaṣṭho hetuḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivī)cālasya ||
body.translated_text:
17.16 'This is the fifth cause, the fifth condition for a great earthquake.'
17.17 'Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s> sets in motion the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel (<s>dharmacakra</s>) — the righteous <s>Dharma</s>-wheel with three turnings and twelve aspects ...'

body.text: 17.19 punar aparaṃ yasmin samaye tathāgato jīvitasaṃskārān adhiṣṭhāyāyuḥsaṃskā(rān utsṛjaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bha)vaty ulk(āpātā diśodāhā antarīkṣe) devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||
body.translated_text: 17.19 'Furthermore, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having sustained the life-forces, relinquishes the life-span forces — at that time there is an exceedingly great earthquake, a fall of meteors, a burning of the directions, and divine drums ...'

body.text: 17.20 ay(aṃ saptamo hetuḥ sap)tam(a)ḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
body.translated_text: 17.20 'This is the seventh cause, the seventh condition for a great earthquake.'

body.text: 17.21 punar aparaṃ na cirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasyānu(padhiśeṣe nirvā)ṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣy(ati || atyarthaṃ tasmin) samaye mahāpṛthivīcālaś ca bhavaty ulkāpātā diśodāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhina(dan)t(i) ||
body.translated_text: 17.21 'Furthermore, before long the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of clinging. At that time there will be an exceedingly great earthquake, a fall of meteors, a burning of the directions, ...'

body.text: 17.22 ayam aṣṭamo hetur aṣ(ṭamaḥ pratyayo mahata)ḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||
body.translated_text: 17.22 'This is the eighth cause, the eighth condition for a great earthquake.'

body.text: 18.1 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 18.1 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 18.2 yathā khalv ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavato bhāṣitasyārtham ājān(āmi bhagava)taitarhi jīvitasaṃskārān adhiṣṭhāyāyuḥsaṃskārā utsṛṣṭāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 18.2 'As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has now, having sustained the life-forces, relinquished the life-span forces.'

body.text: 18.3 evam etad ānandaivam etad ānanda || e(tarhy ānanda) tathāgatena jīvitasaṃskārān (adhiṣṭhāyāyuḥsaṃskār)ā utsṛṣṭāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 18.3 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, <s>Ānanda</s>! Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has, having sustained the life-forces, relinquished the life-span forces.'

body.text: 18.4 saṃmukhaṃ me bhadanta bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukham udgṛhītam || yasya kasyacic catvāra ṛ(ddhipādā) āsevitā bhāvitā bahul(īkṛtā ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ) k(a)lpam api ti(ṣṭh)e(t ka)lpāva(ś)e(ṣa)m api ||
body.translated_text: 18.4 'In your very presence, Venerable Sir, I heard from the <s>Bhagavān</s> directly, in your very presence I received it directly: whoever has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power (<s>catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ</s>), if he so wishes, he could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.'

body.text: 18.5 (bhagavato bhadanta catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā ākāṃkṣamāṇas tathāgatas kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā) ||
body.translated_text: 18.5 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, Venerable Sir, has cultivated, developed, and practiced extensively the four bases of supernatural power. If he so wishes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.'

body.text: 18.6 tiṣṭhatu bhagavān kalpaṃ tiṣ(ṭha)t(u) sugataḥ kalpāvaśeṣam ||
body.translated_text: 18.6 'Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> remain for a <s>kalpa</s>! Let the <s>Sugata</s> remain for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>!'

body.text: 18.7 tavaiv(ānandāpa)r(ā)dhas tav(ai)va duṣkṛ(ta)ṃ yas tv(aṃ tathāgatasya yāvat trir apy audā)r(e) 'vabhās(animi)tt(e p)rāviṣkriyamāṇe na śaknoṣi taṃ nimittaṃ prativ(e)ddhuṃ yathāpi tat sphuṭo māreṇa (pāpī)yasā ||
body.translated_text: 18.7 'This is your very fault, <s>Ānanda</s>, this is your very misdeed — that when the <s>Tathāgata</s> made manifest the conspicuous, broad sign and indication three times, you were unable to understand that sign, since you had been possessed by <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One.'

body.text: 18.8 k(iṃ) manyasa ānanda bh(āṣeta tathāgatas tāṃ vā)caṃ yā syād dvaidhavipākyā || no bhadanta ||
body.translated_text: 18.8 'What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s>? Would the <s>Tathāgata</s> speak a word that would be of twofold result?' 'No, Venerable Sir.'

body.text: 18.9 sādhu sādhv ānanda || asthānam anavakāśo yat tahāgatas tāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣeta yā syād dvaidhavipā(kyā ||)
body.translated_text: 18.9 'Good, very good, <s>Ānanda</s>! It is impossible, there is no occasion, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> would speak a word that would be of twofold result.'

body.text:
19.1 (gaccha tvam ānanda yāvanto bhikṣavaś cāpālaṃ caityam upaniśritya viharanti tān sarvān upasthānaśālāyāṃ sannipātaya ||)
19.2 (evaṃ bhadanta || āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yāvanto bhikṣavaś cāpālaṃ caityam upaniśritya viharanti tān sarvān upasthānaśālāyāṃ sannipātya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ || upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt ||)
19.3 (ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
19.4 (yāvanto bhadanta bhikṣavaś cāpālaṃ caityam upaniśritya viharanti sarve ta upasthānaśālāyāṃ niṣaṇṇāḥ sannipatitāḥ || yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate ||)
19.5 (atha bhagavān yenopasthānaśālā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ || upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat || niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma ||)
19.6 (anityā bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā adhruvā anāśvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇo yāvad alam eva bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārān saṃskaritum alaṃ virantum ||)
19.7 tasmāt tarh(i) bhikṣavo ye te dharm(ā) dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃva(r)tante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya saṃparāy(ahitāya saṃpa)rāyasukhāya te bhikṣubhir udgṛhya paryavāpya (tathā ta)th(ā) dhārayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathedaṃ brahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syāt tad bhaviṣ(yati bahu)janahitāya bahujanasukhāya lo(kānukam)pāyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ||
body.translated_text:
19.1 'Go now, <s>Ānanda</s>. Assemble all the monks who dwell in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine in the assembly hall.'
19.2 'So be it, Venerable Sir.' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, assembled all the monks who dwelt in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine in the assembly hall, and then approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side.
19.3 Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
19.4 'All the monks, Venerable Sir, who dwell in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine are seated and assembled in the assembly hall. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> now do as he sees fit.'
19.5 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:
19.6 'Impermanent, O monks, are all conditioned things (<s>anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ</s>) — unstable, unreliable, subject to change. Therefore, O monks, it is enough to grow weary of all conditioned things, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.'
19.7 'Therefore, O monks, those <s>dharmas</s> that conduce to welfare in this very life, to happiness in this very life, to welfare in the future, and to happiness in the future — those should be taken up, mastered, and upheld by monks, should be studied and recited, so that this holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) may endure for a long time. That will be for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.'

body.text: 19.8 katame te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya (saṃvartante dṛ)ṣṭadharmasukhāya sa(ṃ)parāyahitāy(a saṃparā)y(a)s(u)khāya te bhikṣubhir udgṛhya pūrvavad yāvad devamanuṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 19.8 'What are those <s>dharmas</s> that conduce to welfare in this very life, to happiness in this very life, to welfare in the future, and to happiness in the future — those that should be taken up by monks ... as before ... for the benefit of gods and humans?'

body.text: 19.9 tadyathā catvāri smṛtyup(asthānāni catvāri) s(a)myakprahāṇāni catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendri(yāṇi pañca ba)lāni sapta bodhyaṅgāny āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 19.9 'They are as follows: the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni</s>), the four right exertions (<s>catvāri samyakprahāṇāni</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ</s>), the five faculties (<s>pañcendriyāṇi</s>), the five powers (<s>pañca balāni</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>sapta bodhyaṅgāni</s>), and the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ</s>).'

body.text: 19.10 ime te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvart(ante pūrvavad yāvad devamanu)ṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 19.10 'These are the <s>dharmas</s> that conduce to welfare in this very life ... as before ... for the benefit of gods and humans.'

body.text: 20.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 20.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 20.2 āgamayānanda yena kuṣṭhagrāmakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 20.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Kuṣṭhagrāmaka</s>.'

body.text:
20.3 evaṃ bhad(ant)e(ty āyu)ṣmān ānando bhagava(taḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||)
20.4 (bha)gavān vaiśālīsāmantakenātikraman dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitenāvalok(ayati ||)
20.5 (adrākṣīd ā)yuṣmān ānando bhagavantaṃ da(kṣiṇena sarvakāye)na nāgāvalokitena vyavalokayantaṃ dṛṣṭvā punar bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text:
20.3 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
20.4 The <s>Bhagavān</s>, as he was crossing through the outskirts of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, turned and looked back with the <s>nāgāvalokita</s> (elephant-look), turning his whole body to the right.
20.5 The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> looking back with the <s>nāgāvalokita</s>, turning his whole body to the right. Having seen this, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
20.6 nā(h)e(tv apratyayaṃ bhadanta tathāga)tā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā nā(gāvalokitam ava)lokayanti || ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo nāgāvalokita(sya ||)
20.7 (e)v(am e)tad ānandaivam etad ānanda || nāhe(tv apratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitenāvalokayanti ||)
20.8 (idam ānanda tathāgatasya vaiśā)lyāḥ paścimaṃ da(r)śanaṃ na bhūya iha sa(ṃ)buddho (vaiśālīm āgamiṣyati || parinirvāṇāya gamiṣyati mallānām upavartanaṃ yamakaśālavanam ||)
20.9 (athānyataro bhi)kṣus tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ babhāṣe ||
body.translated_text:
20.6 'Surely not without reason and cause, Venerable Sir, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), look with the <s>nāgāvalokita</s> (elephant-look). What, Venerable Sir, is the reason? What is the cause for the <s>nāgāvalokita</s>?'
20.7 'Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, just so, <s>Ānanda</s>! Not without reason and cause do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones, look back with the <s>nāgāvalokita</s>, turning the whole body to the right.'
20.8 'This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s last sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Never again will the <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>. He proceeds toward <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, to the <s>Upavartana</s> of the <s>Mallas</s>, to the twin <s>Śāla</s> grove (<s>Yamakaśālavana</s>).'
20.9 Then a certain monk, at that moment, uttered this verse:

body.text:
20.10 i(dam apaścimakaṃ nātha
  vaiśālyās tava darśanam ||
body.translated_text:
20.10 'This, O Protector, is your last
  sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text:
na bhūyaḥ sugato buddho
  vaiśālīm āgamiṣyati ||
body.translated_text:
Never again will the <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>,
  come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text:
nirvāṇāya) prayāto 'yaṃ
  mallānām upavartane |
body.translated_text:
He proceeds toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
  to the <s>Upavartana</s> of the <s>Mallas</s>.'

body.text: 21.1 atha bhaga(vān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caraṅ kuṣṭhagrāmakam anuprāptaḥ kuṣṭhagrāmake viharaty uttareṇa grāma)sya śiṃśapāvane ||
body.translated_text: 21.1 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Kuṣṭhagrāmaka</s>. At <s>Kuṣṭhagrāmaka</s> he dwelt to the north of the village, in the <s>Śiṃśapā</s> (Indian rosewood) grove.

body.text:
21.2 tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate |
21.3 itīmāni bhikṣ(avaḥ śīlāni || ayaṃ samādhiḥ || iyaṃ prajñā || śīlaprabhāvitaḥ samādhiś cirasthitiko bhavati || prajñāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ samyag eva vimucyate rāgadveṣamohebhyaḥ ||)
21.4 (evaṃ samyaksuvimuktacitta āryaśrāvakaḥ samyag eva prajānāti ||)
21.5 (kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi ||)

children.text: <hier im Tib. und Skt. Uddāna; cf. MPS p. 495>:
children.translated_text: [Here in the Tibetan and Sanskrit: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse); cf. MPS p. 495]:
<s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>Gaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Āmra</s>,
<s>Jambu</s>, <s>Śūrpa</s>, <s>Tūla</s>, and <s>Hasti</s>,

body.translated_text:
21.2 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:
21.3 'These, O monks, are the precepts (<s>śīla</s>). This is concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). This is wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Concentration that is cultivated on the basis of moral conduct becomes enduring. A mind cultivated on the basis of wisdom is completely liberated from desire (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>).'
21.4 'A noble disciple whose mind is thus rightly liberated knows rightly:'
21.5 '"Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done; I know that there is nothing further beyond this existence."'

body.text:
grāmau (ca) vṛjimallau
bhoganagarakaṃ tathā |>
21.6 (yathā ku)ṣṭhagrāmaka evaṃ gaṇḍagrāmako droṇagrāmakaḥ śūrpagrāmaka ā(mragrāmako jambugrāmako hastigrāmakaḥ ||)
21.7 (vṛjigrāmakān mallagrāmakād bhoganagarakam anu)prāptaḥ || bhoganagarake viharaty uttareṇa grāmasya śiṃśapāvane ||
body.translated_text:
and the two villages of <s>Vṛji</s> and <s>Malla</s>,
and <s>Bhoganagara</s> likewise.
21.6 As in <s>Kuṣṭhagrāmaka</s>, so too in <s>Gaṇḍagrāmaka</s>, <s>Droṇagrāmaka</s>, <s>Śūrpagrāmaka</s>, <s>Āmragrāmaka</s>, <s>Jambugrāmaka</s>, and <s>Hastigrāmaka</s>.
21.7 From the <s>Vṛji</s> villages through the <s>Malla</s> village, he arrived at <s>Bhoganagara</s>. At <s>Bhoganagara</s> he dwelt to the north of the village, in the <s>Śiṃśapā</s> grove.

body.text:
21.8 ta(t)r(a bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||)
21.9 (itīmāni bhikṣavaḥ śīlāni pūrvavad yāvad nāpa)ram asmād bhāvaṃ prajānāmi ||
body.translated_text:
21.8 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:
21.9 'These, O monks, are the precepts ... as before ... I know that there is nothing further beyond this existence.'

body.text:
22.1 tena khalu samayena mahāpṛthivīcā(laś cābhūd ulkāpātā diśodāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||)
22.2 (athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ) sāyāhne pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya yena (bhaga)vā(ṃs t)e(nopajagāma || upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt ||)
22.3 (ekāntasthita āyuṣmān āna)ndo bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text:
22.1 At that time there was a great earthquake, meteors fell, the sky blazed in the cardinal directions, and celestial drums resounded in the atmosphere.
22.2 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having emerged from his evening meditation, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side.
22.3 Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 22.4 ko bhadanta he(tuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yenaitarhy abhūd mahāpṛthivīcāla ulkāpātā diśodāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinada)nti ||
body.translated_text: 22.4 'What, Venerable Sir, is the reason? What is the cause that at this time there has been a great earthquake, meteors have fallen, the sky has blazed in the cardinal directions, and celestial drums have resounded in the atmosphere?'

body.text:
22.5 traya ime ānanda hetavas trayaḥ pratyayā (mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||)
22.6 (katame trayaḥ ||)
22.7 (iyaṃ mahāpṛthivy apsu pratiṣṭhitā pūrvavad yāvac cālayanti ||)
22.8 (ayaṃ prathamo hetuḥ pra)th(amaḥ) pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcāl(asya ||)
22.9 (punar aparaṃ bhikṣur maharddhiko bhavati pūrvavad yāvac cālayati ||)
22.10 <Nur Tibetisch.>
22.11 (ayaṃ dvitīyo hetur dvitīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||)
22.12 (punar a)paraṃ na cirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasyānu(padhi)ś(e)ṣ(e) n(irvāṇa)dhātau parini(rvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati || atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcā)l(a)ś ca bhavaty ulk(āpātā diśo)dāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||
body.translated_text:
22.5 'There are three reasons, <s>Ānanda</s>, three causes for a great earthquake.'
22.6 'What are the three?'
22.7 'This great earth rests upon water ... as before ... and it trembles.'
22.8 'This is the first reason, the first cause of a great earthquake.'
22.9 'Furthermore, a monk of great supernatural power ... as before ... causes it to tremble.'
22.10 [Text only in Tibetan.]
22.11 'This is the second reason, the second cause of a great earthquake.'
22.12 'Furthermore, before long the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau</s>). At that time there will be a great earthquake, meteors will fall, the sky will blaze in the cardinal directions, and celestial drums will resound in the atmosphere.'

body.text:
22.13 ayaṃ tṛtīyo (hetu)s tṛtīy(aḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya ||)
23.1 (athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
23.2 (āsca)ryādbhutadharmasa(manvāgatā)s tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ || yatredānīṃ na cira(sya tathāgatasyānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhavi)ṣyaty aty(a)rthaṃ tasmi(n samaye) mahāpṛthivīcālaś ca bhavaty ulkāpātā diśodāhā (antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti ||)
23.3 (evam etad ānanda evam e)tad ānanda || āścaryādbh(utadharma)samanvāgatā eva tathāgatā a(rhanta)ḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ||
body.translated_text:
22.13 'This is the third cause, the third condition of a great earthquake.'
23.1 Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
23.2 'The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are endowed with wonderful and marvelous qualities! For now, before long, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (realm of nirvāṇa) without remainder, and at that very time there will be a great earthquake, and meteors will fall, and fires will blaze in the directions, and divine drums will resound in the sky.'
23.3 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, <s>Ānanda</s>. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are indeed endowed with wonderful and marvelous qualities.'

body.text:
23.4 abhijān(āmi khalu punar aham anekaśataṃ kṣatriyapariṣadaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrami)tum upasaṃkrāntasya (ca me yā)d(ṛ)śas teṣām ārohapariṇā(h)o (bhava)ti mamāpi tādṛśa āro(hapariṇāho bhavati || yādṛśī teṣāṃ varṇapuṣkalatā bhavati mam)āpi tādṛśī varṇ(apu)ṣkalatā bhavati || yādṛśī teṣāṃ sv(aragupti)r bhavati mamāpi t(ā)dṛś(ī) s(varaguptir bhavati ||)
23.5 (te yam arthaṃ mantrayanty aham api tam arthaṃ mantrayāmi || te yam a)rtha(ṃ) na mantrayanty (aha)m api tam arthaṃ (na) mantrayāmi || uttare vai (tān dhā)rmyā kathayā sandarśayāmi (samādāpayāmi samuttejayāmi saṃpraharṣayāmi tato) 'ntardhāpayāmi || antarhi(tasya) me na jānanti ka eṣa antarhito devo vā manuṣyo vā ||
body.translated_text:
23.4 'I know well that I have approached many hundreds of assemblies of <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors). And when I have approached, whatever their stature and build is, my stature and build becomes likewise. Whatever the excellence of their complexion is, my complexion becomes likewise. Whatever their manner of speech is, my manner of speech becomes likewise.'
23.5 'Whatever matter they discuss, I also discuss that matter. Whatever matter they do not discuss, I also do not discuss that matter. Then I instruct, inspire, encourage, and gladden them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, and then I make myself invisible. And when I have vanished, they do not know who that vanished being was — whether a god or a human.'

body.text:
23.6 e(vam api brāhmaṇapariṣadaṃ gṛhapatipariṣadaṃ) ś(r)amaṇapariṣadaṃ cā(turmahā)rājikān devāṃs trāyastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇara(tīn parinirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapāriṣadyān brahmapuro)hitān mahābrahma(ṇaḥ pa)rīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān a(pra)m(ā)ṇaśu(bhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛ)hān atapān sudṛś(ān sudarśa)nān akaniṣṭhān devān darśanāyopasaṃkr(amitu)m
23.7 (u)pa(saṃkrā)ntasya ca me (yādṛśas teṣām ārohapariṇāho bhavati pūrvavad yāvad de)vo vā manuṣyo vā ||
body.translated_text:
23.6 'Likewise with assemblies of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, assemblies of householders, assemblies of ascetics, the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapāriṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Abṛha</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — I have approached them all.'
23.7 'And when I have approached, whatever their stature and build is... as before, up to ...whether a god or a human.'

body.text: 23.8 (evam āścaryā)dbhutadharmasamanvāga(tās tathāgatā ar)h(a)ntaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 23.8 'Thus the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are endowed with wonderful and marvelous qualities.'

body.text: 24.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ā(nandam āmantra)yate ||
body.translated_text: 24.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
24.2 tasmāt ta(r)h(i) ta ānanda bhi(kṣubhiḥ) sūtrāntapratisaraṇair bhavitavyaṃ na pudgala(p)r(atisaraṇaiḥ ||)
24.3 (kathaṃ) bhikṣuḥ sūtrāntapratisaraṇo bhavati na (pudgalapratisaraṇaḥ ||)
24.4 ihān(a)nda bhikṣur āgacch(et sa evaṃ) vadet ||
body.translated_text:
24.2 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, monks should take the <s>sūtrāntas</s> (discourses) as their authority, not persons.
24.3 And how does a monk take the <s>sūtrānta</s> as his authority and not persons?
24.4 Here, <s>Ānanda</s>, a monk might come and say thus:'

body.text: 24.5 saṃmukhaṃ me bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukh(am udgṛhītam ayaṃ dha)rmo 'yaṃ vinaya idaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanam ||
body.translated_text: 24.5 '"Face to face with the <s>Bhagavān</s> I heard this, face to face I received it: this is the <s>Dharma</s>, this is the <s>Vinaya</s>, this is the Teacher's instruction."'

body.text: 24.6 t(asya bhikṣavas tan) notsāhayit(a)vyaṃ nāvasādayitavyam || anutsāhayitvānavasādayitvā śrotram avadhā(ya tāni pa)davyaṃjanāny udgṛhya sūtre 'vatār(ayitavyaṃ vina)y(e) saṃdarśayitavyaṃ || yadi sūtr(e) 'vatāryamāṇā vinaye saṃdarśyamānāḥ sūtre nāvataran(ti vinaye) na saṃdṛśyante dharmatāṃ ca vilomayanti (sa eva)ṃ syād vacanīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 24.6 'His words, monks, should neither be approved nor disapproved. Without approving or disapproving, having listened carefully, those words and syllables should be checked against the <s>sūtra</s> (discourses) and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline). If, when checked against the <s>sūtra</s> and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s>, they do not accord with the <s>sūtra</s> and are not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and they contradict the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>, then he should be told thus:'

body.text: 24.7 addhāyuṣmann ime dharmā na bhagavatā bhāṣitāḥ || āyuṣmatā vā ime dharmā du(rgṛhītās tathā) hīme dharmāḥ sūtre 'vatāryamāṇā vinaye saṃd(arśyamānāḥ) sūtre nāvataranti vinaye na saṃdṛśyante dharmatāṃ ca vilomayanti ||
body.translated_text: 24.7 '"Surely, venerable one, these teachings were not spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>; or else the venerable one has wrongly grasped them. For these teachings, when checked against the <s>sūtra</s> and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s>, do not accord with the <s>sūtra</s>, are not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and they contradict the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>."'

body.text: 24.8 nāyaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ vi(nayo nedaṃ śās)tuḥ śāsanam iti viditvā chorayitavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 24.8 '"This is not the <s>Dharma</s>, this is not the <s>Vinaya</s>, this is not the Teacher's instruction" — having thus determined, they should be rejected.'

body.text: 24.9 puna(r apa)ram (ānanda) bhikṣur āgacchet sa evaṃ vadet ||
body.translated_text: 24.9 'Again, <s>Ānanda</s>, a monk might come and say thus:'

body.text:
24.10 amuṣminn āvāse mahān bhikṣusaṃgha(ḥ prativasati sasthaviraḥ sapramokṣaḥ ||)
24.11 (saṃmukhaṃ me tasya mahato bhikṣusaṃghasyāntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukham udgṛhītam ayaṃ dharmo) 'yaṃ vinaya idaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ ||
body.translated_text:
24.10 '"In such-and-such a dwelling a great community of monks resides, with elders and leaders."
24.11 "Face to face with that great community of monks I heard this, face to face I received it: this is the <s>Dharma</s>, this is the <s>Vinaya</s>, this is the Teacher's instruction."'

body.text:
24.12 tasya (bhikṣavas) ta(n notsāhayitavyaṃ nāvasādayitavyam || anutsāhayitvānavasādayitvā śrotram avadhāya tāni padavyaṃja)nāny udgṛhya sūtre 'vatārayitavyaṃ vinaye saṃ(darśayitavyaṃ || yadi sūtre 'vatāryamāṇā vinaye saṃdarśyamānāḥ sūtre nāvataranti vinaye na saṃ)dṛśyante dharmatāṃ ca vilomayanti sa evaṃ syād va(canīyaḥ ||)
24.13 (addhāyuṣmaṃs tena mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena dharmasaṃjñinā ca vinayasaṃjñinā cādharmaś cāvinaya)ś ca bhāṣitaḥ || āyuṣmatā vā ime dharmā durgṛ(hītās tathā hīme dharmāḥ sūtre 'vatāryamāṇā vinaye saṃdarśyamānāḥ sūtre nāvataranti vinaye na saṃdṛśyante dharma)tāṃ ca vilomayanti ||
body.translated_text:
24.12 'His words, monks, should neither be approved nor disapproved. Without approving or disapproving, having listened carefully, those words and syllables should be checked against the <s>sūtra</s> and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s>. If, when checked against the <s>sūtra</s> and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s>, they do not accord with the <s>sūtra</s>, are not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and they contradict the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>, then he should be told thus:'
24.13 '"Surely, by that great community of monks, though they considered it <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, what is not <s>Dharma</s> and not <s>Vinaya</s> has been spoken; or else the venerable one has wrongly grasped them. For these teachings, when checked against the <s>sūtra</s> and verified against the <s>Vinaya</s>, do not accord with the <s>sūtra</s>, are not found in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and they contradict the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>."'

body.text:
24.14 nāyaṃ dharmo nāyaṃ vinayo (nedaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanam iti viditvā chorayitavyāḥ ||)

body.translated_text: 25.1 (Special Text I) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 25.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Rāmagrāmaka</s>.' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 25.3 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Krauḍya</s> territories, arrived at <s>Rāmagrāmaka</s>. At <s>Rāmagrāmaka</s> he dwelt ... [lacuna] 25.4 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In <s>Rāmagrāmaka</s> there dwells a <s>Krauḍya</s> [chieftain] named ... He, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will establish a <s>stūpa</s> for the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bodily relics in <s>Rāmagrāmaka</s>, for the sake of honoring, venerating, esteeming, worshipping, reverencing, and paying homage to the relics.' 25.5 'By this establishment of a relic-<s>stūpa</s> for the <s>Tathāgata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, he will not go to a downfall for ... <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); and having transmigrated and wandered through gods and humans, in his last existence, last abode, last embodiment, last attainment of a personal existence, having obtained a human birth, ... through righteous conduct, having shaved off his hair and beard, having put on saffron robes, having gone forth rightly with faith from the household life into homelessness, he will realize <s>Pratyeka-bodhi</s> (individual awakening).' 25.6 'In <s>Viṣṇudvīpa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śubhākṛtsna</s>. He too, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having established a relic-<s>stūpa</s> in <s>Viṣṇudvīpa</s> —' 25.7 'by this establishment of a relic-<s>stūpa</s>, he will not go to a downfall for ... <s>kalpas</s>; and having transmigrated through gods and humans... as before, up to ...he will realize <s>Pratyeka-bodhi</s>.' 25.8 'In <s>Kapilavastu</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells a <s>Śākya</s> named <s>Buddha</s>. He too, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having established a relic-<s>stūpa</s> in <s>Kapilavastu</s> —' 25.9 'by this establishment of a relic-<s>stūpa</s>, he will not go to a downfall for ... <s>kalpas</s>; having transmigrated through gods and humans... as before, up to ...he will realize <s>Pratyeka-bodhi</s>.' 25.10 'In <s>Rājagṛha</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells King <s>Ajātaśatru Vaidehīputra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>. He too, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will establish a relic-<s>stūpa</s> in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, for the sake of honoring, venerating, esteeming, worshipping, reverencing, and paying homage to the relics.'

body.translated_text:
27.6 'Prepare for the <s>Tathāgata</s> a fourfold-folded upper robe, <s>Ānanda</s>. My back is ailing; I wish to stretch it out for a while.'
27.7 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, quickly ...

27.11 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, took the bowl and went to the river <s>Kukustā</s>.
27.12 At that time, about five hundred carts had recently crossed the river <s>Kukustā</s>. The water had been stirred up, churned, and made turbid by them.
27.13 Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having taken drinking water from the river <s>Kukustā</s> with the bowl, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
27.14 'Here, Venerable Sir, about five hundred carts have recently crossed the river <s>Kukustā</s>. The water has been stirred up, churned, and made turbid by them.'
27.15 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> rinse his face and wash his feet with this water, Venerable Sir. Not far from here, Venerable Sir, is the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> may drink water and bathe his limbs.'
27.16 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> washed his feet and rinsed his face with that bowl-water. Having rested and refreshed himself, he rose and sat down cross-legged, straightening his body, and established mindfulness before him.
