body.translated_text:
28.1 At that time, <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, was traveling along that same road.
28.2 <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> — inspiring, confidence-producing, with tranquil faculties, with a tranquil mind, one who tames the minds of others, utterly calm and serene, radiant like a golden staff — seated at the foot of a certain tree.
28.3 Having seen him, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat down to one side.
28.4 The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, who was seated to one side:
28.5 '<s>Putkasa</s>, do you approve of the purity practices of any ascetic or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>?'
28.6 'Venerable Sir, I approve of the purity practices of <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>.'
28.7 'Why, <s>Putkasa</s>, do you approve of the purity practices of <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>?'
28.8 'On one occasion, Venerable Sir, <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>, while traveling, turned aside from the road and sat at the foot of a certain tree for his day's abiding.'
28.9 'At that time, about five hundred carts had recently passed along that very road.'
28.10 'Then a certain man who had been left behind those carts approached <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>. Having approached, he said this to <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>:'
28.11 '"Did you, sir, see about five hundred carts passing by?"'
28.12 '"No, good man, I did not see them."'
28.13 '"Did you, sir, not hear the sound of about five hundred carts passing by?"'
28.14 '"No, good man, I did not hear it."'
28.15 '"Were you, sir, lying asleep?"'
28.16 '"No, good man, I was not lying asleep."'
28.17 '"Were you then, sir, conscious and awake when you did not hear the sound of five hundred carts passing by?"'
28.18 '"I was indeed conscious, good man, and awake, yet I did not hear the sound of five hundred carts passing by."'

body.text:
28.19 atha tasya puruṣasyaita(d abhavat ||)
28.20 (āścaryaṃ bata pravrajitānāṃ śāntavihāriṇāṃ yatredānīṃ saṃjñī) samāno jāgran nāśrauṣīt pañcānāṃ śakaṭaśatānāṃ vyatikramamāṇā(nāṃ śabdam || tathāpi cīvaraṃ rajasāvakīrṇam ||)
28.21 (prasannaś cāsya sa puruṣo vaśīkṛtaḥ || evam evāhaṃ) bhadantārāḍasya kālāmasya śauceyān dharmān rocayāmi ||
body.translated_text:
28.19 'Then this thought occurred to that man:'
28.20 '"How wonderful are these renunciants who dwell in tranquility! For even while conscious and awake, he did not hear the sound of five hundred carts passing by. And yet his robe was covered with dust."'
28.21 'That man became full of faith and was won over. Just so, Venerable Sir, I approve of the purity practices of <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>.'

body.text: 28.22 kiṃ manyase (putkasa katara uttamo yaḥ pañcānāṃ śakaṭaśatānāṃ vya)tikramamāṇānāṃ śabdo yo vā devasya garjato 'śanyāś ca sphoṭatyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 28.22 'What do you think, <s>Putkasa</s>? Which is greater — the sound of five hundred carts passing by, or the sound of a thundering cloud and crashing lightning?'

body.text: 28.23 kiṃ bhadanta kari(ṣyanti pañcamātrāṇi daśa vā sahasraṃ vā śakaṭaśatāni || uttamaḥ) śabdo yo devasya garjato 'śanyāś ca sphoṭatyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 28.23 'What can five hundred, or ten, or even a thousand hundred carts compare to? The greater sound is that of a thundering cloud and crashing lightning.'

body.text: 28.24 eko 'yaṃ putkasa samaya ādum(ā)y(āṃ) vihar(āmi bhūtāgāre || pūrvāhṇe nivasya pātracīvaram ādāyādumāṃ piṇḍā)ya praviśāmi || ādumāṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātaḥ pra(tikramya pātracīvaraṃ pratiśamayya pādau prakṣālya bhūtāgāre niṣaṇṇaḥ pratisaṃla)yanāya ||
body.translated_text: 28.24 'On one occasion, <s>Putkasa</s>, I was dwelling at <s>Ādumā</s>, in the Ghost House. In the forenoon, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered <s>Ādumā</s> for alms. Having walked through <s>Ādumā</s> for alms, having finished the meal and returned from the alms-round, having put away the bowl and robe and washed my feet, I sat down in the Ghost House for meditation.'

body.text: 28.25 tena khalu samayenādumāyāṃ devena garjatāśanyā (ca) sph(o)ṭatyā c(atvāro balivardakā hatā dvau ca kārṣakau bhrātarau || tadādumāyā uccaśabdamahāśa)bdo mahājanakāyasya nirghoṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 28.25 'At that time, in <s>Ādumā</s>, a thundercloud crashed and lightning struck, and four draft-oxen were killed and two farmer brothers. Then a loud cry, a great noise of a multitude of people arose in <s>Ādumā</s>.'

body.text:
28.26 so 'haṃ sāyāhne pratisaṃlayan(ād vyutthāya bhūtāgārasya cchāyāyām abhyavakāśe caṅkrame caṅkramye ||)
28.27 (athānyatamaḥ pu)ruṣas tasmān mahājanakāyād yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ || upetya mam(a pādau śirasā vanditvā māṃ caṅkramamāṇam anucaṅkramyate ||)
28.28 (tam aham evam ā)mantraye ||
body.translated_text:
28.26 'I, in the evening, having emerged from meditation, was walking back and forth on the walking path in the shade outside the Ghost House.'
28.27 'Then a certain man from that great multitude of people approached me. Having approached, he bowed his head at my feet and walked along behind me as I paced.'
28.28 'I addressed him thus:'

body.text:
28.29 kim etad bhoḥ puruṣādumāyā uccaśabdamahāśabdo mahājanakāyasya ni(rghoṣaḥ ||)
28.30 (sa āha || idānīṃ bhadantādumāyāṃ devena garjatāśanyā ca sph)oṭatyā c(atvāro ba)liv(ardak)ā (hatā) dvau ca kārṣakau bhrātarau || ta(d)aiṣa uccaśabdamahāśab(do mahājanakāyasya nirghoṣaḥ ||)
28.31 (kiṃ nu bhagavān devaṃ garjantam aśaniṃ ca sphoṭatīṃ nāśrauṣīt ||)
28.32 (na bhoḥ puruṣāśrauṣam ||)
28.33 (āha sa) puruṣaḥ || ki(ṃ) nu bhagavāñ (śaye suptaḥ ||)
28.34 (na bhoḥ puruṣāhaṃ śaye suptaḥ ||)
28.35 (kiṃ nu) bhagavān saṃjñy e(va) samāno j(āgran nāśrauṣīd devasya garjato 'śanyāś ca sphoṭatyāḥ śabdam ||)
28.36 (saṃ)jñy evāhaṃ bhoḥ puruṣ(a samāno jāgran nāśrauṣaṃ devasya garjato 'śa)nyāś ca sphoṭatyāḥ śabdam ||
body.translated_text:
28.29 '"What is this, good man — this loud cry, this great noise of a multitude of people in <s>Ādumā</s>?"'
28.30 'He said: "Just now, Venerable Sir, in <s>Ādumā</s> a thundercloud crashed and lightning struck, and four draft-oxen were killed and two farmer brothers. Hence this loud cry, this great noise of a multitude of people."'
28.31 '"Did the <s>Bhagavān</s> not hear the thundering cloud and the crashing lightning?"'
28.32 '"No, good man, I did not hear it."'
28.33 'That man said: "Was the <s>Bhagavān</s> lying asleep?"'
28.34 '"No, good man, I was not lying asleep."'
28.35 '"Was the <s>Bhagavān</s> then conscious and awake when he did not hear the sound of the thundering cloud and the crashing lightning?"'
28.36 '"I was indeed conscious, good man, and awake, yet I did not hear the sound of the thundering cloud and the crashing lightning."'

body.text:
28.37 atha tasya puruṣasy(aitad abhavat || āścaryaṃ bata) tathāgatānām a(rhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śāntavihāriṇāṃ yatredānīṃ saṃ)jñy eva sam(ā)no jāgran nāśrauṣīd devasya garjato ('śanyāś ca sphoṭatyāḥ śabdam ||)
28.38 (pra)sannaś ca me sa puru(ṣo vaśīkṛtaḥ ||)
28.39 (sa āha || ko bhadanta bhaga)vato n(ā)bhiprasīdet || eṣāhaṃ bhadanta bhagava(ta udāram abhiprasannaḥ ||)
28.40 atha putkaso mallamahā(mātra upakārakaṃ puruṣam idam avocat ||)
28.41 anuprayaccha me bhoḥ (pu)ru(ṣa) navaṃ suvarṇapītaṃ duṣya(yugaṃ tenāhaṃ bhagavantam ācchādayi)ṣy(ā)mi ||
body.translated_text:
28.37 'Then this thought occurred to that man: "How wonderful are the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, who dwell in such tranquility! For even while conscious and awake, he did not hear the sound of the thundering cloud and the crashing lightning."'
28.38 'That man became full of faith and was won over.'
28.39 'He said: "Who, Venerable Sir, would not have faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>? I, Venerable Sir, am greatly inspired with faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>."'
28.40 Then <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, addressed his attendant thus:
28.41 'Give me, good man, a new pair of gold-colored garments; with them I shall cover the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: 28.42 adād upa(k)ā(rakaḥ puruṣaḥ putkasāya mallamahāmātrā)ya navaṃ (suva)r(ṇa)pī(taṃ duṣ)yayugam ||
body.translated_text: 28.42 The attendant gave <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, a new pair of gold-colored garments.

body.text:
28.43 atha putkaso ma(llamahāmātro navaṃ suvarṇapītaṃ duṣyayu)gam ād(ā)ya bhaga(vantam idam avocat ||)
28.44 (idaṃ navaṃ suvarṇapī)taṃ duṣya(yugam a)sm(ākaṃ pri)y(aṃ) manāpaṃ ca tad bhagavā(n pratigṛhṇātv anukampām upādāya ||)
28.45 (pra)tigṛhṇāti bhagavān putk(asasya mallamahāmātrasya navaṃ su)varṇapītaṃ duṣyayu(ga)m anukampām upādāya ||
body.translated_text:
28.43 Then <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, taking the new pair of gold-colored garments, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
28.44 'This new pair of gold-colored garments is dear and pleasing to us. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept them out of compassion.'
28.45 The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the new pair of gold-colored garments from <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, out of compassion.

body.text: 28.46 atha putkaso mall(amahāmātro bhagavanta)m idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 28.46 Then <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 28.47 pun(ar ahaṃ bhadantopasthāsyāmi bhagavantaṃ bhi)kṣusaṃghañ ca ||
body.translated_text: 28.47 'I shall again attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>, Venerable Sir.'

body.text: 28.48 kalyāṇam idaṃ putkasocyate bhagavān avocat ||
body.translated_text: 28.48 'This is well said, <s>Putkasa</s>,' said the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 28.49 atha pu(tka)so m(alla)mahāmātro bhagav(ato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavatpādau) śirasā vanditvā bha(ga)vato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 28.49 Then <s>Putkasa</s>, the <s>Malla</s> chief minister, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: 28.50 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmanta(m ānandam āmantra)yate ||
body.translated_text: 28.50 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: 28.51 anuprayaccha ma (ānanda navaṃ suvarṇapītaṃ duṣyayugaṃ śastra)lūnaṃ kṛtvācchādayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 28.51 'Give me, <s>Ānanda</s>, the new pair of gold-colored garments; having cut them to size, I shall cover myself with them.'

body.text:
28.52 adād āyuṣmān ānando bhagavato (navaṃ suvarṇapītaṃ du)ṣyayugaṃ śastralūnaṃ kṛ(tvā ||)
28.53 (tad ācchāditaṃ bhagavataś chavivarṇā)vabhāsena hatāvabhāsam iva khy(ā)ti ||
body.translated_text:
28.52 The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> gave to the <s>Bhagavān</s> a (new golden-yellow) pair of garments, having cut them with a blade.
28.53 (That, when draped upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, appeared as if) its radiance were outshone by the radiance of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s skin.

body.text:
28.54 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagava(n)t(am idam avocat ||)
28.55 (ahaṃ bhadanta viṃśatiṃ varṣāṇi sādhikaṃ bhagavantam) upat(i)ṣṭhā(mi) nābh(i)jānāmy (e)v(aṃ)vidhasya cchavivarṇāvabhāsasya prādurbhāvaṃ || ko bhadanta het(uḥ kaḥ pratyayo 'syaivaṃvidhasya chavivarṇāvabhāsasya prādurbhā)vāya ||
body.translated_text:
28.54 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
28.55 'Venerable Sir, (I have attended upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>) for more than twenty years, yet I have never witnessed the appearance of such a radiance of skin-color. What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, (what is the condition for the appearance of such a radiance of skin-color)?'

body.text:
28.56 evam etad ānanda || evam etad ānanda || dvāv imau hetū dvau pratyayāv asyaivaṃvidhasya (cchavivarṇāvabhāsasya prādurbhāvāya ||)
28.57 (katamau dvau ||)
28.58 (yasyāṃ rātrau bodhisat)vo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho yasyāṃ ca rātrau tathāgato 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇ(adhātau parinirvāsyate ||)
28.59 (imau dvau hetū dvau pratyayāv evaṃvidhas)ya cchavivarṇāvabhāsasya prādurbhāvāya ||
body.translated_text:
28.56 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>. So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>. There are two causes and two conditions for the appearance of such (a radiance of skin-color).
28.57 (What are these two?)
28.58 (The night on which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>) fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and the night on which the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain final <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the (remainder-less <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm).
28.59 (These are the two causes and two conditions) for the appearance of such a radiance of skin-color.'

body.text: 29.1 tatra bhagavān āyu(ṣ)m(a)ntam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 29.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
29.2 āga(mayānanda yena nadī hiraṇyavatī ||)
29.3 (evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmā)n ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text:
29.2 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, (let us go to the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>.)'
29.3 '(So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable) <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
29.4 atha bhagavān yena nadī hiraṇyavatī tenopajagām(opetya nadyā hiraṇyavatyās tīre nivāsanam ekānte sthāpayitvā nadīṃ hiraṇ)y(a)vatīm abhyavagāhya gātrāṇi pariṣicya nadīṃ hiraṇyavatīṃ pratyu(tth)ā(ya nyaṣīdad gātrāṇi viśoṣayan ||)
29.5 (atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
29.6 syād ānanda cundasya karmāraputrasya vipratisāraḥ pare(ṣām āpāditaḥ || tasya te cunda na labdham alābhā || tasya te durlabdhaṃ na sulabdhaṃ ya)sy(a) te śāstā p(a)śc(i)maṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhujyānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau pa(rinirvṛtaḥ ||)
29.7 (dvividhānanda cundasya karmāraputrasya vipratisāriṇo kaukṛtyaṃ v)inodayitavyam ||
body.translated_text:
29.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> went to the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>. (Having arrived at the bank of the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, setting down his robe in a secluded spot, he plunged into the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>), bathed his limbs, emerged from the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, (and sat down, drying his limbs.)
29.5 (Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:)
29.6 '<s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Cunda</s> the smith's son may have remorse (brought about by others): "It is your loss, <s>Cunda</s>, it was not gained. It was ill-gotten, not well-obtained, that your teacher, having partaken of his) last meal-offering, attained final <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the remainder-less <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm."
29.7 "(<s>Ānanda</s>, the remorse and regret of <s>Cunda</s> the smith's son) should be dispelled in two ways."

body.text:
29.8 saṃmukhaṃ ma āyuṣmaṃś cunda bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukh(am udgṛhītaṃ dvau piṇḍapātau samasamau vipākena ||)
29.9 (yaṃ ca piṇḍapātaṃ) bhuktvā bodhisatvo 'nuttarāṃ samya(ksa)ṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
29.8 "In my presence, venerable <s>Cunda</s>, from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s own mouth it was heard, (in his presence it was learned: 'Two meal-offerings are of equal result in their fruition.)
29.9 (The meal-offering) having eaten which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>),

body.text:
29.10 yaṃ ca piṇda(pātaṃ bhuktvā tathāgato 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyate ||)
29.11 (imau dvau piṇḍapātau) samasamau vipākena ||
body.translated_text:
29.10 and the meal-offering (having eaten which the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain final <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the remainder-less <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm) —
29.11 (these two meal-offerings) are of equal result in their fruition."

body.text:
29.12 tad idam ānanda cundena karmāraputreṇāyuḥsaṃ(vartanīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ varṇasaṃvartanīyaṃ balasaṃvartanīyaṃ bhoga)saṃvartanīyaṃ svargasaṃvar(ta)nīyam aiś(va)ryasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhaviṣya(ti ||)
29.13 (athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
29.14 (ayam āyuṣmāñ chandaś caṇḍo rabhasaḥ paruṣo roṣita ākrośa)ko bhikṣū(ṇāṃ || ta)sy(ā)sm(ābhir) bhada(n)ta (bha)gavat(o) 'tyay(ā)t kath(aṃ p)r(a)t(i)p(atta)vy(aṃ ||)
29.15 ch(an)d(a) ā(nanda bhikṣur mamātyayād brahmadaṇḍena tarjanīyaḥ || brahmadaṇḍena tarjitaś ced vipratisāra)vaś(a)m āpatsyate tathāsaṃvignaś ca kātyāyanāvavādenāvavāditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
29.12 'By this, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Cunda</s> the smith's son has performed (a deed that conduces to long life, a deed that conduces to good complexion, a deed that conduces to strength, a deed that conduces to) enjoyment, a deed that conduces to heaven, a deed that conduces to sovereignty.'
29.13 (Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:)
29.14 '(This venerable <s>Chanda</s> is violent, impetuous, harsh, wrathful, and abusive) toward the monks. How, Venerable Sir, should we (deal with him) after the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s passing?'
29.15 '<s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Chanda</s>, after my passing, should be punished with the <s>brahma-daṇḍa</s> (penalty of silence). (If, having been punished with the <s>brahma-daṇḍa</s>, he becomes filled with remorse) and is thus chastened, he should be admonished with the admonition of <s>Kātyāyana</s>.'

body.text:
30.1 tatra bhag(av)ā(n āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
30.2 (āgamayānanda yena kuśinagarī ||)
30.3 (evaṃ badantety āyuṣmān ānando) bhagavataḥ praty(a)śrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text:
30.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> (addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:)
30.2 ('Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Kuśinagarī</s>.')
30.3 ('So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>) replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
30.4 atha bhagavān antar(ā) ca nadī(ṃ) hiraṇyavatīm antarā ca kuśi(nagarīṃ malleṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ carann atrāntarādhvapratipanno mārgād avakramyāyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
30.5 (prajñāpayā)nanda tathāgatasya caturguṇam uttarāsaṅgaṃ pṛṣṭhī ma āvilāyati t(ā)ṃ tāvad āyām(ayiṣye ||)
30.6 (evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya laghu laghv eva caturguṇam utta)rāsa(ṅ)gaṃ prajñapya bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text:
30.4 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, between the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s> and <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, (wandering on a tour through the <s>Malla</s> territories, midway on the road, turning aside from the road, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:)
30.5 '(Prepare) for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, a fourfold-folded upper robe. My back is ailing; I wish (to stretch it out for a while.)'
30.6 ('So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, quickly) prepared the fourfold-folded upper robe and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

30.7 'The fourfold-folded (upper robe) has been prepared for the <s>Tathāgata</s>. (Now let the <s>Bhagavān</s> do as he sees fit.)'
30.8 (Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, placing his folded outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) upon his head,) lay down on his right side, placing foot upon foot, mindful, (fully aware, with the perception of light, keeping in mind the thought of rising.)
30.9 (There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:)
30.10 '(Let the) <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) (come to your mind), <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.translated_text:
30.11 'The <s>smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga</s> (mindfulness factor of awakening), Venerable Sir, was by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself (directly known, rightly realized, well-expounded — based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment.)
30.12 (<s>Dharmavicaya</s> (investigation of phenomena), <s>vīrya</s> (energy), <s>prīti</s> (rapture), <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) — each is a factor of awakening, (Venerable Sir, by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself directly known, rightly realized, well-expounded — based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment.)'
30.13 ('Has energy come to your mind, <s>Ānanda</s>?')
30.14 ('Energy has come to mind, <s>Bhagavān</s>.')
30.15 ('<s>Ānanda</s>, energy, when cultivated, developed, and practiced abundantly, conduces to unsurpassed perfect awakening.')
30.16 (Having spoken thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s> rose and) sat down, crossing his legs, holding his body erect, establishing mindfulness (before him.)

body.translated_text: 31.17 (ST.II) 'With what kind of inherited strength from father and mother, Venerable Sir, are the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>) endowed?'

body.text:
31.18 (ST.II) (icchatha) yūyaṃ vāsiṣṭhās tathāgatasyāntikāt tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ mātāpaitṛ(kaṃ balaṃ śrotuṃ ||)
31.19 (ST.II) (paramaṃ bhadan)ta bhagavann icchāmaḥ paramaṃ sugatecchāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
31.18 (ST.II) 'Do you wish, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, to hear from the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the inherited strength from father and mother of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones?'
31.19 (ST.II) 'Very much so, Venerable Sir, <s>Bhagavān</s>! We wish to hear.'

body.text: 31.20 (ST.II) tena hi yūyaṃ vāsiṣṭhāḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
body.translated_text: 31.20 (ST.II) 'Then listen, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, well and thoroughly bear it in mind; I shall speak.'

body.translated_text: 31.21 (Special Text II) 'The strength of ten ordinary cows equals the strength of one blue bull. The strength of ten blue bulls equals the strength of one great bull. The strength of ten great bulls equals the strength of one <s>camara</s> (yak). The strength of ten <s>camaras</s> equals one rhinoceros-strength. Ten rhinoceros-strengths equal the strength of one ordinary elephant. The strength of ten ordinary elephants equals the strength of one <s>vāmānuka</s> elephant. The strength of ten <s>vāmānuka</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>kaṇeruka</s> elephant. The strength of ten <s>kaṇeruka</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>karāḍa</s> elephant. The strength of ten <s>karāḍa</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>Nīlagiri</s> (Blue Mountain) elephant. Likewise [progressing through] <s>Pītagiri</s> (Yellow Mountain), <s>Lohitagiri</s> (Red Mountain), <s>Śvetagiri</s> (White Mountain), <s>Saugandhika</s>, <s>Madhugandhika</s>, <s>Utpalagandhika</s>, [up to] the strength of a <s>Kumudagandhin</s>. The strength of ten <s>Kumudagandhin</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>Padma</s> (Lotus) elephant. The strength of ten <s>Padma</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>Mahāpadma</s> (Great Lotus) elephant. The strength of ten <s>Mahāpadma</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>Haimavata</s> (Himalayan) elephant. The strength of ten <s>Haimavata</s> elephants equals the strength of one <s>Gajagandha</s> (Elephant-Scented) elephant. The strength of ten <s>Gajagandha</s> elephants equals the strength of one half-<s>mahānagna</s>. The strength of two half-<s>mahānagnas</s> equals the strength of one <s>mahānagna</s>. The strength of ten <s>mahānagnas</s> equals the strength of one half-<s>praskandin</s>. The strength of two half-<s>praskandins</s> equals the strength of one <s>praskandin</s>. The strength of ten <s>praskandins</s> equals the strength of one ... [lacuna] ... one <s>varāṅga</s>-strength. Ten <s>varāṅga</s>-strengths equal one half-<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-strength ... [lacuna] ... The strength of two half-<s>Nārāyaṇas</s> equals ... [lacuna] ... hundreds of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-strengths — that is the strength of one <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.'

body.translated_text: 31.22 (Special Text II) '... [lacuna] ... the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones bear such strength. And those past and those future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — all are perfectly equal: equal in voice, equal in marks, equal in qualities ... [lacuna] ... in lifespan and in bodily form.'

31.23 (ST.II) īdṛśen(a) vāsiṣṭhā mātāpaitṛkena balena samanvāgatās tathāg(atā arhantaḥ pūrvavad yāvad āyuṣā śarīradehena ca ||)

body.translated_text: 31.23 (Special Text II) 'Endowed with such paternal and maternal strength, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, are the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s> ... as before, up to ...in lifespan and in bodily form.' 31.24 'We have heard thus from the <s>Bhagavān</s> about the paternal and maternal strength of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones.'

body.text: 31.25 (ST.II) (kīdṛśena bhadanta puṇyabalena samanvāgatās tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyak)saṃbuddhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.25 (Special Text II) 'What kind of merit-strength (<s>puṇyabala</s>), Venerable Sir, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones possess?'

body.text:

body.translated_text: 31.26 (Special Text II) 'Do you, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, wish to hear from the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the merit-strength of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones?' 31.27 'Indeed, Venerable Sir! We wish it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! We wish it, O <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.translated_text: 31.28 (Special Text II) 'Then listen, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, and attend well and thoroughly; I shall speak.' 31.29 'Whatever merit, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, belongs to the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — placing that beside the merit of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, it does not reach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth ... [lacuna] ... nor does it approach even a fraction thereof.'

body.translated_text: 31.30 (Special Text II) 'Whatever merit, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, belongs to the beings of two continents — placing that beside the merit of a <s>Cakravartin</s> lord of two continents, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before, up to 'nor does it approach even a fraction.' 'Whatever merit, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, belongs to the beings of three continents — placing that beside the merit of a <s>Cakravartin</s> lord of three continents, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before, up to 'nor does it approach even a fraction.' 'Whatever merit, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, belongs to the beings of four continents — placing that beside the merit of a <s>Cakravartin</s> lord of four continents, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before, up to 'nor does it approach even a fraction.'

body.translated_text: 31.31 (Special Text II) 'There are, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, four [types of] <s>Cakravartins</s> ...' [lacuna] 31.32 'For a one-continent <s>Cakravartin</s>, an iron wheel appears, [reaching] one <s>samantakrośa</s> (league on all sides). For a two-continent <s>Cakravartin</s>, a ... wheel appears, [reaching] two <s>samantakrośas</s>. For a three-continent <s>Cakravartin</s>, a silver wheel appears, [reaching] three <s>samantakrośas</s>. For a four-continent <s>Cakravartin</s>, a divine, all-golden wheel with hub and rim appears, [reaching] four <s>samantakrośas</s>.' 31.33 '... radiant ... [lacuna] ... whatever merit [belongs to a four-continent Cakravartin] — placing that beside the merit of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great King) gods, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before, up to 'nor does it approach even a fraction.' 'Whatever merit belongs to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods — placing that beside the merit of the Four Great Kings, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before. 'Whatever merit belongs to the Four Great Kings — placing that beside the merit of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before. 31.34 'Whatever merit belongs to a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods — placing that beside the merit of ... [lacuna] ..., it does not reach even a hundredth part,' as before.

[lacuna] ... likewise the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, [with] <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> <s>devaputra</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, <s>Brahmā Sabhāpati</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Radiance) gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Unlimited Radiance) gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Streaming Radiance) gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> (Limited Beauty) gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Total Beauty) gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> (Cloudless) gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> (Merit-Born) gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit) gods, the <s>Abṛha</s> (Not Falling) gods, the <s>Atapa</s> (Without Heat) gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> (Beautiful to See) gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (Highest) gods.'

body.translated_text: 31.46 (ST.II) 'As far, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, as the <s>Ādityas</s> (suns), revolving, illuminate the directions as radiant ones — in a thousandfold world there are a thousand moons, a thousand suns, a thousand <s>Sumerus</s>, kings of mountains, a thousand ...'

body.translated_text: 31.47 (ST.II) 'The thousand of the thousandfold summit-world-systems — this is called the two-thousand-fold middle world-system. The thousand of the two-thousand-fold world-systems — this is called the three-thousand ...'

body.text: 31.48 (ST.II) sa eṣa vāsiṣṭhās trisahasramahāsahasro lokadhātuḥ pūrṇaḥ syāc chāriputrasamair bhikṣubhiḥ prajñāyās tathāgatasya prajñām upanidhāya śatimām api kalāṃ nopaiti yāvad upaniṣadam api nopaiti ||
body.translated_text: 31.48 (ST.II) 'Were this three-thousand-great-thousand-fold world-system, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, filled with monks equal to <s>Śāriputra</s> — compared with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s wisdom, their wisdom would not equal even a hundredth part, up to ...'

children.text: 31.50 (ST.II) īdṛ(śena) vās(i)ṣṭh(āḥ) prajñābal(e)na samanvāgat(ā a)rhant(aḥ) s(a)my(a)ksa(ṃ)buddhāḥ || y(e) cāt(ī)t(ā ye cānāgatāḥ) pū(r)vavad yāvad āyu(ṣā) ś(a)r(ī)r(a)d(e)h(e)n(a) c(a) ||
children.translated_text: 31.50 (ST.II) 'With such wisdom-power are the <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>) endowed — those of the past, those of the future,' as before, 'up to life-span, bodily form ...'

body.text: 31.51 (ST.II) śrutam asm(ā)bh(ir eva ta)thāgatasyāntikāt tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānā(ṃ) mātāpaitṛkaṃ balam || śrutaṃ puṇyabalam || śruta(ṃ) prajñābala(ṃ) ||
body.translated_text: 31.51 (ST.II) 'We have heard from the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself about the inherited strength of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones. We have heard about the power of merit (<s>puṇyabala</s>). We have heard about the power of wisdom (<s>prajñābala</s>).'

body.text:
ṛddhibala
31.52 (ST.II) kīdṛśena bhadantarddhibalena samanvāgat(ā arha)ntaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ||
body.translated_text:
[Supernatural power (<s>Ṛddhibala</s>)]
31.52 (ST.II) 'With what kind of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhibala</s>), Venerable Sir, are the <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones endowed?'

body.text: 31.53 (ST.II) icchatha yūyaṃ vāsiṣṭhās tathāgatasyāntikāt tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhān(ā)m ṛddhibalaṃ śrotum ||
body.translated_text: 31.53 (ST.II) 'Do you wish, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, to hear from the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the supernatural power of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones?'

body.text: 31.54 (ST.II) paramaṃ bhadanta bhagavann icchāmaḥ || paramaṃ sugatecchāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.54 (ST.II) 'Very much so, Venerable Sir, <s>Bhagavān</s>! We wish to hear. Very much so, <s>Sugata</s>! We wish to hear.'

body.text: 31.55 (ST.II) tena hi yūyaṃ vāsiṣṭhāḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
body.translated_text: 31.55 (ST.II) 'Then listen, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, well and thoroughly bear it in mind; I shall speak.'

body.text: 31.56 (ST.II) eko 'yaṃ vāsiṣṭhā()ḥ samayo vairaṇyā(yāṃ vi)harāmi naḍerapicumandamūle || tena khalu samayena vairaṇyāyāṃ durbhikṣam abhūt kṛcchraḥ kāntāro durlabhaḥ piṇḍako yācanakena bhikṣavaś (ca) lūhabho(janena) pariklamanti || atha maudgalyāyano bhikṣur yen(ā)haṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ || upetya mām idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 31.56 (ST.II) 'There was one occasion, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, when I was dwelling at <s>Vairaṇyā</s>, at the foot of a <s>naḍera-picumanda</s> tree. At that time there was a famine at <s>Vairaṇyā</s> — a time of hardship, a wilderness, when alms-food was hard to obtain by begging ...'

body.text:
31.57 (ST.II) yat khalu bhadanta bhagavāṃ jānīyāt || etarhi vairaṇyāyāṃ durbhi(kṣaṃ kṛc)chr(aḥ) kāntāro durlabhaḥ piṇḍako yācanakena bhikṣavo lūhabhojanena pariklamanti
31.58 (ST.II) saṃmukhaṃ me bhadanta bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukham udgṛhītam || yo 'syāṃ m(ahāpṛ)th(i)vyāṃ pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadhātuḥ so 'dhastād avakṣipto mamāpy evaṃ samyak pratyātmaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate || yo 'syāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadh(ātuḥ so 'dhastād avakṣipta)s tad icchāmi mahāpṛthivīṃ pariva(r)ta(yi)tu(m || yat ta)syādhastāt pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadhātus tad ūrdhvaṃ kariṣyāmi yad ūrdhvaṃ tad a(dhastāt ||)
31.59 (ST.II) (tam enam evaṃ vadāmi ||) mahāpṛthivīṃ cen maudgalyāyana parivarta(yi)tum icchasi || sa evam āha || mahāpṛthivīṃ bhadanta parivartayitum icch(āmi ||)
31.60 (ST.II) (tam enam evaṃ vadāmi || kathaṃsthi)to mahāpṛthivīṃ parivartayiṣyasi || sa evam āha || cakravāḍamahācakravāḍābhyāṃ sthāne sthito mahāpṛthi(vīṃ parivartayiṣyāmi ||)
31.61 (ST.II) (tam enam evaṃ vadāmi || ma)hāpṛthivīṃ cen maudgalyāyana parivartayitum ichasi ye pṛthivīsaṃniśritā bhūtāḥ satvāḥ prāṇinaś ca tāṃ (kathaṃ kariṣyasi || sa evam āha || mahāpṛthivīṃ) bhadanta parivartayitum icchāmi ye pṛthivīsaṃniśritā bhūtāḥ satvāḥ prāṇinaś ca tāṃ vāmena + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (mahā)pṛthi(v)īṃ parivartayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text:
31.57 (ST.II) 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> please know, Venerable Sir: at present there is a famine at <s>Vairaṇyā</s> — a time of hardship, a wilderness, when alms-food is hard to obtain by begging. The monks are suffering from meager food.'
31.58 (ST.II) ...

body.text: 31.62 (ST.II) tam enam e(vaṃ) vadāmi || mahāpṛthivīṃ maudgalyāyana parivartayaṃ kathaṃsaṃjñī (bhaviṣyasi) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (parama)laghusaṃjñī bha(vi)ṣyāmi tadyath(ā) bal(avān puruṣaḥ ka)dalīpatraṃ parivartayaṃ paramalaghu(saṃjñī) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (parama)l(a)gh(u)saṃjñī bha(vi)ṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 31.62 (ST.II) 'I said to him: "If you were to overturn the great earth, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, what would you perceive?" ... [lacuna] ... "I would perceive it as exceedingly light, just as ..."'

body.text:
31.63 (ST.II) tam enam ev(aṃ vadāmi || avasitaṃ) maudgal(yāyana ava)sitaṃ maud(ga)lyāyan(a) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + st. n. + + (e)t(e)na mah(ā)pṛth(ivīṃ parivartayitum || ta)t kasm(ād dhetoḥ)() + + + bhū(tā) + m(au)dgaly(āyan.) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (kālaṃ kur)yuḥ || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || eṣo 'pi maudgal(yāyana mahā)pḥ(thi)vy(āṃ) pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadhātur nacir + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + .y. ti tad ime satvā bhūtāḥ prāṇinaś cāhārarasagredhāt paramam utpādam āpadyeyur ucchidya kālaṃ kuryu(ḥ ||)
31.64 (ST.II) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + pṛthivīṃ parivartayitum || īdṛśena vāsiṣṭhā ṛddhibalena samanvāgato maudgalyāyano bhikṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.63 (ST.II) 'I said to him: "Enough, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, enough, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>!" ... [lacuna] ... by this [power] the great earth [was overturned] ...'

body.text: 31.65 (ST.II) (yāvad eva vāsiṣṭhā ādityāḥ pariharanto diśo) bhāsante vairocanāḥ pūrvavad yāvad ayam ucyate trisahasramahāsahasro lokadhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.65 (ST.II) 'As far, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, as the <s>Ādityas</s>, revolving, illuminate the directions as radiant ones,' as before, 'up to: this is called the three-thousand-great-thousand-fold world-system.'

body.text:
31.66 (ST.II) sa eṣa vāsi(ṣṭhās trisahasramahāsahasro lokadhātuḥ pū)rṇaḥ syād ṛddhimadbhir maudgalyāyanasadṛśair bhikṣubhis tathāgatasyarddhyām ṛddhir upanidhāya śatimām api pūrvavad y(ā)v(ad upaniṣadam api nopaiti ||)
31.67 + + + + (śrā)vakapratyekabuddhānāṃ kāyavāhinī man(o)vāhinī carddhis tathāgatānām arhat(ā)ṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānā(ṃ) manoj(avā) + + +
31.68 (ST.II) (īdṛśena vāsiṣṭhā ṛddhibalena sama)n(v)āgatās tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ || ye cātītā ye cānāgatāḥ pūrvavad yāvad (ā)yuṣā śarīradehe(na ca ||) + + +
body.translated_text: 31.66 (ST.II) 'Were this three-thousand-great-thousand-fold world-system, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, filled with monks possessing supernatural power, equal to <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> — compared with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s supernatural power, their power would not equal even a hundredth part,' as before.

body.text: Es folgt eine größere Lücke!
body.translated_text: [A larger lacuna follows in the manuscript.]

body.text: 31.70 (ST.II) + + + vā + .e + + + + (kauśināgarā ma)llā bhagavato 'nt(i)kān mohaga(tā)ḥ kathaṃcil labdh(a) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (ekatyā bā)hūn pragṛhya prakrośanti || ekatyāś cetoduḥkhasamarpitās tiṣṭhanti || ekatyā dharmatām eva prati(sma)r(anti ||) pr(ā)g evās(mā)k(aṃ bhaga)vatākhyāt(aṃ sarvair iṣṭaiḥ kāntaiḥ priyai)r manāpair nānābhāvo bhaviṣyati vinābhāvo viprayogo visaṃyogaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.70 (ST.II) ... or ... the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>, having come into the presence of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, overcome by grief, having somehow obtained ... some, raising their arms, cried out loudly; some stood immersed in mental sorrow; some reflected upon the true nature of things: "Indeed, the <s>Bhagavat</s> has previously declared to us that from all that is dear, beloved, pleasant, and agreeable, there will be separation, parting, disunion, and disconnection."

body.text: 31.71 (ST.II) atha kauśināgarā mallāḥ kapotavalgusvarā dīrgham u(cchvasya) sv(āsrūṇi ca) utstīrya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte tasthuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.71 (ST.II) Then the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>, with voices soft as doves, having drawn a long breath and wiped away their tears, bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> with their heads, and stood to one side.

body.text: 31.72 (ST.II) atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ mahatyāṃ pṛthvīśilāyām ekānte nyaṣīdat sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgh(e)na || k(au)śinā(ga)rā api malllās tasyām eva pṛthvīśilāyām ekānte nyaṣīdan ||
body.translated_text: 31.72 (ST.II) Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> sat down on one side of that great rock slab of the earth, together with the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). The <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> also sat down on one side of that same great rock slab of the earth.

body.text: 31.73 (ST.II) atha bhagavāṃ kauśināgarān mallān saṃjñ(ā)payann iva kauśināgarān mallān idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 31.73 (ST.II) Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, as if awakening the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> to awareness, spoke thus to the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>:

body.text: 31.74 (ST.II) iyaṃ vāsiṣṭhā mahatī pṛthvīśilā pūrvakalpikānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāyāmaśilā babhūva tathā hy asyā adyāpi d(ṛ)śyante 'ṅgulici(hnā)ni || evam anityā vāsiṣṭhāḥ sarvasaṃskārā evam adhruvā evam anāśvāsikā evaṃ vipariṇāmadharm(ā)ṇaḥ sarvasaṃskārā yāvad alam eva sa(r)vasa(ṃ)skār(e)bhyo nirvett(u)m alaṃ viraktum alaṃ vimoktum ||
body.translated_text: 31.74 (ST.II) "This great rock slab of the earth belonging to the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s> was a place of exercise for people of former ages; for even now the finger-marks are visible upon it. Thus impermanent, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, are all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations); thus unstable, thus unreliable, thus subject to the nature of change are all <s>saṃskāras</s>. Therefore it is fitting to become disenchanted with all <s>saṃskāras</s>, fitting to become dispassionate, fitting to become liberated."

body.text: 31.75 (ST.II) asmi(ṃ) khalu mahāsiṃhanādike dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe 'yaṃ trisahasramahāsahasro lokadhātus trikṛtvaḥ kaṃpitaḥ saṃka(ṃ)pitaḥ saṃprakaṃpitaḥ calitaḥ saṃ(ca)litaḥ saṃpracalito vyathitaḥ saṃvyathitaḥ saṃpravyathitaḥ kṣubhitaḥ saṃkṣubhitaḥ saṃprakṣubhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.75 (ST.II) When this <s>dharma</s>-discourse called the Great Lion's Roar was being spoken, this tri-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system trembled three times — it trembled, shook greatly, and shook violently; it quaked, quaked greatly, and quaked violently; it was agitated, greatly agitated, and violently agitated; it was disturbed, greatly disturbed, and violently disturbed.

body.text: 31.76 (ST.II) atha brahmaṇaḥ sabhāpateḥ śakrasya c(a deve)ndrasya svanikāyasthitayor etad abhavat || ayaṃ buddho bh(a)g(av)ā(ṃ) kuśinagarīsamīpe sthitaḥ kauśināgarān mallān mahatarddhiprātihāryeṇāvarjayi(tvā na) cirasyedānīṃ bhagavān anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parini(r)vāsyati || yannu vayaṃ gatvā bhagavantaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paścimaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 31.76 (ST.II) Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, standing each in their own assembly, had this thought: "This <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, stationed near <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, having won over the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> through a display of great supernatural power — before long the <s>Bhagavat</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder. Let us therefore go and approach the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for a final audience."

body.text: 31.77 (ST.II) a(tha brahmā) s(abhā)patiḥ śakraś ca devendraḥ svanikāye 'ntarhitau kāmāvacarair devaiḥ sār(dhaṃ) + + + + + + + + ty. .ṛ + + kaṃ + stri + brahmā sabhāpati + + + + + + + + + +
body.translated_text: 31.77 (ST.II) Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, having vanished from their own assemblies, together with the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire-realm) gods ... [lacuna] ... <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> ... [lacuna]

body.text: Textlücke
body.translated_text: [Textual lacuna]

body.text: 31.78 (ST.II) ity uktvā brahmā sabhāpatiḥ śakraś ca devendro bhagavataḥ p(ā)dau śirasā (van)d(itvā) + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + (pra)s(a)rat(a)ḥ praṇamataḥ praṇamataḥ śira(sā vanditv)ā t(a)tr(aivān)tarhitau ||
body.translated_text: 31.78 (ST.II) Having spoken thus, <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> with their heads ... [lacuna] ... advancing, bowing down, bowing down, having saluted with their heads, they vanished right there.

body.text:
31.79 (ST.II) (atha bhagavān tasya mahājanakāyasya tathābhiprasannasyāśayaṃ cānuśayaṃ) ca gatiṃ ca prakṛt(i)ñ ca vijñāya tādṛśīm eva caturāryasatyasaṃprakāś(ikāṃ dharmadeśanām akarod)
31.80 (ST.II) (yāṃ śrutvānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair uṣmagatāni) kuśalamūl(ā)ny utpāditāni ||
body.translated_text:
31.79 (ST.II) Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, having discerned the disposition, latent tendencies, destiny, and nature of that great multitude, so well disposed in faith, gave just such a <s>dharma</s>-teaching that illuminated the Four Noble Truths.
31.80 (ST.II) Having heard which, by many hundreds of thousands of living beings, wholesome roots that had reached the stage of warmth were generated.

body.text: 31.81 (ST.II) kaiścit kṣāntayo mūrdhānaḥ satyānulomikā laukikā (agradharmāḥ || kecic chrotaāpattiphale vyavasthāpitāḥ kecit sakṛdāgāmiphale kecid anāgāmi)phale kaiścit tan niṣkramya pravrajit(vā) sarvakleśaprahāṇād (ar)h(at)vaṃ sākṣīkṛtam || kaiścic chr(ā)v(akabodhau kaiścit pratyekabodhau kaiścid anuttarasamyaksaṃbo)dhau cittam u(tp)āditam ||
body.translated_text: 31.81 (ST.II) By some, <s>kṣāntis</s> (patient acceptances), <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summits), <s>satyānulomikās</s> (conformities to truth), and worldly <s>agradharmas</s> (supreme mundane qualities) were attained. Some were established in the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry), some in the fruit of <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), some in the fruit of <s>Anāgāmin</s> (non-returning); by some, having gone forth from the household life and taken ordination, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>Arhatva</s> (Arhatship) was directly realized. By some, the mind was set upon the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening (disciples' awakening), by some upon <s>Pratyeka</s>-awakening (solitary awakening), and by some the mind was generated toward <s>Anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text:
31.82 (ST.II) (avandhya)dharmadeśanā(ṃ sādareṇa) g(ṛhītvā) yadbhūyasā sā pariṣad (buddha)ni(mnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā ||)
31.83 (ST.II) (atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ parṣadaṃ buddhanimnāṃ dharmapravaṇāṃ saṃghaprāgbhārāṃ vyavasthāpyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||)
body.translated_text:
31.82 (ST.II) Having received the fruitful <s>dharma</s>-teaching with reverence, for the most part that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, flowing toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
31.83 (ST.II) Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, having established that assembly as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, flowing toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text:
32.1 (tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
32.2 (āgamayānanda yena kuśinagarī ||)
32.3 (evaṃ bhadantet)y (ā)yuṣmān (ā)nando (bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||)
32.4 (atha bhagavān malleṣu janapadeṣu caryāṃ caraṅ kuśinagarīm anuprāptaḥ || kuśi)nagaryāṃ viharati mallānām upavartane yamakaśālavane ||
body.translated_text:
32.1 There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:
32.2 "Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Kuśinagarī</s>."
32.3 "So be it, Venerable One," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
32.4 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Malla</s> territories, arrived at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>. In <s>Kuśinagarī</s> he dwelt in the <s>Upavartana</s> grove of the <s>Mallās</s>, in the grove of twin <s>śāla</s> trees.

body.text:
32.5 atha bhagavāṃs tadaiva (parinirvāṇakālasamaya āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma ||)
32.6 (prajñāpayānanda tathā)gatasyāntareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśīrṣaṃ mañcam adya tathāgatasya rātryā (madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||)
32.7 (evaṃ bhadan)tety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutyāntareṇa yamakaśā(layor uttarāśīrṣaṃ mañcaṃ prajñapya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma ||)
32.8 (upetya bhaga)vatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt ||
body.translated_text:
32.5 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, at that very time, the moment of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> having arrived, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:
32.6 "Prepare, <s>Ānanda</s>, a couch for the <s>Tathāgata</s> between the twin <s>śāla</s> trees, with the head facing north. Today, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) will take place in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder."
32.7 "So be it, Venerable One," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavat</s>, prepared a couch with the head facing north between the twin <s>śāla</s> trees, and approached the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
32.8 Having approached, he bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> with his head, and stood to one side.

body.text: 32.9 ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānand(o bhagavantam idam avocat || prajñapto bhadanta tathāgatasyāntareṇa yamakaśālayor) uttarāśīrṣo mañcaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 32.9 Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: "Venerable One, the couch has been prepared for the <s>Tathāgata</s> between the twin <s>śāla</s> trees, with the head facing north."

body.text:
32.10 atha bhagavān yena mañcas tenopajagāma || upetya dakṣiṇena pārśve(na śayyāṃ kalpayati pādaṃ pādenopadhāyālokasaṃjñī pratismṛtaḥ saṃprajāno nirvāṇasaṃjñām eva manasi kurvāṇaḥ ||)
32.11 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthito mañcam avalaṃbya prārodīd aśr(ū)ṇi vartayamān(a evam āha ||)
32.12 (atikṣipraṃ bhagavān parinirvāty atikṣipraṃ sugataḥ) parinirvāty atikṣipraṃ cakṣur lokasyāntardhīyate ||
body.translated_text:
32.10 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> approached the couch. Having approached, he lay down on his right side, placing foot upon foot, mindful, fully aware, with the perception of light, cultivating in his mind the perception of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
32.11 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, standing behind the <s>Bhagavat</s>, leaning against the couch, began to weep, shedding tears, and spoke thus:
32.12 "Too quickly the <s>Bhagavat</s> attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the eye of the world disappears!"

body.text: 32.13 pūrve ca bhikṣavas tābhyas t(ā)bhy(o digbhyas tebhyas tebhyo janapadebhya āgacchanti bhagavato 'ntikenopadarśa)nāya bhagavantaṃ paryupāsanāyai || teṣām upasaṃkrāntānāṃ bhagavān dharmaṃ deśay(aty ādau kalyā)ṇ(aṃ) ma(dh)ye kalyāṇ(aṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ) paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ prakāśayati ||
body.translated_text: 32.13 "Previously, <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) used to come from those various directions and from those various countries for an audience with the <s>Bhagavat</s>, to attend upon the <s>Bhagavat</s>. To those who had come, the <s>Bhagavat</s> would teach the <s>Dharma</s>, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, and would reveal the holy life that is complete, fulfilled, pure, and perfectly clean."

body.text:
32.14 yato ('nukā)laṃ gaṃbhīragaṃbhī(rāṃ dharmakathāṃ ye śrotum āgatās te bhaga)vān parinirvṛta iti śrutvā nāgamiṣyanti || mahato dharmasaṃbhogasy(aiva loke 'ntardhānaṃ bhaviṣyati ||)
32.15 (atha) bhagav(ā)n bhikṣūn āman(t)r(ayate ||)
32.16 (kva ca nu sthita ānando) bhikṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text:
32.14 "From time to time, those who came to hear the profound and deeply profound <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, upon hearing that the <s>Bhagavat</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will no longer come. There will be a disappearance in the world of the great enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s>."
32.15 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks):
32.16 "Where is the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Ānanda</s> standing?"

children.text: 32.17 eṣa bhadantāyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthito mañcam avalaṃbya prāro(dīd aśrūṇi pravartaya)mānaḥ
children.translated_text: 32.17 "Here, Venerable One, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> is standing behind the <s>Bhagavat</s>, leaning against the couch, weeping and shedding tears."
32.18 As before.
32.19 "...there will be a disappearance."

body.text: 32.20 tatra bhaga(v)ān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 32.20 There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
32.21 mā tvam ānanda śoca mā klā(ma || tat kasmād dhetoḥ ||)
32.22 (ta)th(āga)ta upasthitas ta (ānanda maitreṇa kāyakarmaṇā hitena sukhenādvayenāpramāṇena || maitreṇa vākkarmaṇā maitreṇa manaskarmaṇā hitena sukenādvayenā)pramāṇena ||
body.translated_text:
32.21 "Do not grieve, <s>Ānanda</s>, do not be weary. For what reason?
32.22 The <s>Tathāgata</s> has been attended by you, <s>Ānanda</s>, with friendly bodily action that is beneficial, happy, without duality, and immeasurable; with friendly verbal action, with friendly mental action that is beneficial, happy, without duality, and immeasurable."

body.text:
32.23 ye te ('tīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samya)ks(aṃ)buddhās teṣ(āṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sadṛśam upasthānaṃ kariṣyate tadyathā tvayā mahyam etarhi ||)
32.24 (ye) 'pi te bhaviṣyanty a(nāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ) samyaksaṃbuddhās te(ṣā)m api buddh(ānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sadṛśam upasthānaṃ kariṣyate tadyathā tvayā mahyam eta)r(h)i ||
body.translated_text:
32.23 "Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who existed in the past — to those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s>, equal service will have been rendered, just as you have rendered to me now.
32.24 Those who will be <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the future — to those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> also, equal service will be rendered, just as you have rendered to me now."

body.text:
32.25 (mā) tasmāt tvam ān(anda śoca mā klāma || kasmād eva tat || kuta etal labhyaṃ ya)t taj jātaṃ bhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ pūrv(avad)
32.26 (yāvad visaṃyogaḥ ||)
32.27 (atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ā)nandaṃ saṃhar(ṣayituṃ bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||)
32.28 (catvāro bhikṣava āścaryā adbhutā dha)rmā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ || katame ca(tvāraḥ ||)
32.29 (sacet kṣatriyapariṣad rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ darśa)nāyopa(saṃkrāmaty āptamanaskā bhavati darśanena || saced upasaṃkrāntāyāṃ dharmaṃ deśa)yaty āptamanaskā bhavati dharmaśr(avaṇena ||)

children.translated_text: 32.30 'If the assembly of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [approaches... as before]...'
32.31 'If the assembly of householders [approaches... as before]...'

children.text: 32.32 (chramaṇapariṣad rājānaṃ) cakravartinaṃ da(r)ś(anāyopasaṃkrāmaty āptamanaskā bhavati darśa)nena || saced upasaṃkrāntāyāṃ dharm(a)ṃ (deśayaty āptamanaskā bhavati dharmaśrava)ṇena ||
children.translated_text: 32.32 'If the assembly of ascetics (<s>śramaṇas</s>) approaches the wheel-turning king for an audience, they are satisfied at the sight. If, when the assembly has approached, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, they are satisfied by hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.translated_text: 32.25 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, do not grieve, do not be weary! For how could it be otherwise? It is impossible that what is born, come into being, made, conditioned...' as before, 32.26 '...up to ...dissociation.' 32.27 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in order to encourage the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, addressed the monks: 32.28 'There are, O monks, four wonderful and marvelous qualities of a wheel-turning king (<s>Cakravartin</s>). What are the four?' 32.29 'If the assembly of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> approaches the wheel-turning king for an audience, they are satisfied at the sight. If, when the assembly has approached, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, they are satisfied by hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: 32.33 evam eva (bhikṣavaś catvāra āścaryā adbhutā dharmā ānandasya bhikṣoḥ || katame catvā)raḥ ||
body.translated_text: 32.33 'In the same way, O monks, there are four wonderful and marvelous qualities of the monk <s>Ānanda</s>. What are the four?'

body.text: 32.34 saced bhikṣupariṣad ānan(da)ṃ (darśanāyopasaṃkrāmaty ā)ptamanaskā bhavati (darśanena || saced upasaṃkrāntāyāṃ dharmaṃ deśayaty āptamanaskā bhavati dha)rm(a)śravaṇena ||
body.translated_text: 32.34 'If the assembly of monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>) approaches <s>Ānanda</s> for an audience, they are satisfied at the sight. If, when the assembly has approached, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, they are satisfied by hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text:
32.35 sa(c)e(d) bhikṣu(ṇīpariṣad)
32.36 (upāsakapariṣad)
32.37 (upā)sikāpari(ṣad ānandaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmaty āptamanaskā bhavati darśanena || saced upasaṃkrāntāyāṃ dharmaṃ deśayaty āptamanaskā bhava)ti dharmaśrava(ṇena ||)
32.38 (apare 'pi catvāro bhikṣava āścaryā adbhutā dharmā ānandasya bhikṣoḥ || katame catvāraḥ ||)
32.39 (saced ānanda bhikṣur bhikṣupariṣade dharmaṃ deśayati satkṛtya deśa)yati nāsatkṛtya (deśayati tato bhikṣusaṃghasyaivaṃ bhavati || aho batāyuṣmān ānando dharmam eva bhāṣeta na tūṣṇīṃ syāt || atṛptaiva bhavati bhikṣupariṣad ānandasya) bh(i)kṣor dharmaśravaṇena || (punar ānando bhikṣus) tūṣṇīṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 32.35 'If the assembly of nuns (<s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>) [approaches... as before]...' 32.36 '[If] the assembly of male lay followers (<s>upāsakas</s>) [approaches... as before]...' 32.37 '[If] the assembly of female lay followers (<s>upāsikās</s>) approaches <s>Ānanda</s> for an audience, they are satisfied at the sight. If, when the assembly has approached, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, they are satisfied by hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.' 32.38 'There are yet another four wonderful and marvelous qualities of the monk <s>Ānanda</s>. What are the four?' 32.39 'If <s>Ānanda</s> the monk teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the assembly of monks, he teaches it respectfully, not disrespectfully. Then the community of monks thinks thus: "Oh, if only the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> would continue speaking the <s>Dharma</s> and not fall silent!" The assembly of monks is never sated with the monk <s>Ānanda</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Then <s>Ānanda</s> the monk falls silent.'

body.text:
32.40 saced bhikṣuṇīpariṣada
32.41 upāsakapari(ṣada)
32.42 upāsikāpariṣade dharmaṃ deśa(yati) satkṛtya deśayati nās(atkṛtya deśayati tata upāsakasaṃghāder e)vaṃ bhavati || aho batāyuṣmān ānando dharmam eva bhāṣeta na tūṣṇīṃ syāt || atṛptaiva bhavaty upāsikāpariṣad ānandasya bhikṣor dharma(śravaṇena ||) punar ānando bhikṣu(s) t(ūṣṇīṃ bha)vati ||
body.translated_text: 32.40 'If [he teaches] the assembly of nuns...' 32.41 'the assembly of male lay followers...' 32.42 'If [he teaches] the <s>Dharma</s> to the assembly of female lay followers, he teaches it respectfully, not disrespectfully. Then the assembly of lay followers and others thinks thus: "Oh, if only the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> would continue speaking the <s>Dharma</s> and not fall silent!" The assembly of female lay followers is never sated with the monk <s>Ānanda</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Then <s>Ānanda</s> the monk falls silent.'

body.text: 33.1 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavatā saṃharṣito bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 33.1 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having been encouraged by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 33.2 saṃvidyante bhadantemāny evaṃrū(pāṇi mahānagarāṇi tadyath)ā śrāvas(t)ī (sāke)taṃ caṇpā bārāṇasī v(ai)śālī rājagṛham || kasmād bhagavān evaṃrūpāṇi mahānagarāṇy utsṛjyāsmiṃ ku(nagarake kuṃjakalake koṭṭe śākhāna)garake nagarasthāṇuke parin(i)rvātavyaṃ manyate ||
body.translated_text: 33.2 'There exist, Venerable Sir, great cities of such kind — namely, <s>Śrāvastī</s>, <s>Sāketa</s>, <s>Campā</s>, <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Why does the <s>Bhagavān</s>, leaving aside such great cities, choose to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this miserable little town, this small jungle settlement, this backwater, this branch-town, this mere stump of a city?'

body.text: 33.3 mā ()tvam ānanda kuśinagarīṃ kunagarakaṃ manyasva kuṃjakalakaṃ vā ko(ṭṭaṃ śākhānagarakaṃ vā nagarasthāṇu)kaṃ vā || tat kasmād dhetoḥ ||
body.translated_text: 33.3 'Do not, <s>Ānanda</s>, think of <s>Kuśinagarī</s> as a miserable little town, a small jungle settlement, a backwater, a branch-town, or a mere stump of a city! For what reason?'

body.text: 34.1 bhūtapūrvam ānanda kuśinagarī (kuś)āvatī nāma rājadhānī babhūva || ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca s(ubhikṣā cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca dvādaśa yo)janāny āyāmena saptayojanāni vistāreṇa ||
body.translated_text: 34.1 'In the past, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Kuśinagarī</s> was a royal capital named <s>Kuśāvatī</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people — twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length and seven <s>yojanas</s> in width.'

body.text: 34.2 kuśāvat(y) ānanda rājadhānī saptabhiḥ prākāraiḥ parikṣiptā babhūva catu(r)v(i)dh(ai)ḥ prākār(ai)ḥ s(au)va(r)ṇ(ai) rājat(ai)r v(aiḍūryamayaiḥ) sphaṭikamayaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.2 'The royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, was surrounded by seven ramparts — ramparts of four kinds: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), and crystal.'

body.text: 34.3 kuśāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ caturvidhāni dvārāṇi māpitāny abhūvan sauvarṇāni rājatāni vaiḍūryamayāṇi sphaṭikamayāni ||
body.translated_text: 34.3 'In the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, gates of four kinds were constructed: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal.'

body.text: 34.4 teṣu khalu (dvāreṣ)u (catu)rvidhā iṣ(ṭi)kā māpitā abhūvan sauvarṇā rājatā vaiḍūryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ saptapauruṣā ardhacaturthapauruṣāś ca nikhātā dṛḍhāḥ sthirāḥ sāravatyo 'calā asaṃpravedhinyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.4 'At those gates, pillars of four kinds were constructed: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal — seven times the height of a man, and three-and-a-half times the height of a man sunk into the ground, firm, stable, solid, immovable, and unshakable.'

body.text: 34.5 kuśāvatī rājadhānī saptabhiḥ parikhābhiḥ parikṣiptā babhūva || tāḥ khalu parikhāś caturvidhābhir iṣṭikābhiś citā abhūvan sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.5 'The royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s> was surrounded by seven moats. Those moats were lined with bricks of four kinds: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal.'

body.text: 34.6 kuśāvatī rājadhānī saptabhis tālapaṅktibhiḥ parikṣiptā babhūva caturvidhais tālaiḥ sauvarṇai rājatair vaiḍūryamayaiḥ sphaṭikamayaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.6 'The royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s> was surrounded by seven rows of palm trees — palm trees of four kinds: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal.'

body.text: 34.7 sauvarṇasya tālasya rājataṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ māpitam abhūt || rājatasya sauvarṇaṃ vaiḍūryamayasya sphaṭika(mayaṃ sphaṭikama)yasya (v)aiḍūryamayaṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ māpitam abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 34.7 'The golden palm tree had leaves, flowers, and fruit fashioned of silver. The silver palm tree had those of gold. The <s>vaiḍūrya</s> palm tree had leaves, flowers, and fruit fashioned of crystal. The crystal palm tree had those of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>.'

body.text: 34.8 teṣāṃ khalu tālānāṃ vāyunā pre(rit)ānām ayam evaṃrūpo manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati (yathā pañcāṅgikasya) tūryasya kuśalena puruṣeṇa samyaksupravāditasya ||
body.translated_text: 34.8 'When those palm trees were stirred by the wind, there issued forth a sound so pleasant — like a five-part musical ensemble well-played by a skilled musician.'

body.text: 34.9 tāsu khalu tālāntarikāsu puṣk(a)riṇy(o) māpitā abhūvan tāḥ khalu puṣkariṇ(yaś caturvidhābhir iṣṭikā)bh(i)ś c(i)tā abhūvan sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.9 'In the spaces between those palm trees, lotus ponds were constructed. Those lotus ponds were lined with bricks of four kinds: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal.'

body.text: 34.10 tāsu khalu puṣkariṇīṣu caturvidhāni sopānān(i māpitāny abhū)va(n) sauvarṇāni rājatāni vaiḍūryamayāṇi sphaṭikamayāni ||
body.translated_text: 34.10 'In those lotus ponds, stairways of four kinds were constructed: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal.'

body.text: 34.11 tāḥ khalu puṣkariṇyaś c(aturvi)dhābhir vedikābhiḥ parikṣiptā abhūvan sauvarṇ(ībhī rā)jatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ || sauvarṇyā vedikāyā rājataṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt || rājatyāḥ sauvarṇaṃ sphaṭikam(ayyā vaiḍūryama)yaṃ vaiḍūryamayyāḥ sphaṭikamayaṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 34.11 'Those lotus ponds were surrounded by railings of four kinds: golden, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal. The golden railing had its needles, crossbars, and base fashioned of silver. The silver railing had those of gold. The crystal railing had those of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>. The <s>vaiḍūrya</s> railing had its needles, crossbars, and base fashioned of crystal.'

body.text: 34.12 tāsu khalu puṣkariṇīṣu vividhāni jalajāni mālyāni ropitā(ny abh)ūvan tadyathotpalaṃ padmaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ saugandhikaṃ madhugandhikaṃ sarvartukaṃ sarvakālikam anāvṛtaṃ sarvajanasya ||
body.translated_text: 34.12 'In those lotus ponds, various water-born flowers were planted: namely, <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily), <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus), <s>saugandhika</s>, and <s>madhugandhika</s> — [blooming in] all seasons, at all times, open to all people.'

body.text: 34.13 tāsāṃ kha(lu) p(uṣ)kariṇīnāṃ tīreṣu vividhāni sthalajāni mālyāni ropitāny abhūvan tadyathātimuktakaś campakaḥ pāṭalā vārṣikā mālikā navamālikā sumanā yū(thikā dhānuṣk)ārī sarvartukaṃ sarvakālikam anāvṛtaṃ sarvajanasya ||
body.translated_text: 34.13 'On the banks of those lotus ponds, various land-born flowers were planted: namely, <s>atimukta</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, <s>vārṣikā</s>, <s>mālikā</s>, <s>navamālikā</s>, <s>sumanā</s>, <s>yūthikā</s>, and <s>dhānuṣkārī</s> — [blooming in] all seasons, at all times, open to all people.'

body.text: 34.14 tāsāṃ khalu puṣkariṇīnāṃ tīreṣu rājñā mahāsudarśanena kanyāḥ sthāpitā (abhūvan) yā annam annārthibhyaḥ prayacchanti pānaṃ pānārthibhyo vastraṃ vastrārthibhyaḥ || mālāgandhavilepanāni mālāgandhavilepanārthibhyaḥ prayacchanti ||
body.translated_text: 34.14 'On the banks of those lotus ponds, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> had stationed maidens who gave food to those seeking food, drink to those seeking drink, garments to those seeking garments, and garlands, fragrances, and ointments to those seeking garlands, fragrances, and ointments.'

body.text:
34.15 ye khal(u) kuśāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ dhūrtā vā matt(ā vā śauṇḍā vā krīḍitukāmā rami)tukāmāḥ paricārayitukāmā bhavanti te tāsu tālāntarikāsu krīḍanti ramanti paricār(ayanti ||)
34.16 tenaiva tālavṛntaśabdena kuśāvat(y ānanda rājadhānī dvādaśena) vin(ā)ditā babhūva tadyathā hastiśabdenāśvaśabdena rathaśabdena pattiśabdena śaṃkha(śabdena) paṭahaśabdena bherīśabdena mṛ(daṅgaśabdena vādyaśabdena gītaśabdena vaṃśa)śabdena || dānāni dadata || puṇyāni kuruta || upa(v)āsam upavasata || śīlaṃ samādāya vartadhva(ṃ) śabdena ||
body.translated_text: 34.15 'Those in the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s> who were rogues, drunkards, topers, or those desiring play, pleasure, and entertainment — they would play, enjoy, and entertain themselves in those spaces between the palm trees.' 34.16 'By that very sound of the palm-leaf fans, the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, was filled with twelve kinds of sound — namely: the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of infantry, the sound of conches, the sound of kettledrums, the sound of drums, the sound of <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, the sound of music, the sound of singing, the sound of flutes — and the sound [proclaiming]: "Give gifts! Make merit! Observe the fast-day! Undertake and maintain the precepts!"'

body.text: 34.17 kuś(ā)vat(y)ām ānanda rājadh(ā)ny(āṃ rājā mahā)sudarśano nāma( babhū)v(a) saptabhī ratnaiḥ samanvāgataś catasṛbhiś ca mānuṣikābhir ṛddhibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.17 'In the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there was a king named <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, endowed with the seven treasures and the four kinds of human prosperity (<s>mānuṣikā ṛddhi</s>).'

body.text: 34.18 katamaiḥ saptabhiḥ || tadyathā cakraratnena hastiratnenāśva(ratnena maṇiratne)n(a) strīratnena gṛhapatiratnena pariṇāyakaratnena saptamena ||
body.translated_text: 34.18 'What are the seven [treasures]? They are: the wheel-treasure (<s>cakraratna</s>), the elephant-treasure (<s>hastiratna</s>), the horse-treasure (<s>aśvaratna</s>), the jewel-treasure (<s>maṇiratna</s>), the woman-treasure (<s>strīratna</s>), the householder-treasure (<s>gṛhapatiratna</s>), and as the seventh, the counselor-treasure (<s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>).'

body.text: 34.19 katamābhiś catasṛbhir mānuṣikābhir ṛddhibhiḥ || rājā mahā(sudarśano dīrghāyuṣko ')bhūc cirasthitikaḥ || sa caturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇi kumārakrīḍāyāṃ krīḍitavān || caturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇi yauvarā(jyaṃ kāritavān ||) caturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇi mahārājyaṃ kāritavān || caturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇi rājarṣir brahmacaryam acārṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 34.19 'With which four human supernatural powers [was he endowed]? King Mahāsudarśana was long-lived, of long duration. He spent eighty-four thousand years in princely sports; eighty-four thousand years ...'

body.text: 34.20 yad ānanda rājā mahāsuda(r)ś(ano dīrghāyuṣko 'bhūc cirasthitikaś catu)raśītivarṣasahasrāṇi kumārakakrīḍāyāṃ krīḍitavān pūrvavat || iyaṃ rājño mahāsudarśanasyarddhir ity (u)cyate ||
body.translated_text: 34.20 'That King Mahāsudarśana was long-lived, of long duration — he spent eighty-four thousand years in princely sports,' as before. 'This is called the supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) of King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>.'

body.text: 34.21 punar a(paraṃ rājā mahāsudarśano ')bhirūpo 'bhūd darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrāntaś ca mānuṣyakaṃ varṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam ||
body.translated_text: 34.21 'Furthermore, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> was handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, surpassing the human complexion but not yet attaining the divine complexion.'

body.text: 34.22 yad ānanda rājā mahāsuda(r)śan(o 'bhirūpo 'bhūd darśanīyaḥ pūrvavat || iyaṃ rā)jño mahāsudarśanasyarddhir ity ucyate ||
body.translated_text: 34.22 'That King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> was handsome, beautiful,' as before. 'This is called the supernatural power of King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>.'

body.text:
34.23 punar aparaṃ rājā mahāsudarśano 'lpābādho 'bhūd arogajātīyaḥ samav(ipacanayā grahaṇyā samanvāgato nātyu)ṣṇayā nātiśītayāvyābādhayartusukhayā yayāsyāśitapītakhāditāsvāditaṃ samyak sukhena paripākaṃ (gatam abhūt ||)
34.24 (yad ānanda rājā mahā)sudarśano 'lpābādho 'bhūd arogajātīyaḥ pūrvavat || iyaṃ rājño mahāsudarśanasyarddhir ity ucyate ||
body.translated_text: 34.23 'Furthermore, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> had few ailments, was of healthy constitution, endowed with an even digestion — neither too hot nor too cold, free from disease, comfortable in all seasons — so that whatever he ate, drank, chewed, or tasted ...'

body.text: 34.25 punar aparaṃ rājā mahāsuda(r)ś(anaḥ sarva)j(ā)n(a)padānāṃ priyaś cābhūn manāpaś ca tadyathā putrāṇāṃ pitā || rājño 'pi mahāsudarśanasya naigamaj(ā)napadāḥ priy(ā)ś cā(bhūvan manāpāś ca tadyathā pi)tuḥ putrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.25 'Furthermore, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> was beloved and dear to all the people of the realm, just as a father is to his children. And the townspeople and countryfolk were also beloved and dear to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> ...'

body.text:
34.26 eko 'yaṃ samayo rājā mahāsudarśana udyānabhūmiṃ niryān sārathim āmantrayate || manda(ṃ) mandaṃ tāvat sārathe rathaṃ (vartaya yathāhaṃ naigamajānapadāṃś ciraṃ paśyeyaṃ || naigamajāna)padā api tatra sārathim āmantrayante || (mandaṃ mandaṃ tāvat sārathe rathaṃ vartaya yathā vayaṃ devaṃ ciraṃ paśyema ||)
34.27 (yad ānanda rājā mahāsudarśanaḥ sarvajānapadānāṃ priyaś cābhūn) manāpaś ca pūrvavat || i(yaṃ rājño mahāsudarśanasyarddhir ity ucyate ||)
34.28 (atha naigama)jānapadāḥ prabhūtaṃ suvarṇam ādāya maṇi(ratnaṃ ca kaṃbalaratnaṃ ca yena rā)jā mahāsudarśanas te(nopajagmuḥ || upetya rājānaṃ mahāsudarśanam idam avocan ||)
34.29 (idaṃ devāya prabhū)taṃ suvarṇam ānītaṃ maṇiratnaṃ ca kaṃbalaratnaṃ ca || tad devaḥ pra(tigṛhṇātv anukampām upādāya ||)
34.30 (madrājye 'pi yad evaṃ dhanajātam ity uktvā niravekṣāsyotpannā pratigrahītuṃ nādhivāsayati ||)
34.31 (nai)gamajānapadā rājānaṃ mahā(sudarśanam idam avocan ||)
34.32 (idaṃ devāya prabhūtaṃ suvarṇam ānītaṃ maṇiratnaṃ ca kaṃbalaratnaṃ ca || tad devaḥ pratigṛhṇātv anu)kampām upādāya ||
body.translated_text: 34.26 'On one occasion, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, going out to the garden grounds, addressed his charioteer: "Drive the chariot slowly, slowly, charioteer, so that I may gaze upon the townspeople and countryfolk for a long time." The townspeople and countryfolk ...'

body.text:
34.33 dvir api trir a(pi rājā mahāsudarśano naigamajānapadān āmantrayate ||)
34.34 (madrājye 'pi ya)d (e)va(ṃ) dhanajāta(m) ity uktvā nirav(e)kṣā(sy)ot(pannā pratigrahītuṃ nā)dhivāsayati ||
body.translated_text:
34.33 'A second time and a third time, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> addressed the townspeople and countryfolk:'
34.34 '"Whatever wealth there is in my kingdom" — having said this, he looked [at them] without concern, not consenting to accept ...'

body.text:
34.35 atha naigamaj(ānapadānām etad abhavat ||)
34.36 (nāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ syād yad idaṃ devāya prabhūtaṃ suvarṇam ānīya maṇiratnaṃ ca kaṃbalaratnaṃ ca) tad vayam ādāya svakasvaka(niveśanaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ || yannu vayaṃ rājño mahāsudarśanasya purato mahāntaṃ suvarṇasya ca rājata)sya (ca rā)śim ākīrya maṇiratnaṃ kaṃbalaratnaṃ caikānta upanikṣipy(ai)t(ad) de(vasya dhanajātam ity upekṣya prakrāmema ||)
34.37 (iti viditvā rājño mahāsudarśanasya pu)rato mahāntaṃ suvarṇa(sya ca rājatasya ca rāśim ākīrya maṇiratnaṃ kaṃbalaratnaṃ caikānta upanikṣipyaitad devasya dhanajātam ity upekṣya prakrāntāḥ ||)
34.38 (atha rājño mahā)sudarśanasyaitad abhavat ||
body.translated_text:
34.35 Then this thought occurred to the townspeople and countryfolk:
34.36 '"It would not be fitting for us [to let this be]. Let us bring to the lord abundant gold, jewel-treasures, and blanket-treasures." Having taken these, each from his own [stores] ...'

body.text:
34.39 saṃpanna(ṃ) me dhanajātaṃ dharmeṇa nādharmeṇa || yannv ahaṃ dh(ārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpayeyam ||)
34.40 (aśrauṣuś caturaśītikoṭṭarāja)sahasrāṇ(i) rājā mahāsudarśano dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpayitukāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
34.39 '"My wealth is righteously obtained, by <s>Dharma</s>, not by <s>adharma</s>. What if I were to have a <s>Dharma</s>-palace constructed?"'
34.40 'Eighty-four thousand vassal kings heard that King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> [intended to build] a <s>Dharma</s>-palace ...'

body.text: 34.41 śrutvā ca (yena rājā mahāsudarśanas tenopajagmuḥ || upetya rājānaṃ) mah(ā)sudarśanam idam avocan ||
body.translated_text: 34.41 'Having heard, they approached King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>. Having approached, they said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:'

body.text: 34.42 alpotsuko devo bhavatu dhārmāt prāsādāt (|| vayaṃ dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpa)yiṣy(ā)maḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.42 '"Let the lord be of little concern regarding the <s>Dharma</s>-palace. We shall have the <s>Dharma</s>-palace constructed."'

body.text: 34.43 (grā)m(aṇ)y(o madrājye 'py evaṃ)rūpāṇi (dha)najātāny ity (uktvā nādh)i(vāsa)yati ||
body.translated_text: 34.43 '"There are such kinds of wealth in my kingdom, headmen" — having said this, he did not consent.'

body.text: 34.44 (dvir api trir api caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi rājānaṃ mahā)sudarśanam idam avocan ||
body.translated_text: 34.44 'A second time and a third time, the eighty-four thousand vassal kings said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:'

body.text:
34.45 a(l)p(otsuko devo bhavatu dhārmāt prāsādāt || vayaṃ dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpayiṣyāmaḥ ||)
34.46 (dvir api trir api rājā mahāsudar)śanaś caturaśītiṃ koṭṭarājasaha(srāṇy āmantrayate ||)
34.47 (grāmaṇyo madrājye 'py evaṃrūpāṇi dhanajātāny ity uktvā nādhivāsayati ||)
34.48 atha caturaśītiḥ koṭṭarājasaha(srāṇi rājño mahāsudarśanas)y(a pāda)y(or vai) ś(irasās)ādya || e(ka)tyā bāhū(n) pragṛhya || ekatyāś cīv(arakarṇakaṃ pragṛhya ||) ekatyā yena rājā mahāsudarśa(nas tenāñ)jali(ṃ) praṇamya rājānaṃ mahāsudarś(anam idam a)vo(can ||)
34.49 alpotsuko devo bh(avatu dhārmāt prāsādāt || vayaṃ dhā)rma(ṃ) prāsādaṃ māpayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
34.45 '"Let the lord be of little concern regarding the <s>Dharma</s>-palace. We shall have the <s>Dharma</s>-palace constructed."'
34.46 'A second time and a third time, King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> addressed the eighty-four thousand vassal kings ...'

body.text:
34.50 adhivāsayati rājā mahāsudarśanaś caturaś(ī)ti(koṭṭarājasa)hasrāṇāṃ tūṣṇ(ī)mbh(āvena ||)
34.51 (atha caturaśītikoṭṭarājasaha)srāṇi rājño mahāsudarśanasya tūṣṇī(mbhāvenādhi)vāsanaṃ viditvā svakasvakani(veśana)m āgatya
34.52 prabhūtaṃ suvarṇa(hiraṇyam ekaikaṃ ca ratnastambham ādāya) y(e)na rājā mahāsudarśanas tenopasaṃkr(ān)t(ā)ḥ || āgatya rājā(naṃ mahāsudarśa)nam idam avocan ||
body.translated_text:
34.50 'King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> consented to the eighty-four thousand vassal kings by silence.'
34.51 'Then the eighty-four thousand vassal kings, understanding King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>'s consent through his silence ...'

body.text: 34.53 kutra vayaṃ deva (dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpayema kī)van vā ||
body.translated_text: 34.53 '"Where, O lord, shall we construct the <s>Dharma</s>-palace, and of what size?"'

body.text:
34.54 tena hi yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ pū(rveṇa kuśāva)ty(ā r)ā(jadhā)ny(ā) asya dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ mā(pa)yatha yojanam āyāmena yoja(naṃ vistāreṇa ||)
34.55 (evaṃ deveti caturaśītikoṭṭarājasaha)srāṇi rājño mahāsudarśanasya (pratiśrutya pūrveṇa kuśāvatyā) dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ māpayanti (taṃ ca) yojanam āyāmena yojana(ṃ) vistā(reṇa ||)
34.56 (dhārma ānanda prāsāde caturvi)dhāni prācīnāni māpit(ā)ny a(bhū)van (s)auvarṇāni rājatāni vaiḍūrya(ma)yāṇi sphaṭi(kama)yāni || caturvidhāny ās(anāni māpitāny abhūvan sauvarṇāni rājatāni) vaiḍū(r)yamayā(ṇi) s(phaṭikamayāni ||)
34.57 dhārme prāsāde caturv(i)dhāḥ staṃbhā ucchritā abhūvan sauvarṇā rājatā vaiḍūryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ ||
body.translated_text:
34.54 '"Then, headmen, to the east of <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, the royal capital, construct this <s>Dharma</s>-palace — one <s>yojana</s> in length and one <s>yojana</s> in breadth."'
34.55 '"So be it, O lord," the eighty-four thousand vassal kings ...'

body.text: 34.58 sauvarṇasya staṃbhasya rājataḥ ku(ṃ)bhakaḥ kṛpaṭakaśīrṣakaṃ go(sā)rako māpito babhūva || rājatasya sauvarṇaḥ vaiḍūryamayasya spha(ṭ)ikamayaḥ sph(aṭikamayasya s)t(aṃ)bhasya vaiḍūryamayaḥ kuṃbhakaḥ kṛpaṭakaśīrṣakaṃ gosārako māpito babhūva ||
body.translated_text: 34.58 'For a golden pillar, a silver capital, bracket, and head-piece with a bull-ornament were constructed. For a silver [pillar], a golden [capital]; for one of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), one of crystal; for a crystal pillar ...'

body.text: 34.59 dhārme prāsāde ca(turvidhā gopānasyo māpitā abhūvan sauvarṇā rāja)tā vaiḍūryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.59 'In the <s>Dharma</s>-palace, four kinds of rafters were constructed — golden, silver, of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and of crystal.'

body.text:
34.60 dhārme prāsāde caturvidhā baladharaṇīyā māpitā abhūvan sauv(arṇā rājatā vaiḍūryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ ||)
34.61 (dhārme prā)sāde caturvidhā avaṣaṅgā māpitā abhūvan sauvarṇā rājatā vaiḍūryamayāḥ (s)phaṭikamayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.60 In the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, four types of pillars (<s>baladharaṇīya</s>) were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal). 34.61 In the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, four types of hooks (<s>avaṣaṅga</s>) were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>.

body.text: 34.62 dhārme (p)r(āsāde caturvidhā aṭṭālā māpitā abhūvan sauvarṇā rājatā vaiḍū)ryamayāḥ sphaṭikamayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.62 In the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, four types of watchtowers (<s>aṭṭāla</s>) were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>.

body.text:
34.63 dhārmaḥ prāsādaś (ca)turvidhaiḥ phalakaiś channo 'bhūt sauvarṇai rājatair vaiḍūryamayai(ḥ sphaṭikamayaiḥ ||)
34.64 (dhārme prāsāde caturvidhāni sopānāni māpitāny abhūvan) sauvarṇāni rājatāni vaiḍūryamayāṇi sph(aṭi)kamayāni ||
body.translated_text: 34.63 The <s>Dharma</s> Palace was covered with four types of panels (<s>phalaka</s>): golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. 34.64 In the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, four types of staircases (<s>sopāna</s>) were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>.

body.text:
34.65 dhārmaḥ prāsādaś caturv(i)dhābhir vedikābhiḥ parikṣipto ('bhūt sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ ||)
34.66 sauvarṇyā v(e)dikāyā rājataṃ sūcy(ā)l(aṃ)banam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt || rāja(ty)āḥ sauvarṇaṃ vaiḍūrya(mayyāḥ sphaṭikamayaṃ sphaṭikamayyā vaiḍūryamayaṃ sūcyālaṃba)nam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 34.65 The <s>Dharma</s> Palace was enclosed by four types of railings (<s>vedikā</s>): golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. 34.66 On the golden railing, a silver needle-pendant (<s>sūcyālaṃbana</s>) base was constructed. On the silver [railing], a golden one; on the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [a base] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; on the <s>sphaṭika</s> one, [a base] made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — [such] needle-pendant bases were constructed.

body.text: 34.67 dhārma ānanda prāsāde caturaśītikūṭāgārasahasrāṇi māpitā(ny abhūvan ekaikaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ tadyathā sauvarṇānāṃ) rājatānāṃ vaiḍūryamayāṇāṃ sphaṭikamayānām ||
body.translated_text: 34.67 'In the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, O <s>Ānanda</s>, eighty-four thousand pavilions (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>) were constructed, each of four colors — namely, golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and made of <s>sphaṭika</s>.'

body.text:
