34.68 sauvarṇe kūṭāgāre rājataḥ paryaṅkaḥ sthāpito 'bhū(t paṭikāstṛto goṇikāstṛtas tūlikāstṛtaś citrikā)stṛtaḥ paṭalikāstṛtaḥ kāliṅgaprāvārapratyāstaraṇaḥ sottaracchadapaṭa ubhayāntalo(hitopadhānaḥ ||)
34.69 (rājate sauvarṇo vaiḍūryamaye sphaṭikama)yaḥ sphaṭikamaye vaiḍūryamayaḥ paryaṅkaḥ sthāpito 'bhūt paṭikāstṛto goṇikāstṛtas tūlikāstṛtaś citri(kāstṛtaḥ paṭalikāstṛtaḥ kāliṅgaprāvārapratyā)staraṇaḥ sottaracchadapaṭa ubhayāntalohitopadhānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.68 In the golden pavilion, a silver couch (<s>paryaṅka</s>) was placed — spread with rugs (<s>paṭikā</s>), spread with fleeces (<s>goṇikā</s>), spread with cushions (<s>tūlikā</s>), spread with embroidered cloths (<s>citrikā</s>), spread with fine coverlets (<s>paṭalikā</s>), with a <s>Kāliṅga</s> (Kaliṅga) cloak as counter-spread, with an upper covering cloth, and with red pillows at both ends. 34.69 In the silver [pavilion], a golden [couch]; in the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [a couch] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; in the <s>sphaṭika</s> one, [a couch] made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — [each] couch was placed, spread with rugs, spread with fleeces, spread with cushions, spread with embroidered cloths, spread with fine coverlets, with a <s>Kāliṅga</s> cloak as counter-spread, with an upper covering cloth, and with red pillows at both ends.

body.text:
34.70 sauv(arṇas)y(a) kūṭāg(ā)r(as)y(a p)ura(s)t(ā)d r(ā)jatas tālo mā(pito 'bhūt sauvarṇena patreṇa puṣpeṇa phalena || rājatasya sauvarṇo vaiḍūryamayasya sphaṭikamayaḥ || sphaṭikamayasya) vaiḍūryamayaḥ sphaṭikamayena patreṇa puṣpe(ṇa phalena ||)
34.71 (teṣāṃ khalu tālānāṃ vāyunā preritānām ayam evaṃrūpo manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati yathā pañcāṅgikasya) tūryasya kuśalena puruṣeṇa (samyaksupravāditasya ||)
34.72 (dhārmaḥ prāsādaḥ kanakavālikāstṛto 'bhūc candanavāripariṣikto hemajālāvatata)s suvarṇakaṅkaṇikāvṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.70 In front of the golden pavilion, a silver palm tree (<s>tāla</s>) was constructed, with golden leaves, flowers, and fruit. In front of the silver one, a golden [palm]; of the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [a palm] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; of the <s>sphaṭika</s> one, [a palm] made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, with <s>sphaṭika</s> leaves, flowers, and fruit. 34.71 When those palm trees were stirred by the wind, such a delightful sound issued forth — like that of a five-part musical ensemble skillfully and well played by an expert man. 34.72 The <s>Dharma</s> Palace was strewn with golden sand, sprinkled with sandalwood water, hung with golden nets, and covered with golden bells.

body.text: <Hier im Tib. Uddāna>
body.translated_text: [Here in the Tibetan: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse)]

body.text: 34.73 atha caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi s(arvajātakṛtaniṣṭhitaṃ dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ viditvā dhārmasya prāsādasya purastād dhārmīṃ puṣkariṇīṃ māpayanti yojanam āyā)mena yojanaṃ vistāreṇa ||
body.translated_text: 34.73 Then the eighty-four thousand fortress-kings, knowing the <s>Dharma</s> Palace to be fully completed in every respect, constructed in front of the <s>Dharma</s> Palace the <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool (<s>dhārmī puṣkariṇī</s>) — one <s>yojana</s> in length, one <s>yojana</s> in breadth.

body.text:
34.74 dhārmī puṣkariṇī caturvi(dhābhir iṣṭikābhiś citā babhūva sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ ||)
34.75 (tasyāṃ khalu puṣkariṇ)y(āṃ) caturvidhāni sopānāni māpitāny abhūv(an) s(auvarṇāni rājatāni vaiḍūryamayāṇi sphaṭikamayāni ||)
34.76 (sā khalu puṣkariṇī caturvidhābhiḥ vedikābhiḥ parikṣiptā ba)bhūva sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sph(aṭikamayībhiḥ || sauvarṇyā vedikāyā rājataṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt || rājatyāḥ sauvarṇaṃ vai)ḍūryamayyāḥ sphaṭikamayaṃ sphaṭi(kamayyā vaiḍūryamayaṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt ||)
34.77 (tasyāṃ khalu puṣkariṇyāṃ vividhāni ja)lajāni mālyāni ropitāny (abhūvan tadyathotpalaṃ padmaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ saugandhikaṃ madhugandhikaṃ sarvartukaṃ sarvakālikam anāvṛtaṃ sa)rvajanasya ||
body.translated_text: 34.74 The <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool was lined with four types of bricks: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. 34.75 In that pool, four types of staircases were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. 34.76 That pool was enclosed by four types of railings: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. On the golden railing, a silver needle-pendant base was constructed; on the silver [railing], a golden one; on the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [a base] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; on the <s>sphaṭika</s> one, [a base] made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — [such] needle-pendant bases were constructed. 34.77 In that pool, various aquatic flowers were planted — namely, <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (white water-lilies), <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses), <s>saugandhibkas</s> (fragrant lotuses), [and] <s>madhugandhibkas</s> (honey-scented lotuses) — blooming in all seasons, at all times, open to all people.

body.text:
34.78 tasyāḥ khalu puṣkariṇyās tīre (vividhāni sthalajāni mālyāni ropitāny abhūvan tadyathātimuktakaś caṃpakaḥ pāṭalā vārṣikā mālikā navamā)likā s(u)manā y(ū)thikā dhānuṣkārī sarv(artukaṃ sarvakālikam anāvṛtaṃ sarvajanasya ||)
34.79 (dhārmī puṣkariṇī kanakavālikāstṛtābhūc candanavāripariṣi)ktā he(majālāvatat)ā suvarṇakaṅkaṇikāvṛtā ||
body.translated_text: 34.78 On the banks of that pool, various land-growing flowers were planted — namely, <s>atimuktaka</s> (jasmine), <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s> (trumpet-flower), <s>vārṣikā</s> (rain-lily), <s>mālikā</s> (garland-flower), <s>navamālikā</s> (new garland-flower), <s>sumanā</s> (great-flowered jasmine), <s>yūthikā</s> (wild jasmine), [and] <s>dhānuṣkārī</s> (bow-flower) — blooming in all seasons, at all times, open to all people. 34.79 The <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool was strewn with golden sand, sprinkled with sandalwood water, hung with golden nets, and covered with golden bells.

body.text: 34.80 atha caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi sarvaj(ā)ta(k)ṛtan(i)ṣṭh(i)t(aṃ) dh(ār)m(aṃ prā)s(ādaṃ) dh(ār)m(ī)ñ c(a) pu(ṣ)k(a)r(iṇīṃ viditvā dhārmyāḥ) puṣkari(ṇyāḥ purastād dhā)rmaṃ tālavanaṃ māpayanti yojanam āyāmena yojanaṃ vistāreṇa ||
body.translated_text: 34.80 Then the eighty-four thousand fortress-kings, knowing the <s>Dharma</s> Palace and the <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool to be fully completed in every respect, constructed in front of the <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool the <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove (<s>dhārmaṃ tālavanaṃ</s>) — one <s>yojana</s> in length, one <s>yojana</s> in breadth.

body.text: 34.81 dhārme tālavane caturvidhās tālā māpitā abhūvan sauvarṇā rājatā v(ai)ḍūryamayāḥ spha(ṭi)kamay(ā)ḥ || sauvarṇasya tālasya rājataṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ māpitam abhūt || rājatasya sauvarṇam || vaiḍūryamayasya sphaṭikamayam || sphaṭikamayasya vaiḍūryamayaṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ māpitam abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 34.81 In the <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove, four types of palm trees (<s>tāla</s>) were constructed: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>. The golden palm tree had silver leaves, flowers, and fruit constructed for it; the silver one, golden [leaves, flowers, and fruit]; the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [those] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; the <s>sphaṭika</s> one had <s>vaiḍūrya</s> leaves, flowers, and fruit constructed for it.

body.text: 34.82 teṣāṃ khalu tālānāṃ vāyunā preritānām ayam evaṃrūpo manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati tadyathā pañcāṅgikasya tūryasya kuśalena puruṣeṇa samyaksupravāditasya ||
body.translated_text: 34.82 When those palm trees were stirred by the wind, such a delightful sound issued forth — like that of a five-part musical ensemble skillfully and well played by an expert man.

body.text: 34.83 dhārmaṃ tālavanaṃ caturvidhābhir vedikābhiḥ parikṣiptam abhūt sauvarṇībhī rājatībhir vaiḍūryamayībhiḥ sphaṭikamayībhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.83 The <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove was enclosed by four types of railings: golden, silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, [and] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>.

body.text: 34.84 sauva(r)ṇ(y)ā vedikāyā rājataṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt || rājatyāḥ sauvarṇaṃ vaiḍūryamayyāḥ sphaṭikamayaṃ sphaṭikamayyā vaiḍūryamayaṃ sūcyālaṃbanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ māpitam abhūt ||
body.translated_text: 34.84 On the golden railing, a silver needle-pendant (<s>sūcyālaṃbana</s>) base was constructed. On the silver [railing], a golden one; on the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> one, [a base] made of <s>sphaṭika</s>; on the <s>sphaṭika</s> one, [a base] made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — [such] needle-pendant bases were constructed.

body.text: 34.85 dhārmaṃ tālavanaṃ kanakavālikāstṛtam abhūc candanavāripariṣiktaṃ hemajālāvatataṃ suvarṇakaṅkaṇikāvṛtam ||
body.translated_text: 34.85 The <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove was strewn with golden sand, sprinkled with sandalwood water, hung with golden nets, and covered with golden bells.

body.text: 34.86 atha caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhitaṃ dhārmaṃ prāsādaṃ dhārmīṃ puṣkariṇīṃ dhārmaṃ ca tālavanaṃ viditvā yena rājā mahāsudarśanas tenopajagmur upetya rājānaṃ mahāsudarśanam idam avocan ||
body.translated_text: 34.86 Then the eighty-four thousand fortress-kings, knowing the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, the <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool, and the <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove to be fully completed in every respect, approached King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> and, having approached, said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:

body.text: 34.87 sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhito devasya dhārmaḥ prāsādo dhārmī puṣkariṇī dhārmaṃ ca tālavanam || yasyedānīṃ d(e)v(aḥ) kālaṃ man(yat)e ||
body.translated_text: 34.87 'The <s>Dharma</s> Palace, the <s>Dharma</s> Lotus Pool, and the <s>Dharma</s> Palm Grove are fully completed in every respect for the Lord (<s>Deva</s>). Now let the Lord determine the [appropriate] time.'

body.text: 34.88 atha rājño mahāsudarśanasyaitad abhavat ||
body.translated_text: 34.88 Then this thought arose in King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:

body.text: 34.89 na mama pra(ti)rūpaṃ syād yad aham evam eva dhārme prāsāde adhyāvaseyam || yannv ahaṃ ye (madviji)te sādhu(rūpasaṃmatāḥ) śr(a)maṇabrāhmaṇāḥ prativasanti tān prathamatar(aṃ) dhārme prāsāde bhojayitvā pratyekapratyekaṃ duṣyayugenācchādayeyam ||
body.translated_text: 34.89 'It would not be fitting for me to simply take up residence in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace. Rather, let me first feed the <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of good repute who dwell in my realm in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, and then clothe each one with a pair of garments (<s>duṣyayuga</s>).'

body.text: 34.90 atha rājā mahāsud(arśa)no ye (svavijite sādhu)rūpasaṃmatāḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ prativasanti tān prathamataraṃ dhārme prāsāde bhojayitvā pratyekapratyekaṃ duṣyayugenācchādaya(t)i ||
body.translated_text: 34.90 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> first fed the <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of good repute who dwelt in his realm in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, and clothed each one with a pair of garments.

body.text:
34.91 atha rājño mahāsu(darśa)n(a)sy(aita)d (a)bh(avat ||)
34.92 n(a) m(a)ma pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ dhārme prāsāde pañca(kāmaguṇair sama)rpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtaḥ krīḍeyaṃ rameyaṃ paricārayeyaṃ || yannv ah(aṃ) dhārme prāsāda ekena puruṣeṇopasthāyakena rājarṣir brahmacary(aṃ careyam ||)
34.93 (atha rā)jā mahāsudarśana ekena puruṣenopasthāyakena dhārme prāsāde rājarṣir brahmacaryam acārṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 34.91 Then this thought arose in King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>: 34.92 'It would not be fitting for me to amuse myself, enjoy myself, and take pleasure in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>pañcakāmaguṇa</s>). Rather, let me practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) as a royal sage (<s>rājarṣi</s>) in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace, with a single male attendant.' 34.93 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, with a single male attendant, practiced the holy life as a royal sage in the <s>Dharma</s> Palace.

body.text:
34.94 atha rājā mahāsudarśano dhārme prāsāde (p)r(aviśya s)auv(ar)ṇ(aṃ) kūṭ(ā)gāra(m a)dhiruhya rājate paryaṅke niṣadya viviktaṃ kāmaiḥ pūrvavad yāvat prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya vyahā(rṣīt ||)
34.95 sauvarṇāt kūṭāgā(rā)n niṣkramya rājataṃ (kūṭāgā)ram adhiru(hya) s(au)varṇe paryaṅke niṣadya viviktaṃ kāmai(ḥ) pūr(va)vad yāvat pr(atha)maṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya vyahārṣīt ||
body.translated_text:
34.94 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, having entered the <s>Dhārma</s> palace, ascended the golden <s>kūṭāgāra</s> (upper chamber), sat upon a silver couch, and secluded from sensual desires, as before up to attaining the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he dwelt in joy.
34.95 Coming forth from the golden <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, he ascended the silver <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, sat upon a golden couch, and secluded from sensual desires, as before up to attaining the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he dwelt in joy.

body.text: 34.96 rājatāt kū(ṭāgārān ni)ṣk(ra)mya vaiḍ(ūryamayaṃ kūṭāgāram adhiruhya sphaṭikama)ye paryaṅke niṣadya viviktaṃ kāmaiḥ p(ū)rvavad y(ā)vat pratha(ma)ṃ dhyānam upasaṃpad(ya vya)hārṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 34.96 Coming forth from the silver <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, he ascended the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, sat upon a crystal couch, and secluded from sensual desires, as before up to attaining the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he dwelt in joy.

body.text:
34.97 vaiḍūryamay(ā)t (kū)ṭā(gārān niṣkramya sphaṭikamayaṃ kūṭāgāram adhiruhya vaiḍūryamaye paryaṅke niṣadya viviktaṃ kāmaiḥ pūrvavad yāvat prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya vyahārṣīt ||)
34.98 (atha caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇi yena strīratnaṃ tenopajagmuḥ || upetya strīratnam idam avocan ||)
34.99 (devi prativedayasva || ciram asmābhir adṛṣṭo rājā yena vayaṃ rājānaṃ darśanāyātyutsukyāḥ || rājānaṃ vayaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ ||)
34.100 (āgamayadhvaṃ tāvad bhaginyo yāvad ahaṃ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ prakṣyāmi ||)
34.101 (atha strīratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ dūtenāhūyaivam āmantrayate || senāpate jānīhi || ciram asmābhir adṛṣṭo rājā yena vayaṃ rājānaṃ darśanāyātyutsukyāḥ || rājānaṃ vayaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ ||)
34.102-106 (tena hi yūyaṃ bhaginyaḥ sarvāḥ pītālaṅkāraṃ pītavastramālyābharaṇāni pītānulepanaṃ pītaparivāraṃ saṃpādayatha || yāvad ahaṃ caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi caturaśītināgasahasrāṇy upoṣathanāgarājapramukhāni caturaśītyaśvarājasahasrāṇi vālāhāśvapramukhāni caturaśītirathasahasrāṇi nandighoṣarathapramukhāni saṅgrahiṣyāmi ||)
34.107 (atha sarvās tāḥ striyaḥ pītālaṅkāraṃ pītavastramālyābharaṇāni pītānulepanaṃ pītaparivāraṃ samapādayan ||)
34.108-111 (pariṇāyakaratnaṃ ca caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi caturaśītināgasahasrāṇy upoṣathanāgarājapramukhāni caturaśītyaśvarājasahasrāni vālāhāśvapramukhāni caturaśītirathasahasrāṇi nandighoṣarathapramukhāni samagrahīt ||)
34.112 (saṅgṛhya strīratnaṃ nandighoṣarathe nyaṣīdat || anyā avaśeṣastriyaḥ svakasvakarathaṃ niṣadya yena dhārmaḥ prāsādas tenopajagmuḥ ||)
34.113 (tena khalu samayena dhārmasya prāsādasyādhastād mahājanakāyasyoccaśabdamahāśabdo nāditaḥ ||)
34.114 (aśrau)ṣ(ī)d rājā mahāsudarśano dh(ārmasya prāsādasyādhastād mahājanakāyasyoccaśabdamahāśabdam || śrutvā cānyatamam antevāsinaṃ puruṣam evam āmantrayate ||)
34.115 k(i)m etad bhoḥ p(u)ruṣa dhārmasya prās(ā)dasyā(dhastād mahājanakāyasyoccaśabdamahāśabdaḥ ||)
34.116-120 (imāni deva caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇi strīratnapramukhāni caturaśītikoṭṭarājasaha)srāṇi pariṇāyakaratnapramukhāni cat(uraśītināgasahasrāṇy upoṣathanāgarājapramukhāni pūrvavat ||)
34.121 (tena bhoḥ puruṣa dhārmasya prāsādasyādhastād sauvarṇaṃ bha)dr(ā)sanaṃ prajñ(ā)paya yatrāhaṃ niṣadya mahāja(nakāyaṃ nirīkṣeya ||)
34.122 (evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājño mahāsudarśanasya pratiśrutya dhārmasya prāsādasyādhastāt sauvarṇaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ prajñapya yena r)ājā mahāsudarśanas tenopajagāma || upetya rājā(naṃ mahāsudarśanam idam avocat ||)
34.123 (prajñaptaṃ deva dhārmasya prāsādasyādhastāt sau)varṇaṃ bhadrāsanam || yasyedānīṃ devaḥ k(ālaṃ) manyate ||
body.translated_text:
34.97 Coming forth from the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, he ascended the crystal <s>kūṭāgāra</s>, sat upon a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> couch, and secluded from sensual desires, as before up to attaining the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he dwelt in joy.
34.98 Then eighty-four thousand women approached the <s>strīratna</s> (queen-jewel). Having approached, they said this to the <s>strīratna</s>:
34.99 "O Queen, please inform him. It has been long since we have seen the King. We are eager to see him. We wish to behold the King."
34.100 "Wait, sisters, while I ask the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s> (general-jewel)."
34.101 Then the <s>strīratna</s>, having summoned the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s> through a messenger, addressed him thus: "O General, know this — it has been long since we have seen the King. We are eager to see him. We wish to behold the King."
34.102-106 "Then, sisters, all of you prepare yellow ornaments, yellow garments, garlands, jewelry, yellow ointments, and a yellow retinue. Meanwhile I shall assemble eighty-four thousand vassal kings headed by the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>, eighty-four thousand elephants headed by the elephant-king <s>Upoṣatha</s>, eighty-four thousand horse-kings headed by the horse-king <s>Vālāha</s>, and eighty-four thousand chariots headed by the chariot <s>Nandighoṣa</s>."
34.107 Then all those women prepared yellow ornaments, yellow garments, garlands, jewelry, yellow ointments, and a yellow retinue.
34.108-111 And the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s> assembled eighty-four thousand vassal kings, eighty-four thousand elephants headed by the elephant-king <s>Upoṣatha</s>, eighty-four thousand horse-kings headed by the horse-king <s>Vālāha</s>, and eighty-four thousand chariots headed by the chariot <s>Nandighoṣa</s>.
34.112 Having assembled them, the <s>strīratna</s> seated herself upon the <s>Nandighoṣa</s> chariot. The remaining women, each mounting their own chariot, approached the <s>Dhārma</s> palace.
34.113 At that time, beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace, a great uproar of loud and mighty sound arose from the great multitude.
34.114 King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> heard the loud and mighty sound of the great multitude beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace. Having heard it, he addressed a certain attendant man thus:
34.115 "What is this, good man — this loud and mighty sound of the great multitude beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace?"
34.116-120 "These, Your Majesty, are eighty-four thousand women headed by the <s>strīratna</s>, eighty-four thousand vassal kings headed by the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>, eighty-four thousand elephants headed by the elephant-king <s>Upoṣatha</s>, as before."
34.121 "Then, good man, set out a golden throne beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace, where I may sit and look upon the great multitude."
34.122 "Yes, Your Majesty." That man, having assented to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, set out a golden throne beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace and approached King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>. Having approached, he said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:
34.123 "Your Majesty, a golden throne has been set out beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace. May Your Majesty come when he sees fit."

body.text:
34.124 adrākṣīd rājā mahāsudarśano dhārmaprāsādādhastāt sarvās tāḥ stri(yaḥ pītavastramālyābhāraṇāḥ pītā)nulepanā(ḥ ||)
34.125 dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyaitad abhavat || atirañjanīyo bata mātṛgrāma (i)ti viditvendriyāṇy utkṣ(i)pati ||
body.translated_text:
34.124 King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> saw beneath the <s>Dhārma</s> palace all those women wearing yellow garments, garlands, and jewelry, anointed with yellow ointments.
34.125 And having seen them, this thought occurred to him: "How exceedingly alluring is womankind!" Knowing this, he withdrew his senses.

body.text: 34.126 adrākṣīt strī(ratnaṃ rājānaṃ mahāsu)d(a)rśanam ind(r)iyāṇy utkṣipantam || dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyā etad abhavat ||
body.translated_text: 34.126 The <s>strīratna</s> saw King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> withdrawing his senses. And having seen this, the following thought occurred to her:

body.text:
34.127 yathā khalu de(vo 'smān dṛṣṭv)endriyāṇy utkṣi(pa)ti mā haiva devo 'smābhi(ḥ saṅgamyāpakāraṃ kariṣyati ||)
34.128 (atha) rājā mahāsudarśano dhārmāt prāsādād avatīrya sauvarṇe (prajñaptabhadrāsane nyaṣīdat ||)
34.129 atha strīratn(aṃ) y(e)na rājā mahā(s)ud(arśanas tenopajagāma || upetya rājānaṃ) mahāsudarśanam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text:
34.127 "Since Your Majesty, upon seeing us, withdraws his senses, may it not be that Your Majesty, by associating with us, will come to harm."
34.128 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, having descended from the <s>Dhārma</s> palace, sat upon the golden throne that had been prepared.
34.129 Then the <s>strīratna</s> approached King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>. Having approached, she said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:

body.text:
34.130 imāni devasya caturaśītistrī(sahasrāṇi ||) atra devaś chandaṃ janayatv ave(kṣāṃ devaḥ karotu jīvite ||)
34.131 caturaśītikoṭṭarājasahasrāṇi pariṇāya(ka)ratnapramukhā(ni || atra devaś chandaṃ janayatv avekṣāṃ devaḥ karotu jīvite ||)
34.132 (caturaśītināgasahasrā)ṇy upoṣathanāgarājapramukhāni || atra devaś chandaṃ janayatv avekṣāṃ (devaḥ karotu jīvite ||)
34.133 (caturaśītyaśvasahasrāṇi vālāhāśva)rājapramukhāni || atra de(vaś cha)ndaṃ janayatv avekṣāṃ devaḥ karotu jīvite ||
body.translated_text:
34.130 "These are Your Majesty's eighty-four thousand women. May Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life.
34.131 Eighty-four thousand vassal kings headed by the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s> — may Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life.
34.132 Eighty-four thousand elephants headed by the elephant-king <s>Upoṣatha</s> — may Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life.
34.133 Eighty-four thousand horse-kings headed by the horse-king <s>Vālāha</s> — may Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life."

body.text:
34.134 (caturaśītirathasahasrāṇi nandighoṣa)rathapramukhāni || atra devaś chandaṃ janayatv avekṣāṃ devaḥ karotu jīvite ||()
34.135 caturaśītinagarasah(asrāṇi kuśāvatīrājadhānīpramukhāni || atra devaś chandaṃ janayatv ave)kṣāṃ devaḥ karotu jīvite ||
body.translated_text:
34.134 "Eighty-four thousand chariots headed by the chariot <s>Nandighoṣa</s> — may Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life.
34.135 Eighty-four thousand cities headed by the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s> — may Your Majesty generate desire for them; may Your Majesty have regard for life."

body.text:
34.136 pūrve ca tvaṃ bhagini māṃ mitravat samudācarasi sā t(v)aṃ tarhi sa(patnavat ||)
34.137 (atha strīratnaṃ bhaginīvādena rājñā mahāsudarśanena sam)udācī(r)ṇa(ṃ) pr(ā)r(o)dīd aśrūṇi va(r)t(a)yamānam ||
body.translated_text:
34.136 "Formerly, sister, you addressed me as a friend, but now you speak as a rival wife."
34.137 Then the <s>strīratna</s>, having been addressed as 'sister' by King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, wept, shedding tears.

body.text:
34.138 atha strīratnaṃ cīvarakarṇakenāśrūṇy utstīrya rājānaṃ mahāsudarśanam idam (avocat ||)
34.139 (kathaṃ tarhi vayaṃ devaṃ mi)travat samudācarāmo na sapatnavat ||
body.translated_text:
34.138 Then the <s>strīratna</s>, wiping her tears with the corner of her robe, said this to King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>:
34.139 "How then should we address Your Majesty as a friend and not as a rival wife?"

body.text: 34.140 ehi tvaṃ bhagini || evaṃ vada ||
body.translated_text: 34.140 "Come, sister. Speak thus:"

body.text: 34.141 alpaṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām || gamanīyaḥ sāṃparāyaḥ || kartavyaṃ kuśalam || cari(tavyaṃ brahmacaryam || na prā)ptajātasyāmaraṇam || so 'pi deva kṣaṇo la(vo) muhūrto na prajñāyate yatrā(sya kāyasya) sarveṇa sarvaṃ nikṣepo bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 34.141 "Short is the life of human beings. One must go to the hereafter. One must perform wholesome deeds. One must lead the holy life. For one who is born, there is no escape from death. And that moment, that instant, that brief time is not known, O Lord, when this body will be entirely cast aside."

body.text: 34.142 yad devasya caturaśīti(ṣu) s(trīsahasreṣu strīratnapramukheṣu cchando vā janito rāgo vā janita iṣṭakāntamanāpatvaṃ vā janitaṃ tad) devaḥ prajahātu niravekṣo devo bhavatu jīvite ||
body.translated_text: 34.142 "Whatever desire Your Majesty has generated, whatever passion has arisen, whatever fond attachment has been produced toward the eighty-four thousand women headed by the <s>strīratna</s> — may Your Majesty abandon that. May Your Majesty be without regard for life."

body.text: 34.143 yad devas(ya caturaśītiṣu koṭṭarājasahasreṣu pariṇāyakaratnapramukheṣu cchando vā pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo) devo bhavatu jīvite ||
body.translated_text: 34.143 "Whatever desire Your Majesty has generated toward the eighty-four thousand vassal kings headed by the <s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>, as before up to — may Your Majesty be without regard for life."

body.text:
34.144 yad devasya caturaśītiṣu nāgasahasreṣv (upoṣathanāgarājapramukheṣu cchando vā pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo devo bhavatu) jī(vite ||)
34.145 (yad devasya catu)raśītiṣv aśvasahasreṣu vālāhāśvarāja(pramukheṣu cchando vā pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo devo bhavatu jīvite ||)
34.146 (ya)d d(e)vasya catur(aśītiṣu rathasaha)sr(e)ṣu nandighoṣarathapramukheṣu cchando vā (pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo devo bhavatu jīvite ||)
34.147 (yad devasya caturaśītiṣu) nagarasahasre(ṣu kuśāvatīrāja)dhānīpramukheṣu cchando vā pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo devo bha(vatu jīvite ||)
34.148 (tā idam avocan || tathā hi vayaṃ samudācarāmo devaṃ mitrava)t ||
body.translated_text:
34.144 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand elephants, headed by <s>Upoṣatha</s>, the king of elephants — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.145 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand horses, headed by <s>Vālāha</s>, the king of horses — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.146 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand chariots, headed by the chariot named <s>Nandighoṣa</s> — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.147 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand cities, headed by the royal capital <s>Kuśāvatī</s> — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.148 'They spoke thus: "For we address the Lord as a friend."'

body.text:
34.149 alpaṃ deva jīvi(taṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ) gamanīyaḥ sāṃparāyaḥ kartavyaṃ ku(śalaṃ cari)tavyaṃ bra(hmacaryam || na prāptajātasyāmaraṇam || so 'pi deva kṣaṇo lavo muhūrto na prajñā)yate yatrāsya kā(yasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ nikṣepo bhaviṣyati ||)
34.150 (yad devasya caturaśītiṣu strīsahasreṣu strīratnapramukheṣu cchando vā janito rāgo vā janita iṣṭakāntamanāpatvaṃ vā janitaṃ tad devaḥ prajahātu niravekṣo devo bhavatu jīvite ||)
34.151 (yad devasya caturaśītiṣu koṭṭarājasahasreṣu pariṇāyakaratnapramukheṣu cchando vā pūrvavad yāvan niravekṣo devo bhavatu jīvite ||)
34.152 (yad devasya caturaśītiṣu nāgasahasreṣv upoṣathanāgarājapramukheṣu cchando vā) pū(rvavat) ||
body.translated_text:
34.149 'Short, O Lord, is the life of human beings; the future life must be journeyed to. Wholesome deeds must be done; the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) must be practiced. For one who is born, there is no escaping death. And that moment, that instant, that second cannot be discerned when there will be a complete laying down of this body.'
34.150 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand women, headed by the woman-treasure (<s>strīratna</s>), or if passion has arisen, or if longing for what is dear, pleasant, and agreeable has arisen — let the Lord relinquish that. Let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.151 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand vassal kings, headed by the counselor-treasure (<s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>) — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.152 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand elephants, headed by <s>Upoṣatha</s>, the king of elephants — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before.'

body.text: 34.153 (yad dev)asya catu(raśīti)ṣv (a)śvasahasr(e)ṣu cchand(o) vā pū(r)vava(t) ||
body.translated_text: 34.153 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand horses — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before.'

body.text:
34.154 (yad deva)sya caturaś(ī)t(i)ṣu (rathasahasreṣu cchando vā pūrvavat ||)
34.155 (yad) devasya caturaś(ītiṣ)u (nagarasaha)sre(ṣu ccha)nd(o) vā pūrvavad yāva(n) niravekṣo devo bhavatu (jīvite ||)
34.156 atha rājā mahāsu(darśanaḥ strīratnam anenāvavādenānuśāsya dhārmaṃ prā)sādam adhiruhya sauva(r)ṇaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ pr(avi)śya rājate paryaṅke niṣadya maitrāsahagatena cittenāvaireṇāsapa(tnenāvyāvadhyena vipulena mahadgatenāpramāṇenādvaye)na subhāvite(naikāṃ diśa)m adhimucya spharitvopasaṃpadya vyahārṣīt ||
body.translated_text:
34.154 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand chariots — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before.'
34.155 'If the Lord has desire for his eighty-four thousand cities — [let the Lord relinquish that desire], as before, up to '...let the Lord be without attachment to life.'
34.156 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, having instructed and admonished the woman-treasure (<s>strīratna</s>) with this exhortation, ascended the <s>Dharma</s>-palace, entered the golden upper chamber, sat down upon the silver couch, and having suffused one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) — free from enmity, free from rivalry, free from malice, vast, great, immeasurable, without duality, well-cultivated — he pervaded it and dwelt therein with satisfaction.

body.text: 34.157 tathā dvitīyāṃ tathā tṛtīyāṃ (tathā caturthīm ity ūrdhvam adhas tiryak sarvaśaḥ sarvā)vant(am imaṃ) lokaṃ maitrāsaha(ga)tena c(i)ttenāvaireṇāsapatnenāvyāvadhyena vipulena mahadgatenāpra(māṇenādvayena subhāvitenaikāṃ diśam adhimucya sphari)tvopasaṃ(pad)ya (v)yahārṣīt ||
body.translated_text: 34.157 Likewise the second [direction], likewise the third, likewise the fourth — upward, downward, across, in every way, the entire world he suffused with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) — free from enmity, free from rivalry, free from malice, vast, great, immeasurable, without duality, well-cultivated — having pervaded one direction, he dwelt therein with satisfaction.

body.text:
34.158 sauvarṇāt kūṭāgārān n(i)ṣkramya rājataṃ kūṭāgāraṃ praviśya sauvarṇaparyaṅke niṣadya karuṇāsaha(gatena cittenāvaireṇa pūrvavat ||)
34.159 <Im Tib. Wiederholung von 157>
34.160 (atha) rājatāt kūṭāgārān niṣkramya vaiḍūryamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ praviśya sphaṭikamayaparyaṅke niṣadya muditāsahagatena cittenāvai(reṇa pūrvavat ||)
34.161 <Im Tib. Wiederholung von 157>
34.162 (atha vaiḍūryamayāt kūṭāgārān niṣkramya sphaṭika)mayaṃ kūṭāgār(aṃ pra)viśya vaiḍūryamaye paryaṅke ni(ṣadyope)kṣāsahagatena cittenāvaireṇa pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text:
34.158 Emerging from the golden upper chamber, he entered the silver upper chamber, sat down upon the golden couch, and [suffused all directions] with a mind accompanied by compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) — free from enmity, as before.
34.159 [In the Tibetan: repetition of 157.]
34.160 Then emerging from the silver upper chamber, he entered the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) upper chamber, sat down upon the crystal couch, and [suffused all directions] with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) — free from enmity, as before.
34.161 [In the Tibetan: repetition of 157.]
34.162 Then emerging from the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> upper chamber, he entered the crystal upper chamber, sat down upon the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> couch, and [suffused all directions] with a mind accompanied by equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — free from enmity, as before.

body.text:
34.163 <Im Tib. Wiederholung von 157>
34.164 a(tha rājā mahāsudarśanaś caturo brahmavihārān bhāvayi)tv(ā) k(āmeṣu kāma)cchand(aṃ) pr(a)h(āya) tadbahul(avihārī bra)hmal(o)kasya svabhāvatāy(ā)m upagataḥ ||
body.translated_text:
34.163 [In the Tibetan: repetition of 157.]
34.164 Then King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, having cultivated the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) and having abandoned desire for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), dwelling abundantly in those states, attained the natural condition of the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (Brahmā-world).

body.text: 34.165 rajñ(a ānanda mahāsudarśanasya paści)mā māra(ṇān)t(i)kā vedanā babhūva tadyathā balavataḥ puru(ṣa)sya (subho)jana(ṃ) bhuktavato muhūrte syād bhaktaklamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 34.165 For King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, the final death-sensation arose — just as for a strong man who has eaten a good meal, there would be a momentary heaviness from the food.

body.text:
34.166 syāt khalu te (ānandānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena) samayena rājābhūn mahāsudarśano nāma || na khalv evaṃ draṣṭav(ya)m || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || aham eva sa tena kālena tena samayena r(ā)jā (mahāsudarśano 'bhūvam ||)
34.167 (ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ khalv ā)nanda kuśi(na)garī yāvan nad(ī hira)ṇyavatī yāvad yamakaśālavanaṃ yāvan mallānā(ṃ) makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam atrā(ntarā dvādaśa yojanāni sāmantakena bhūyo 'pi tathāgata)sya (śa)rīranikṣe(p)o (babhū)va tac ca r(ā)jñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya || idaṃ saptamaṃ vāram ||
body.translated_text:
34.166 'Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, you might think that at that time, on that occasion, it was someone else who was the king named <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>. But this should not be seen thus. For what reason? It was I myself who at that time, on that occasion, was King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>.'
34.167 'Six times, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the area extending from <s>Kuśinagarī</s> to the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, to the <s>Yamakaśāla</s> grove, to the <s>Mallās</s>' <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine — within that area of twelve <s>yojanas</s> in circumference — there was a laying down of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, and that of a king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head. This is the seventh time.'

body.text:
34.168 tac c(ānandārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya nāhaṃ taṃ loke) pṛthivīpradeśaṃ samanupaśyāmi (naiva) pūrvasyān diśi dakṣiṇasyāṃ paścimasyām uttarasyāṃ diśi yatra tathāga(tasyāṣṭamaḥ śarīranikṣepaḥ ||)
34.169 (tat kasmād dhetoḥ ||)
  + + + + + + + +
  (sam)ucchi(nnā) bhava(ne)t(r)ī ||
body.translated_text:
34.168 'And that, <s>Ānanda</s>, of the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One — I do not perceive in the world any spot of earth, neither in the eastern direction, nor in the southern, nor in the western, nor in the northern direction, where there would be an eighth laying down of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body.'
34.169 'For what reason?'
[Verse:] '...the cord of existence is cut off;'

body.text:
(v)i(kṣ)ī(ṇo) j(ātisaṃ)sā(ro
  nā)s(t)īdānīṃ punarbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text:
'The cycle of birth (<s>jātisaṃsāra</s>) is exhausted;
there is now no further rebirth.'

body.text:
35.1 tena khalu sama(y)e(nā)yuṣmān upamāno bhaga(vataḥ purastāt sthito 'bhūd bhagavantaṃ vījayan ||)
35.2 (atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam upamānam āmantrayate || bhi)k(ṣ)o mā m(e) purastāt tiṣṭha ||
body.translated_text:
35.1 At that time, the venerable <s>Upamāna</s> was standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, fanning him.
35.2 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Upamāna</s>: 'Monk, do not stand before me.'

body.text: 35.3 athāyuṣmān (ānando bhaga)vantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 35.3 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
35.4 (viṃśatiṃ varṣāṇi samadhikāni bhadanta mayā bhagavān upasthitaḥ || nāśrauṣaṃ pūrve evaṃvidhāṃ paruṣāṃ vācaṃ yathāyuṣmata upamānasyāvasāde ||)
35.5 (tathā hy anekakalpaśatāyuṣo devatā avadhyāyanti kṣipanti vivācayanti ||)
35.6 (kadācit karhicit tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loka utpadyante tadyathoduṃbare puṣpam ||)
35.7 (tasya cādya bhagavato rātryā madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parnirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati || ayaṃ ca mahāśakyamahāśakyo bhikṣur bhagavataḥ purastāt sthito 'smābhiḥ pṛṣṭhena dṛṣṭaḥ || tena na śaknumo bhagavato darśanāya pūjādhikārikāyai samupakramitum ||)
35.8 (kiyata bhadanta bhagavān devatāḥ sañjānāti ||)
35.9 (yāvad ānanda kuśinagarī yāvan nadī hiraṇyavatī yāvad yamakaśālavanaṃ yāvan mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam atrāntarā dvādaśa yojanāni sāmantakena nāsti kiñcin mahāśakyamahāśakyābhir devatābhir asphuṭaṃ spharaṇīyam antato daṇḍakoṭiviṣṭaṃbhanamātram api ||)
body.translated_text:
35.4 'For more than twenty years, Venerable Sir, I have served the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Never before have I heard such a harsh word as [the one spoken] in dismissal of the venerable <s>Upamāna</s>.'
35.5 'For deities of many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> in lifespan are lamenting, reproaching, and complaining.'
35.6 'Only rarely, at long intervals, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones arise in the world — like the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> tree.'
35.7 'And today, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of clinging. And this great <s>Śākya</s> monk is standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and we have been seen from behind by him. Therefore we are unable to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience and to undertake the worship that is our right.'
35.8 'To what extent, Venerable Sir, does the <s>Bhagavān</s> perceive the deities?'
35.9 'As far as, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Kuśinagarī</s> [extends], as far as the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, as far as the <s>Yamakaśāla</s> grove, as far as the <s>Mallās</s>' <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine — within that area of twelve <s>yojanas</s> in circumference — there is not a spot left uncovered by the great and mighty deities, even so much as the space pierced by the tip of a needle.'

body.text:
36.1 (athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
36.2 (kathaṃ vayaṃ bhadanta parinirvṛte bhagavati bhagavataḥ śarīrapūjāyām autsukyam āpadyemahi ||)
36.3 (alpotsukas tvam ānanda bhava śarīrapūjāyāḥ || prasannā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya etad āpādayiṣyanti ||)
36.4 (kathaṃ bhadanta brāhmaṇagṛhapataya etad āpādayiṣyanti ||)
36.5 (tadyāthānanda rājñaś cakravartino yathā ||)
36.6 (kathaṃ) bhadanta rājñaś cakravartina(ḥ ||)
36.7 (rājñaś cakravartinaḥ kāyo vihataiḥ karpāsair veṣṭyate || vihataiḥ karpāsair veṣṭayitvā pañcabhir yugaśatair veṣṭyate || pañcabhir yugaśa)t(ai)r veṣṭayitvā tailapūrṇāyā(m ayodroṇyāṃ prakṣipyānyayāyodroṇyā pracchādya gandhakāṣṭhaiś citāṃ citvā dhyāpyate govatā kṣīreṇa nirvāpyate ||) tāny asthīni sauvarṇe kumbhe pra(kṣipya sauvarṇyāṃ śivikāyām āropya caturmahāpathe śarīrastūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpyate cchatradhvajapatākā āropyante mahaś ca) pr(a)sthāpyate gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpai(r dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkriyate gurukriyate mānyate pūjyate ||)
36.8 (evam evānanda rājñaś cakravartinaḥ || ata uttare tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya ||)
body.translated_text:
36.1 Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Bhagavān:
36.2 'How, Venerable Sir, should we, after the Bhagavān has passed into parinirvāṇa, engage in the worship of the Bhagavān's bodily remains?'
36.3 'Be of little concern, Ānanda ...'

body.translated_text: 36b (ST.III) [Manuscript fragments, largely illegible:] '... the Bhagavān at Kuśinagarī dwelling ... after my parinirvāṇa ... [lacuna] ... lordship ...' [Remainder lost.]

body.text: 37.1 gacchānanda kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānām ārocaya ||
body.translated_text: 37.1 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>:'

body.text: 37.2 adya vo vāsiṣṭhāḥ śāstū (rātryā madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nir)vāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 37.2 'Today, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, in the middle watch of the night, the Teacher will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of clinging.'

body.text: 37.3 yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat k(u)rudhvaṃ mā vaḥ paścād vipratisāro bhaviṣyati k(a)th(a)m (idānīm asmākaṃ grāmakṣetre śāstā parinirvṛto yasya vayaṃ darśanāya pūjādhikārikāyai nopasaṃ)krāntāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 37.3 'Whatever duty or obligation you have, do it now. Let there be no regret for you afterwards, [thinking:] "How is it that the Teacher has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of our village, and we did not have the opportunity to see him and pay worship ..."'

body.text: 37.4 e(vaṃ bha)dantety āyu(ṣmān ānando bhagavato pratiśrutya saṃghāṭim ādāyānyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānāṃ saṃsthāgāras tenopa)jagāma ||
body.translated_text: 37.4 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking his outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>), with another monk as his attendant following behind, approached the assembly hall of the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>.

body.text:
37.5 (tena) khalu sama(yena kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃsthāgāre sanniṣaṇṇāḥ sannipatitā yadbhūyasā tenaiva karaṇīyena ||)
37.6 (athāyuṣmā)n ānand(aḥ kauśi)nāgar(ān mallān idam avocat ||)
37.7 (śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā va pariṣado vā || adya vo vāsiṣṭhāḥ śāstū rātryā madhyame yāme 'nu)padhiśeṣe (nirvā)ṇadhātau pari(nirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||)
37.8 (yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kurudhvaṃ mā vaḥ paścād vipratisāro bhaviṣyati katham idānīm asmākaṃ grāmakṣetre śāstā parinirvṛto yasya vayaṃ darśanāya pūjādhikārikāyai na samupakrāntāḥ ||)
body.translated_text:
37.5 At that time, the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> were seated and assembled in the assembly hall, mostly for that very business.
37.6 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>:

body.text:
38.1 (evam iti kauśināgarā mallā āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ pratiśrutya saputradārāḥ sadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyāḥ samitrāmātyajñātisālohitāḥ) ku(śinagaryā niṣkramya yena yamakaśālavanaṃ tenopajagmuḥ || upetya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdan ||)
38.2 (ekāntaniṣaṇṇān) kauśināgarān mallān (bhagavān dhārmyā kathayā sandarśayati samādapayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati ||)
38.3 (atha kauśināgarā mallā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsa)m (u)ttar(āsa)ṅg(aṃ) kṛtvā (yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocan ||)
38.4 (ete vayaṃ bhadanta kauśināgarā mallā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmo dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca ||) ady(āgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ śikṣāpadāni pratigrahīṣyāmaḥ ||)
38.5 (athāyuṣmata ānandasyaitad abhavat ||)
38.6 (saced ahaṃ kauśināgarān mallān ekaikaṃ bhagavato 'ntike upāsakaśikṣāpadāni pratigrāhayiṣyāmy ardharātry agṛhītaśikṣāpadā prasariṣyati || yannv ahaṃ kauśināgarān mallān bhagavato 'ntika upāsakaśikṣāpadāni yugapat pratigrāhayeyam || evaṃnāmā kauśināgaro mallaḥ saputradāraḥ sadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣe)yaḥ sa(mi)trāmātyajñātisālohito buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati dharmaṃ saṃghañ (ca ||)
38.7 (athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||)
38.8 (evaṃnāmā bhadanta kauśināgaro mallaḥ saputradāraḥ) sadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaḥ sa(mi)trāmātyajñātisālo(hito buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca || śikṣāpadāni pratigrahītum icchati || evam) eva rātryāḥ prathamo yāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 38.1 'So be it,' the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, having assented to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, together with their sons, wives, female and male servants, workers, and attendants, together with their friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen, departing from <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, [went] to the <s>Yamakaśāla</s> grove ...

body.text:
atha ca punar āyuṣm(ān ānando 'natikrānte madhyame yāme tāṃs tāṅ kauśināgarān mallān bhagavato 'ntike śikṣāpadāni pratyajigrahat ||)
38.9 (atha kauśināga)rā mallā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumody(a bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ ||)
body.translated_text:
And furthermore, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, before the middle watch of the night had passed, administered the precepts (<s>śikṣāpada</s>) to those various <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
38.9 Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, [having heard] the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words ...

body.text: 39. Tibetisch-chinesischer Sondertext
body.translated_text: 39. [Tibetan-Chinese special text — not preserved in Sanskrit.]

body.text: 40.1 (tena khalu samayena kuśinagaryāṃ su)bhadraḥ parivrājaka(ḥ) prativasati jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 40.1 At that time, in <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, there dwelt a wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājaka</s>) named <s>Subhadra</s>, old, aged, and advanced in years.

body.text:
40.2 sa vi(ṃśatiśatavayaskaḥ kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānāṃ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rhan saṃmataḥ ||)
40.3 (aśr)auṣīt s(u)bhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ || adya śramaṇasya gautamasya (rātryā madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||)
40.4 (asti ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣitat)v(am ā)śā ca me santiṣṭhate pratibalaś ca (me) sa bhavāṅ gautamas t(at kāṅkṣitatvaṃ prativinodayitum ||)
40.5 (saced yena bhagavāṅ gautamas tenopasaṅkrameyam upasaṅkramya pṛccheyaṃ) kañcid eva pradeśam || saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnasya vyākaraṇā(ya ||)
40.6 (śrutvā ca punaḥ kuśinagaryā niṣkramya yena yamakaśālavanaṃ tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ ||)
40.7 (tena khalu samaye)nāyuṣmān ānanda ārāmadvāre 'bhyavakāś(e) c(aṅk)r(ame caṅkramyate ||)
40.8 (adrākṣīt) subhadraḥ p(a)r(ivrājaka āyuṣmantam ānandaṃ dūrād eva || dṛṣṭvā ca punar yenāyuṣmān ānanda)s t(e)nopajagām(a || upetyāyuṣmanta)m ānandam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 40.2 He was one hundred and twenty years of age, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and regarded as worthy by the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>. 40.3 The wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> heard: 'Tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without residue (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).' 40.4 'I have a certain doubt regarding the teachings (<s>dharmas</s>), and hope remains in me, and that Master <s>Gautama</s> is capable of removing that doubt of mine.' 40.5 'If I could approach the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s> and, having approached, ask about some point — if he would grant me the opportunity for an answer to my question.' 40.6 Having heard this, he departed from <s>Kuśinagarī</s> and approached the twin <s>Śāla</s>-tree grove. 40.7 At that time, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was walking back and forth in the open space at the entrance of the park. 40.8 The wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> saw the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> from afar. Having seen him, he approached the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and, having approached, said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
40.9 śrutaṃ me bho ānandādya śramaṇ(asya gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||)
40.10 (asti) ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣitatvam āśā ca me santiṣ(ṭhat)e pratibalaś ca me sa bh(avāṅ gautamas tat kāṅkṣitatvaṃ prativinodayitum ||)
40.11 (saced yena bhagavāṅ gautama)s tenopasaṅkrameyam upasaṅkramya pṛccheyaṃ kañcid eva pradeśaṃ sac(ed avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnasya vyākaraṇāya ||)
40.12 (ānandāha || alaṃ subhadra mā bhagavantaṃ viheṭhaya śrāntakāyo bhagavāṅ klāntakāyaḥ sugataḥ ||)
40.13 (dvir api trir api subha)d(ra)ḥ parivrā(jaka āyuṣmantam ā)nandam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 40.9 'I have heard, friend <s>Ānanda</s>, that tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without residue. 40.10 I have a certain doubt regarding the teachings, and hope remains in me, and that Master <s>Gautama</s> is capable of removing that doubt of mine. 40.11 If I could approach the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s> and, having approached, ask about some point — if he would grant me the opportunity for an answer to my question.' 40.12 <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Enough, <s>Subhadra</s>! Do not trouble the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body is weary; the <s>Sugata</s>'s body is exhausted.' 40.13 A second and a third time, the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
40.14 śrutaṃ (bho ānanda purāṇānāṃ parivrājakānām antikāj jīrṇānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ mahatāṃ caraṇācāryāṇāṃ ka)dācit karh(icit tathāgatā ar)hantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā lo(ka utpadyante tadyathodumbaraṃ puṣpaṃ ||)
40.15 (tasya cādya bhagavato gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme 'nu)padhiśe(ṣe nirvāṇadhātau parini)rvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 40.14 'I have heard, friend <s>Ānanda</s>, from the ancient wanderers — those who are aged, old, great teachers of conduct — that only rarely do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones arise in the world, just as the <s>udumbara</s> flower [blooms only rarely]. 40.15 And tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of this <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without residue.'

body.text:
40.16 (asti ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣitatvam āśā ca me santiṣṭhate pratibalaś ca me sa bhavāṅ gautamas tat kāṅkṣitatvaṃ prativinodayitum ||)
40.17 (saced yena bhagavāṅ gautamas tenopasaṅkrameyam upasaṅkramya pṛccheyaṃ kañcid eva pradeśam || saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnasya vyākaraṇāya ||)
40.18 (punar a)py (ā)yuṣmān ān(andaḥ subhadraṃ parivrāja)k(a)m (i)dam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 40.16 'I have a certain doubt regarding the teachings, and hope remains in me, and that Master <s>Gautama</s> is capable of removing that doubt of mine. 40.17 If I could approach the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s> and, having approached, ask about some point — if he would grant me the opportunity for an answer to my question.' 40.18 Once again the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>:

body.text:
40.19 (alaṃ subhadra mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhaya śrāntakāyo bhagavāṅ klāntakāyaḥ sugataḥ ||)
40.20 (imaṃ ca punar āyuṣmata ānandasya subhadreṇa) par(iv)r(ājakena) s(ā)rdham antarāk(athāṃ viprakṛtām aśrauṣīd bhagavān divyena) śrotr(e)ṇa vi(śuddhe)nātikrānta(mā)nuṣeṇa || śrutv(ā ca punar āyuṣmantam ānanda)m āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 40.19 'Enough, <s>Subhadra</s>! Do not trouble the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body is weary; the <s>Sugata</s>'s body is exhausted.' 40.20 Now the <s>Bhagavān</s> heard this conversation between the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> with his divine ear (<s>divya śrotra</s>), purified and surpassing that of humans. Having heard, he addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
40.21 al(am ānanda) mā subhad(r)aṃ pariv(rājakaṃ vāraya pravi)śatu pṛcchatu yad yad evākāṅkṣate || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || ayaṃ (me paści)mo 'nyatī(r)thik(a)p(arivrājakaiḥ sārdham a)ntarākath(ā)samu(dāhāraḥ || ayaṃ ca m)e paścimo bhav(iṣyati sākṣācchrā)vakāṇām ehibhikṣukapravr(ajitānāṃ yad uta subhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ ||)
40.22 (atha subha)dra(ḥ) parivrājako bhag(avatā kṛtāvakāśo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita) udagraḥ prītisaumanasyajā(to yena bhagavāṃs) t(e)nopa(saṃkrāntaḥ ||)
40.23 (upasaṃkramya bhagavat)ā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanī(ṃ) saṃrañjan(īṃ) kathā(ṃ) vividhām upasa(ṃ)hṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdat ||
body.translated_text: 40.21 'Enough, <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not turn away the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>. Let him enter and ask whatever he wishes. For what reason? This is my last conversation with a non-Buddhist wanderer. And this will be my last disciple among those ordained directly by the "Come, monk" (<s>ehibhikṣuka</s>) formula — namely, the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>.' 40.22 Then the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>, granted the opportunity by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, joyful, pleased, delighted, elated, filled with rapture and happiness of mind, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 40.23 Having approached, he exchanged with the <s>Bhagavān</s> various kinds of friendly and agreeable conversation, and then sat down to one side.

body.text:
40.24 ekāntaniṣaṇṇ(aḥ subhadraḥ parivrājako bhagavanta)m (i)dam avo(cat ||)
40.25 pṛccheyam ahaṃ bho gautama kañcid eva pradeśam || saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnasya vyākar(aṇāya ||)
40.26 <Nur Tib. und Chin.>
40.27 (yānīmāni bho gauta)ma pṛthag loke tīrthyāyatan(ā)n(i) tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapo maskarī gośālīputraḥ saṃjayī (vai)ru(ṭī)p(ut)r(o 'jitaḥ keśakambalaḥ kakudaḥ kātyāyano nir)grantho jñātiputraḥ pratyajñāsiṣur ime s(vāṃ) svā(ṃ) pratijñām ||
body.translated_text: 40.24 Seated to one side, the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 40.25 'I would ask Master <s>Gautama</s> about a certain point — if he would grant me the opportunity for an answer to my question.' 40.26 [Preserved only in Tibetan and Chinese.] 40.27 'There are, Master <s>Gautama</s>, these various sectarian establishments in the world — namely, <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Sañjayī Vairuṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, [and] <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>. Did they each realize their own doctrines?'

body.text: 40.28 atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ vel(āyā)ṃ gā(th)e babhāṣe ||
body.translated_text: 40.28 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, on that occasion, spoke these verses:

body.text:
40.29 (ekonatriṃśo vayasā subhadra
  yat prāvrajaṃ kiṃ ku)ś(a)laṃ gaveṣī ||
body.translated_text: 40.29 'At the age of twenty-nine, O <s>Subhadra</s>, I went forth, seeking what is wholesome.'

body.text: pañcāśad (varṣā)ṇi samādhikā(ni

children.translated_text: have passed since I went forth, O <s>Subhadra</s>.' [1]

children.text:
40.30 śīlaṃ samā(dhiś caraṇaṃ ca vidyā
  caikāgratā cetaso bhāvitā me ||
children.translated_text: 40.30 'Morality (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>), and knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), and one-pointedness of mind — these have been cultivated by me.'

body.translated_text: 'More than fifty years

body.text: ārya)sya dharmasya pradeśavaktā

children.translated_text: outside of this, there is no [true] ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>).' [2]

children.text: 40.31 yasmin subhadra dharmavinaya āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgo nopalabhy(ate prathamaḥ śramaṇa)s tatra nopalabh(yate) dv(i)t(ī)yas tṛtīy(aś catu)r(thaḥ) ś(ra)m(aṇas ta)tra nopala(bh)yate ||
children.translated_text: 40.31 'In whatever <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s> (Doctrine and Discipline), O <s>Subhadra</s>, the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) is not found — in that, the first ascetic is not found, the second, the third, and the fourth ascetic are not found there.'

body.translated_text: 'A teacher of portions of the noble <s>Dharma</s> —

body.text: 40.32 yasmiṃs tu subhadra dharmavinaya āryāṣṭāṅgo mā(r)ga upal(abhyate prathamaḥ) ś(ra)maṇas tatropalabhyate (dvitīyas tṛtīyaś caturtha)ḥ śramaṇas t(atropa)labhyate ||
body.translated_text: 40.32 'But in whatever <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s>, O <s>Subhadra</s>, the Noble Eightfold Path is found — in that, the first ascetic is found, the second, the third, and the fourth ascetic are found there.'

body.text: 40.33 asmin subhadrārye dharmavinaye ā(ryāṣṭāṅgo mārga upalabhyate tadya)thā samyagd(ṛ)ṣ(ṭiḥ samyaksaṅkalpaḥ samyagvāk samyakkarmāntaḥ samyagājīvaḥ) samyagvyāyāmaḥ samyaksmṛt(i)ḥ samyaksam(ā)dh(iḥ || iha) prath(amaḥ śramaṇa upalabhyata iha dvitīya iha tṛtīya iha caturtho na santīto bahiḥ) ś(ra)maṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ||
body.translated_text: 40.33 'In this noble <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s>, O <s>Subhadra</s>, the Noble Eightfold Path is found — namely: right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṅkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), [and] right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). Here the first ascetic is found, here the second, here the third, here the fourth. Outside of this there are no ascetics (<s>śramaṇas</s>) or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.'

body.text: 40.34 śūnyāḥ paraprav(aca)n(ā)ḥ śramaṇair vā brāhmaṇair vā || evam (atra parṣadi samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadā)mi ||
body.translated_text: 40.34 'Empty of ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are the other teachings. Thus, in this assembly, I roar the correct lion's roar (<s>samyak siṃhanāda</s>).'

body.text:
40.35 asmin kha(lu dharmapa)ryāye (bhā)ṣyamāṇe subhadrasya parivrājakasya virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utp(annam ||)
40.36 (atha subhadraḥ parivrājako dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadhar)m(ā) paryava(gā)ḍhadharmā tīrṇakāṅkṣ(as tī)rṇavicikitso 'parapratyayo 'nanyan(e)y(aḥ śāstuḥ śāsane dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam u)ttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmān ānandas t(e)nāñjaliṃ praṇamyāyuṣmantam ā(na)nd(am ida)m avoc(at ||)
40.37 (lābhā bhadantānandena sulabdhā yad bhagavatānand)o mahācāryeṇa mahā(cā)ryāntevāsyabhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ || asmākam api syur lābhāḥ sul(a)bdh(ā yad va)yaṃ (labhemahi svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam ||)
40.38 (a)thāyuṣ(mā)n ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 40.35 While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>) arose in the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s> with regard to all phenomena. 40.36 Then the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>, having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having penetrated deeply into the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having crossed beyond uncertainty, not dependent on another, not led by another, having attained confidence in the Teacher's teaching with regard to all phenomena — rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, he joined his palms toward the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 40.37 'It is a gain for the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, well gained, that <s>Ānanda</s> has been anointed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great teacher, with the anointing of a great teacher's pupil! It would be a gain for us too, well gained, if we could obtain the going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), the full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the state of a monk (<s>bhikṣubhāva</s>) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s>.' 40.38 Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
40.39 aya(ṃ) bhadanta subhadraḥ pari(v)r(ājaka ākāṅkṣate svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam ||)
40.40 (tatra bhagavān) subh(adraṃ) parivrājakam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 40.39 'This wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>, Venerable Sir, desires the going forth, the full ordination, and the state of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s>.' 40.40 Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>:

body.text: 40.41 ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacar(ya)m ||
body.translated_text: 40.41 'Come, monk (<s>ehi bhikṣo</s>)! Practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>)!'

body.text:
40.42 saiva (ta)sy(āyuṣ)m(ataḥ) pravr(aj)y(ā)bhūt saivopasaṃpat sa eva bh(i)kṣubhāva(ḥ ||)
40.43 evaṃ pravrajitaḥ (sa) āyuṣm(ān eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā vyahārṣīt || eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā viharan)
40.44 yasy(ār)th(aṃ) kulaputrāḥ k(e)ś(aśma)ś(rū)ṇy avat(ā)rya k(āṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya) samyag eva śraddhayāgārād anagārikāṃ pravrajanti tad anuttaraṃ brahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñāya sākṣ(ātkṛtyopasaṃpadya prave)dayati ||
body.translated_text:
40.42 That itself was his ordination, that itself was his full admission, that itself was his becoming a monk.
40.43 Thus ordained, the venerable [<s>Subhadra</s>], dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, exerted himself ...

body.text: 40.45 kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi ||
body.translated_text: 40.45 'Destroyed is birth for me; the holy life has been lived; what had to be done has been done; I know of no further existence beyond this.'

body.text:
40.46 ājñātavān sa āyuṣmān (ar)h(an) babhū(va suvimuktaḥ ||)
40.47 (puna)r athāyuṣmataḥ subhadrasyaitad abhavat ||
body.translated_text:
40.46 The venerable [<s>Subhadra</s>] became one who had direct knowledge — an <s>Arhat</s>, well-liberated.
40.47 Then this thought occurred to the venerable <s>Subhadra</s>:

body.text:
40.48 na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ śāstāraṃ parinirvāyantaṃ paśyeyaṃ yannv ahaṃ prathamatar(aṃ parinirvāyeyam iti ||)
40.49 tatrāyuṣmān subhadraḥ prathamataraḥ parinirvṛta(ḥ) ||
body.translated_text:
40.48 'It would not be fitting for me to see the Teacher passing into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. What if I were to pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> first?'
40.49 Thereupon the venerable <s>Subhadra</s> passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> first.

body.text: 40.50 tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 40.50 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:

body.text: 40.51 tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo 'dyāgreṇā(nya)t(īrthi)kā na pravrājayitavyā nopasaṃpādayitavyāḥ sthāpayitvā jñātiśākyaṃ vāgneyaṃ vā jaṭilam ||
body.translated_text: 40.51 'Therefore, monks, from this day forward, non-Buddhist wanderers (<s>anyatīrthika</s>) are not to be ordained, not to be given full admission — except for a <s>Śākya</s> kinsman or an <s>Āgneya</s> (fire-worshipping) ascetic with matted hair (<s>jaṭila</s>).'

body.text: 40.52 jñātiśākya āgacchet tīrthikadhvajena yady (ā)k(ā)ṅ(kṣeta) dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ tam e(vākāṅkṣa)m(ā)ṇaṃ bhikṣavaḥ pravrājayeyur upasaṃpādayeyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 40.52 'If a <s>Śākya</s> kinsman comes bearing the mark of a non-Buddhist wanderer and desires ordination, full admission, and monkhood in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> — monks, you should ordain and fully admit such a one who desires it.'

body.text: 40.53 tat kasmād dhetoḥ || dadāmy ahaṃ jñātīnāṃ (jñātyabhyanujñāna)m ||
body.translated_text: 40.53 'For what reason? I grant my kinsmen the permission of kinship (<s>jñātyabhyanujñāna</s>).'

body.text: 40.54 anyatīrthikaparivrājakā āgaccheyur yady ākāṅkṣey(uḥ svākhyāte dharma)vinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ tata enāṃ bhikṣavaś caturo māsā(n upādhyāyenākā)lakaiś cīvaraiḥ parivāsayitavyaṃ manyeyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 40.54 'If non-Buddhist wandering ascetics (<s>anyatīrthika parivrājaka</s>) come and desire ordination, full admission, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> — then, monks, those [candidates] for four months, under a preceptor, with appropriate robes ...'

body.text: 40.55 (caturṇāṃ māsā)nām atyayāt parivāsinaḥ paryupāsya bhikṣusaṃghasyārādhitacittās tata en(ān ākāṅkṣamāṇān pravrāja)y(e)yur upasa(ṃ)p(ā)day(e)yuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 40.55 'After the passing of four months, those who have undergone probation, having attended upon the community of monks and satisfied their minds, then — if they so desire — they should be ordained and fully admitted.'

body.text: 40.56 pravrāj(a)y(a)t(a bhik)ṣ(ava) āgneyāñ jaṭilān || upasaṃpādayata bhikṣava āgneyāñ jaṭilān || tat kasmād dhetoḥ ||
body.translated_text: 40.56 'Ordain the <s>Āgneya</s> ascetics with matted hair, monks! Give full admission to the <s>Āgneya</s> ascetics with matted hair, monks! For what reason?'

body.text:
40.57 karmavādi(no hi bhikṣava) āgneyā jaṭilāḥ kriyāvādino hetuvādino vīrya(vādinaḥ ||)
40.58 (ta)smāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam ||
body.translated_text:
40.57 'For the <s>Āgneya</s> ascetics with matted hair, monks, are believers in <s>karma</s> (action), believers in efficacy, believers in causation, and believers in effort.'
40.58 'Therefore, monks, thus should you train:'

body.text: 40.59 yat karmavādinaś ca bhaviṣyāmaḥ kriyāvādi(naś ca hetuv)ādinaś ca vīryavādinaś ca || evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
body.translated_text: 40.59 '"We will be believers in <s>karma</s>, believers in efficacy, believers in causation, and believers in effort." Thus, monks, should you train.'

body.text: 40.60 (tasmāt ta)rhi bhikṣavo ye te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya s(aṃ)vartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya sāṃp(arāyahitāya) sāṃparāyasukhāya te bhikṣubhir udgṛhya paryavāpya ta(thā tathā dhā)rayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathedaṃ brahmacaryaṃ cira(sthitikaṃ bha)viṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya (lokānu)kaṃpāyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 40.60 'Therefore, monks, whatever <s>dharmas</s> conduce to welfare in this present life, to happiness in this present life, to welfare in the next life, and to happiness in the next life — those <s>dharmas</s> should be taken up by monks, mastered, and thus and thus upheld ...'

body.text: 40.61 katame te dharmā dṛṣṭad(harma)h(i)tāya saṃvartante pūrvavad yāvad devamanuṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 40.61 'What are those <s>dharmas</s> that conduce to welfare in this present life?' as before, 'up to: of gods and humans.'

body.text: 40.62 tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ (vyā)karaṇaṃ gāthodānanidānāvadānetivṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmopadeśāḥ || ime te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante pūrvavad yāvad devamanuṣyāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 40.62 'Namely: <s>sūtra</s> (discourses), <s>geya</s> (mixed prose and verse), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecies), <s>gāthā</s> (verses), <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterances), <s>nidāna</s> (introductions), <s>avadāna</s> (legends), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (narratives), <s>jātaka</s> (birth stories), <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive discourses), <s>adbhutadharma</s> (wondrous events), and <s>upadeśa</s> (instructions). These are the <s>dharmas</s> that conduce to welfare in this present life,' as before, 'up to: of gods and humans.'

body.text: 41.1 syā(t kha)l(u yu)ṣ(m)ākaṃ bhikṣavo mamātyayāt || parinirvṛto 'smākaṃ śāst(ā ||) n(ā)sty etarhy asmākaṃ (śāstā) niḥsaraṇa(ṃ) vā ||
body.translated_text: 41.1 'It may be, monks, that after my passing you will think: "Our Teacher has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; we no longer have a Teacher, nor a way out."'

body.text:
41.2 na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyam || yo vo mayānvardhamāsaṃ p(r)ā(t)i(mokṣa uddeśitaḥ sa vo 'dyāgr)eṇa śās(t)ā sa ca v(o niḥsaraṇam ||)
(yāni bhikṣavaḥ kṣudrānukṣudrāṇ)i (śi)kṣāpadā(ni tāni kālena saṃghaḥ samagrībhūtaḥ samuddharatu tat sukhasparśavihārāya) saṃvartate ||
body.translated_text:
41.2 'It should not be viewed thus. The <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of monastic rules) which I have recited to you every half-month — that, from this day forward, shall be your Teacher, and that shall be your way out.'
[Whatever minor and subsidiary training rules, monks ...]

body.text: 41.3 tasmā(t tarhi) cādyāgre(ṇa) navatara(keṇa) bhikṣuṇā vṛddhatarako (bhik)ṣu(r na nāmavādena na gotravā)de(na samudāca)ritavyo 'nyatra bhadant(eti) vāyuṣmad vā ||
body.translated_text: 41.3 'Therefore, from this day forward, a younger monk should not address an elder monk by name or by clan, but rather as "Venerable Sir" (<s>bhadanta</s>) or "Noble One" (<s>āyuṣmat</s>).'

body.text: 41.4 tena ca vṛddhatarakeṇa bhikṣuṇā navatarako bhikṣur upasthāpayitavya upalāḍayitavyaḥ p(ā)tr(e)ṇa cīvareṇa śikyena (sarake)ṇa kāyabandhanena (p)r(akara)ṇikayā paripṛcchanikayodd(e)ś(ena yogena) manasikāreṇa ||
body.translated_text: 41.4 'And an elder monk should look after a younger monk, attending to him with bowl, robe, carrying-cloth, water-strainer, waist-band, and articles for inquiry and questioning ...'

body.text:
41.5 catvāra ime bhi(k)ṣ(avaḥ) pṛ(thivīp)r(adeśāḥ śrāddhasya kulaputrasya kuladuhitur vā yāvajjīvam anusmaraṇīyā bhavanti ||)
41.6 (katame catvā)raḥ || iha bhagavāñ jātaḥ || iha bha(gavān anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ || iha bhagavatā triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ) pravartitam || iha bhagavān anupadhiśeṣe nirvā(ṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ ||)
41.7 (āgamiṣyanti bhikṣavo mamātyayāc caityaparicārakāś caityavandakās ta evaṃ va)kṣ(ya)nti ||
body.translated_text:
41.5 'There are, monks, four places (<s>pṛthivīpradeśa</s>) that should be remembered for life by a faithful son or daughter of good family.'
41.6 'Which four? Here the <s>Bhagavān</s> was born; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> ...'

body.text: 41.8 iha bhagav(ā)ñ (jātaḥ || iha bhagavān anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ || iha bhagavatā triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam || iha bhagavān anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛ)taḥ ||
body.translated_text: 41.8 'Here the <s>Bhagavān</s> was born; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>); here the <s>Bhagavān</s> turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel with three turnings and twelve aspects; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> [passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] ...'

body.text:
41.9 atrāntarā ye kecit prasannacittā mamāntike kālaṃ kariṣyanti te sarve svargopagā ye (kecit sopadhiśeṣāḥ ||)
41.10 apar(aṃ) catvāraḥ pṛthivīpradeśā(ḥ) śrāddhasya kulaputrasy(a ku)laduhitur vā yāvajjīvam abhigamanīyā bhavanti ||
body.translated_text:
41.9 'In the meanwhile, all those who die near me with faithful minds will all be reborn in heaven, as many as still have remainder [of clinging].'
41.10 'Furthermore, there are four places for a faithful son of good family ...'

body.text: 41.11 katame catvāra(ḥ) || iha bhagavāñ jā(taḥ || iha bhagavān a)nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ || iha bhagavatā tripar(iva)rtaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam || iha bhagavān anupa(dh)i(śeṣe nirvāṇadhātau pa)rinirvṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 41.11 'Which four? Here the <s>Bhagavān</s> was born; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel with three turnings and twelve aspects; here [the <s>Bhagavān</s> passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] ...'

body.text:
41.12 āgamiṣyanti bhikṣavo (mamātyayāc caityaparicārakā)ś caityavandak(ā)s t(a evaṃ vakṣyanti ||)
41.13 iha bhaga(vāñ) jātaḥ || i(ha bhagavān anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim a)bhisaṃ(buddhaḥ || iha bhagavatā triparivartaṃ dvāda)śākāraṃ dhārmyaṃ dha(r)macakr(aṃ) pravartitam || iha bhagavān an(upadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau) parinirvṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
41.12 'After my passing, monks, there will come shrine-attendants and shrine-worshippers, and they will say thus:'
41.13 '"Here the <s>Bhagavān</s> was born; here the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening ..."'

body.text: 41.14 atrāntarā ye kecit prasannacittā mamāntike kālaṃ kariṣyanti sarve te svargopagā ye kecit sopadhiśeṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 41.14 'In the meanwhile, all those who die near me with faithful minds will all be reborn in heaven, as many as still have remainder [of clinging].'

body.text: 42.1 tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āman(t)rayate ||
body.translated_text: 42.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks:

body.text: 42.2 pṛcchata bhikṣavo mā vidhārayata || yasya syāt kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā buddhe vā dharme vā saṅghe vā duḥkhe vā samudaye vā nirodhe vā mārge vā sa praśnenāhaṃ vyākaraṇena ||
body.translated_text: 42.2 'Ask, monks, do not hold back! Should anyone have doubt or uncertainty about the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, about suffering, its origin, its cessation, or the path — let him question me, and I will answer.'

body.text: 42.3 syāt khalu yuṣmākam evam || kathaṃ vayaṃ śāstāram āsādyāsādya pratimantrayiṣyāmaḥ || na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyam || bhik(ṣu)r (bh)ikṣo(r āroca)yatā(ṃ) sahāyakaḥ sahāyakasya sa praśnenāhaṃ vyākaraṇena ||
body.translated_text: 42.3 'It may be that you think: "How can we question the Teacher again and again?" It should not be viewed thus. Let a monk inform a monk; let a companion inform a companion; he [will answer] ...'

body.text: 42.4 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 42.4 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: 42.5 yathā khalv ahaṃ bhadanta bh(agavato bhāṣitasyārtha)m (ā)j(ān)āmi nāsti kaścid asyāṃ pariṣady ekabhikṣur api yasya syāt kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā pūrvavad yāvan mārge vā ||
body.translated_text: 42.5 'As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, Venerable Sir, there is not a single monk in this assembly who has any doubt or uncertainty,' as before, 'up to: or about the path.'

body.text: 42.6 sādhu sādhv ānanda prasādena tvam evaṃ vadasi || ta(thāgatasya tv an)uttare jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ||
body.translated_text: 42.6 'Well said, well said, <s>Ānanda</s>! With faith you speak thus. But the <s>Tathāgata</s> has unsurpassed knowledge and vision proceeding [directly].'

body.text: 42.7 yāvantaḥ khalu bhikṣavo 'syāṃ pariṣadi sanniṣaṇṇāḥ sannipatitā nāsti kaścid atra ekabhikṣur api y(asya) syāt kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā pūrvavad yāvan mārge vā ||
body.translated_text: 42.7 'However many monks, indeed, are seated and gathered in this assembly, there is not a single monk among them who has any doubt or uncertainty,' as before, 'up to: or about the path.'

body.text: 42.8 api tu karaṇīyam etat tathāgatena yathāpi tat paścimāṃ janatām anukaṃpamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 42.8 But this must be done by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, inasmuch as he has compassion for the future generation.

body.text: 42.9 atha bhagav(ān svakāyād uttarāsaṅgam ekān)te vivṛtya bhikṣūn āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 42.9 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, having uncovered his upper robe from his own body on one side, addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks):

body.text: 42.10 avalokayata bhikṣavas tathāgatasya kāyam || vyavalokayata bhikṣavas tathāgatasya kāyam || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || durlabhadarśanā y(asmāt tathāgatā) arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tadyathoduṃbare puṣpam ||
body.translated_text: 42.10 "Behold, <s>bhikṣus</s>, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Examine well, <s>bhikṣus</s>, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? Because <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are rare to behold, just as the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree)."

body.text: 42.11 aṅga bhikṣavas tūṣṇīṃ bhavata vyayadharmāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 42.11 "Come, <s>bhikṣus</s>, be silent. All <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) are subject to decay."

body.text:
42.12 iyaṃ tatra tathāgatasya paścimā (vācā ||)
42.13 (tad) uktvā bhagavān prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || prathamād dhyānād vyutth(āya dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || dvitīyād dhyānād vyutthāya tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || tṛtīyād dhyānād vyutthāya caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || caturthād dhyānād vyutthāyākāśānantyāyatanaṃ sam)āpannaḥ || ā(kāśānantyāyatanād vyutthāya vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || vijñānānantyāyatanād vyutthāyākiñcanyāyatanaṃ) samāpann(aḥ || ā)k(i)ñcanyāyatan(ād vyutthāya naivasañ)jñ(ā)nāsa(ñ)jñ(āyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || naivasañjñānāsañjñāyatanād vyutthāya sañjñāve)dayitanirodha(ṃ) s(amāpannaḥ ||)
42.14 (a)thāyuṣmān (ānanda ā)yuṣmant(am aniruddham idam avocat ||)
42.15 (parinirvṛta āyuṣmann aniruddha bhagavān ||)
42.16 (naivam āyuṣmann ānanda || sañjñāvedayitanirodhaṃ sa)māpan(no buddho bhagavān ||)
42.17 (saṃmukhaṃ ma āyuṣmann aniruddha bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukham udgṛhītam || caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpya cakṣuṣmanta āniñjyaṃ śāntiṃ samāpannā buddhā bhagavantaḥ pa)r(i)n(i)rvānti ||
body.translated_text:
42.12 This was the final utterance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
42.13 Having spoken that, the <s>Bhagavat</s> entered the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Rising from the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the second <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the third <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the <s>Ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite space). Rising from the sphere of infinite space, he entered the <s>Vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite consciousness). Rising from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he entered the <s>Ākiñcanyāyatana</s> (sphere of nothingness). Rising from the sphere of nothingness, he entered the <s>Naivasañjñānāsañjñāyatana</s> (sphere of neither perception nor non-perception). Rising from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the <s>Sañjñāvedayitanirodha</s> (cessation of perception and feeling).
42.14 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>:
42.15 "Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."
42.16 "Not so, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, has entered the cessation of perception and feeling."
42.17 "Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, I have heard it face to face from the <s>Bhagavat</s>, received it face to face: 'Having attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the clear-sighted <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having entered the imperturbable peace.'"

body.text:
42.18 atha bhagav(ān sañjñāvedayitanirodhād vyutthāya naivasañjñānāsañjñāyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || naiva)sa(ñ)jñān(asañj)ñ(āyatanād vyutthāyākiñcanyāyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || ākiñcanyāyatanāḍ vyutthāya vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || vijñānānanty)āyatanād vyutth(āyākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samāpannaḥ || ākāśānantyāyatanād vyutthāya caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || caturthād dhyānād vyutthāya tṛtīyaṃ dhyā)naṃ samā(pannaḥ || tṛtīyād dhyānād vyutthāya dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || dvitīyād dhyānād vyutthāya prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || prathamād dhyānād vyutthāya dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ ||) (d)v(i)t(ī)yā(d) dhy(ā)n(ād vyutthāya tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || tṛtīyād dhyānād vyutthāya caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ || caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpya cakṣuṣmān āniñjyaṃ śāntiṃ) samāpanno bud(dh)o( bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ
||)
42.19 (samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavaty atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūd ulkāpātā diśodāhā antarīkṣe devadundubhayo nadanti ||)
body.translated_text:
42.18 Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, rising from the cessation of perception and feeling, entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. Rising from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the sphere of nothingness. Rising from the sphere of nothingness, he entered the sphere of infinite consciousness. Rising from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he entered the sphere of infinite space. Rising from the sphere of infinite space, he entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the third <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the second <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the second <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Rising from the third <s>dhyāna</s>, he entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Having attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the clear-sighted <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, having entered the imperturbable peace, attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.
42.19 Immediately upon the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, at that moment there was a great earthquake, meteors fell, fires blazed in the quarters, and celestial drums resounded in the sky.

body.text: 43 Vorg. 43 ist ein in der Sanskritversion nicht üeberlieferter tibetisch-chinesischer Sondertext (Nr. VI), in dem berichtet wird, wie König Ajātaśatru von Magadha mit Hilfe eines Gemäldes vom Tode des Buddha in Kenntnis gesetzt wird. Siehe unten S. 490-494.
body.translated_text: [Chapter 43 is a special Tibetan-Chinese text (No. VI) not transmitted in the Sanskrit version, which recounts how King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s> was informed of the Buddha's death by means of a painting. See below pp. 490-494.]

body.text: 44.1 (samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavaty ubhau yamakaśālavanasya drumottamau tathāgatasya siṃhaśayyāṃ śālapuṣpair avāki)ratām ||
body.translated_text: 44.1 Immediately upon the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, both the foremost trees of the twin <s>śāla</s> grove showered the lion-couch of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with <s>śāla</s> blossoms.

body.text:
44.2 athānyataro bhikṣus t(asyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ babhāṣe ||)
44.3 (sundarau khalv imau
  śālavanasyāsya) drum(ottamau ||
body.translated_text:
44.2 Then a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) at that moment spoke this verse:
44.3 "Indeed beautiful are these two foremost trees of this <s>śāla</s> grove,

children.translated_text: which showered with blossoms
the Teacher who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."

children.text: 44.4 s(amanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati śa)kro devendras t(asyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ babhāṣe ||)
