children.translated_text: 44.4 Immediately upon the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, at that moment spoke this verse:

body.text:
44.5 (anityā vata saṃskārā
  utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 44.5 "Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations), having the nature of arising and passing away.

children.translated_text: Having arisen, they cease;
their stilling is bliss."

children.text: 44.6 (sa)manantarapar(inirvṛte buddhe bhagavati brahmā sahāṃpatir gāthāṃ babhāṣe ||)
children.translated_text: 44.6 Immediately upon the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> spoke this verse:

body.text:
44.7 (sarvabhūtāni loke 'smin
  nikṣepsyanti sa)m(u)c(ch)rayam ||
body.translated_text: 44.7 "All beings in this world will lay down their bodily form,

body.text:
(e)vaṃvidho yatra śā(stā
  lokeṣv apratipudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: when such a Teacher, without equal in the worlds,

body.text:
tathāgatabalaprāptaḥ
  cakṣuṣmān parinirvṛtaḥ |)
44.8 (samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavaty āyuṣmān a)nir(u)ddhas t(asy)āṃ (velāyāṃ) gāthā babh(āṣe ||)
44.9 (sthitā āśvāsapraśvāsā
  sthiracittasya tāyinaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
endowed with the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the clear-sighted one, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."
44.8 Immediately upon the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> at that moment spoke these verses:
44.9 "With in-breathing and out-breathing stilled, the Protector whose mind was steady,

body.text:
āniñjyaṃ śāntim āgamya
  cakṣuṣmān) parini(rvṛtaḥ ||)
44.10 (tadābhavad bhīṣaṇakaṃ
  tadābhūd romaharṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text:
having attained the imperturbable peace, the clear-sighted one has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."
44.10 "Then there was terror, then there was hair-raising dread,

body.text:
sarvākārabalopetaḥ
  śāstā kālaṃ yadākarot |)
44.11 (asaṃlīnena cittena
  vedanā adhivāsayan ||
body.translated_text:
when the Teacher, endowed with all powers and excellences, passed away."
44.11 "With mind unshrunken, enduring the feelings,

body.text:
pradyotasyeva nirvāṇaṃ
  vimokṣas tasya cetasaḥ |)
44.12 (tatraikatyā bhikṣavaḥ pṛthivyām āvartante parivartante || ekatyā bāhūn pragṛhya prakrośanti || evaṃ cāhuḥ || atikṣipraṃ bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ || atikṣipraṃ sugataḥ parinirvṛtaḥ || atikṣipraṃ cakṣur lokasyāntarhitaḥ ||)
44.13 (ekatyāś cetoduḥkhasamarpitās tiṣṭhanti || ekatyā dharmatām eva pratismaranti || prāg evāsmākaṃ bhagavatākhyātaṃ sarvair iṣṭaiḥ kāntaiḥ priyair manāpair nānābhāvo bhaviṣyati vinābhāvo viprayogo visaṃyogaḥ || kuta etal labhyaṃ yat taj jātaṃ bhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vedayitaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ kṣayadharmaṃ vyayadharmaṃ vibhavadharmaṃ virāgadharmaṃ nirodhadharmaṃ pralokadharmaṃ na prarujyate nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||)
44.14 (athāyuṣmān aniruddha āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||)
44.15 (mandaṃ mandaṃ) tāvad āyuṣmann ānanda bhikṣavaḥ parākramantu ||
body.translated_text:
like the extinguishing of a lamp was the liberation of his mind."
44.12 Thereupon, some <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) rolled and writhed on the ground; some, raising their arms, cried out loudly, and spoke thus: "Too quickly the <s>Bhagavat</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the eye of the world has vanished!"
44.13 Some stood immersed in mental sorrow; some reflected upon the true nature of things: "Indeed, the <s>Bhagavat</s> has previously declared to us that from all that is dear, beloved, pleasant, and agreeable, there will be separation, parting, disunion, and disconnection. How could it be obtained that what is born, come into being, made, conditioned, felt, dependently arisen — subject to the nature of decay, of destruction, of dissolution, of dispassion, of cessation, of disintegration — should not be destroyed? Such a state does not exist."
44.14 Then the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:
44.15 "Gently, gently now, venerable <s>Ānanda</s> — let the <s>bhikṣus</s> restrain themselves."

body.text: 44.16 tathā hy anekakalpaśatāyuṣo d(e)vatā avadhyāyanti kṣipanti vivācayanti ||
body.translated_text: 44.16 "For deities whose lifespan extends over many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) are reproaching, criticizing, and blaming."

body.text: 44.17 katham idānīṃ bhikṣavaḥ svyākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitā apratisaṅkhyānabahulā viharanti ||
body.translated_text: 44.17 "How is it that <s>bhikṣus</s>, gone forth in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, dwell given over to lack of reflection?"

body.text: 44.18 kiyata āyuṣmān aniruddho devatāḥ saṃjānāti ||
body.translated_text: 44.18 "To what extent does the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> perceive the deities?"

body.text: 44.19 yāvad āyuṣmann ānanda kuśinagarī yāvan nadī hiraṇyavatī yāvad yamakaśālavanaṃ yāvan mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam atrāntarā dvādaśa yojanāni sāmantakena nāsti kiñcin mahāśakyamahāśakyābhi(r) devatābhir asphuṭaṃ spharaṇīyam antato daṇḍakoṭiviṣṭambhanamātram api ||
body.translated_text: 44.19 "As far as <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, as far as the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, as far as the twin <s>śāla</s> grove, as far as the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> <s>caitya</s> (shrine) of the <s>Mallās</s> — within this area of twelve <s>yojanas</s> all around, there is not even a space the size of the tip of a stick that is not pervaded by great and mighty deities."

body.text: 44.20 tata ekatyā devatā(ḥ) pṛthivyām āvartante parivartante || ekatyā bāhūn p(ragṛ)hya prakrośanti pūrvavad yāvan nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: 44.20 Thereupon some deities rolled and writhed on the ground; some, raising their arms, cried out loudly — as before, up to "such a state does not exist."

body.text: 44.21 tāṃ khalu rātrim āyuṣmān aniruddha āyuṣmāṃś cānando yadbhūyasā dhārmyā viniścayakathayātināmi(tavantau ||)
body.translated_text: 44.21 Indeed, that night, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spent the greater part in doctrinal discussion and decisive discourse.

body.text: 45.1 (a)thāyuṣmān aniruddha āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 45.1 Then the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text:
45.2 gacchānanda kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānām ārocaya || parinirvṛto vo vāsiṣṭhāḥ śāstā yad (va)ḥ k(ṛtya)ṃ (vā karaṇī)ya(ṃ) vā tat kurudhvaṃ || mā vaḥ paścād vipratisāro bhaviṣyati || katham idānīm asmākaṃ grāmakṣetre śāstā par(i)n(ir)vṛ(to) yasya vaya(ṃ) pūj(ā)dhikārikām au(t)suky(aṃ) na s(amāpannāḥ ||)
45.3. (evam ity āyuṣmā)n ānanda āyuṣmato 'niruddhasya pratiśrutya saṃghāṭim ādāyānyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānāṃ saṃsthāgāras t(e)n(o)pajagāma ||
body.translated_text:
45.2 "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>: 'Your Teacher, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Whatever duty or obligation you have, do it now. Let there be no regret for you afterwards, [thinking:] "How is it that the Teacher has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of our village, and we did not undertake the eagerness for the right of worship."'"
45.3 "So be it," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, taking his outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>), with another <s>bhikṣu</s> as his attendant following behind, approached the assembly hall of the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>.

body.text: 45.4 tena khalu samayena kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃsthāgāre sanniṣaṇṇāḥ sannipatitā yadbhūyasā tenaiva karaṇīyena ||
body.translated_text: 45.4 At that time, the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> were seated and assembled in the assembly hall, mostly occupied with that very business.

body.text: 45.5 athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kauśināgarān mallān idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 45.5 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> with these words:

body.text: 45.6 śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā || parinirvṛto vo vāsiṣṭhāḥ śāstā yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kurudhvam || mā vaḥ paścād vipratisāro bhaviṣyati || katham idānīm asmākaṃ grāmakṣetre śāstā parinirvṛto yasya vayaṃ pū(j)ādhikārikām autsukyaṃ na samāpannāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 45.6 "Hear this, noble <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, whether you be communities, guilds, corporations, or assemblies! O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, your Teacher has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing). Whatever duty or obligation you have, attend to it now. Let there be no regret for you later, thinking: 'How is it that the Teacher attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in our domain and we did not undertake the eagerness befitting his worship?'"

body.text: 45.7 śrutvā ca punas tata ekatyāḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ pṛthivyām āvartante parivartante || ek(atyā bāhūn pragṛhya prakrośanti || e)vam āhuḥ || atikṣipraṃ bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ || atikṣipraṃ sugata(ḥ par)i(nirvṛtaḥ || atikṣipraṃ cakṣur lo)kasyāntarhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 45.7 And having heard this, some of the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> rolled and writhed upon the ground; some, stretching out their arms, cried out aloud. Thus they said: "Too quickly has the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly has the <s>Sugata</s> attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly has the Eye of the World vanished!"

body.text: 45.8 e(katyāś cetoduḥkhasamarpitās ti)ṣṭhanti || ekatyā dharmatām eva pratisaranti || prāg evāsmāka(ṃ) bhagavatākhyātaṃ sa(r)vai(r iṣṭaiḥ kāntaiḥ priyair manāpair nānābhāvo) bhaviṣyati vin(ābhāvo viprayogo visaṃyogaḥ ||) kuta etal labhyaṃ yat taj jātaṃ bhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vedayitaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ (kṣayadharmaṃ vyayadharmaṃ vibhavadharmaṃ virāgadharmaṃ ni)rodhadharmaṃ (p)r(a)lo(kadharmaṃ na prarujyate) nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: 45.8 Some stood afflicted by mental anguish; some took recourse to the nature of things, saying: "Long ago the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared to us that there will be separation, parting, division, and dissociation from all that is cherished, beloved, dear, and agreeable. How could it be otherwise? That which is born, come into being, made, conditioned, experienced, and dependently arisen — subject to decay, subject to dissolution, subject to destruction, subject to dispassion, subject to cessation, subject to the law of perishing — that it should not break apart, such a state does not exist."

body.text:
46.1 atha kauśināgarā mallā yāvat k(u)śinagaryāṃ gandhaṃ mālyaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ vādya(ṃ) tat sarv(aṃ samudānīya saputradārāḥ sadāsīdāsapauruṣeyāḥ samitrāmātyajñātisālohitāḥ kuśina)garyā niṣkramya y(e)na yamakaśālavanaṃ ten(o)pajagm(uḥ ||)
46.2 u(pe)tya bh(a)gavataḥ siṃhaśayyāṃ gan(dh)air (mā)l(y)aiḥ (puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkurvanti guru)kurvanti māna(yan)t(i) pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text:
46.1 Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, having gathered whatever perfume, garlands, flowers, incense, and music there was in <s>Kuśinagara</s> — together with their sons and wives, their male and female servants and attendants, their friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relations — went forth from <s>Kuśinagara</s> and proceeded to the grove of twin <s>śāla</s> trees.
46.2 Having approached, they honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the <s>Bhagavān's</s> lion-couch (<s>siṃhaśayyā</s>) with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music.

body.text:
46.3 athānyatra utsadaḥ kauśināgaro malla āyuṣ(ma)ntam ānandam idam (avocat ||)
46.4 (kathaṃ bhadantānanda puna)r bhagavataḥ śar(ī)rapūjāyām au(tsukyam āpadyemahi ||)
46.5 tadyathā vāsiṣṭhā rājñaś cakravartino yathā ||
body.translated_text:
46.3 Then a certain <s>Malla</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> named <s>Utsada</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> with these words:
46.4 "How, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, should we undertake the eagerness for the worship of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body?"
46.5 "As for a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning) king, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>."

body.text:
46.6 kathaṃ bhadantānanda (rājñaś cakravartinaḥ ||)
46.7 (vāsiṣṭhā rājña)ś cakravartinaḥ kāyo vihataiḥ (karpāsair veṣṭyate || vihataiḥ) karpāsair veṣṭayitvā pañcabhir yugaśatair veṣṭyate || pañcabhir yugaśatai(r veṣṭayitvā tailapūrṇāyām ayo)dro(ṇ)y(āṃ) n(i)kṣip(yānyayāyodroṇyā pracchādya) gandhakāṣṭhaiś citā(ṃ) citvā dhyāpyate govatā kṣīreṇa nirvāpyate || tāny asthīni s(auvarṇe kuṃbhe prakṣipya sauvarṇ)y(āṃ śi)vikāyām āro(pya caturmahāpathe śarīrastū)paḥ pratiṣṭhāpyate cchatradhvajapatākāś c(ā)r(o)py(an)te mahaś ca prasthāpyat(e) gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair (dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkri)yate gurukriy(a)te mānyate pūjyate ||
body.translated_text:
46.6 "How is it done for a <s>cakravartin</s> king, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>?"
46.7 "O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, the body of a <s>cakravartin</s> king is wrapped in carded cotton; having wrapped it in carded cotton, it is wrapped in five hundred pairs of cloth; having wrapped it in five hundred pairs of cloth, it is placed in an iron oil-trough filled with oil, covered with another iron trough, and a funeral pyre is built with fragrant wood and set ablaze; it is quenched with cow's milk. Those bones are placed in a golden urn, mounted upon a golden palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>), and a <s>śarīrastūpa</s> (reliquary shrine) is erected at the crossroads of four great roads. Parasols, banners, and flags are raised, and a great festival is held; it is honored, revered, respected, and worshipped with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music.

body.text: 46.8 (evam eva vāsiṣṭhā) rājñaś cakravartinaḥ || ata uttare tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya ||
body.translated_text: 46.8 "Just so, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, for a <s>cakravartin</s> king — and even more so for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)."

body.text: 47.1 ath(ā)nyataraḥ kauśināga(ro malla āyu)ṣmantam ānandam idam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 47.1 Then a certain <s>Malla</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> with these words:

body.text: 47.2 y(athā khalu va)yaṃ bhadantānandasya (bhā)ṣ(i)tasyārtham ājānīmas tad idam (a)h(ānta)ram a(thavā dvitryahāntaraṃ na samudānayāmaḥ || saptāhāntaraṃ) samudānayit(vā siṃhaśayyāyāṃ va)yaṃ bhagavataḥ ś(arī)rapūjāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 47.2 "As we understand the meaning of the venerable <s>Ānanda's</s> words, we cannot gather these things in one day, or even in two or three days. Having gathered them over seven days, we shall perform the worship of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body upon the lion-couch (<s>siṃhaśayyā</s>)."

body.text:
47.3 e(vam evety āyuṣmata ānandāc chrutvā)
47.4 (tasmin saptāhe bhagavataḥ siṃhaśayyāyāṃ kauśi)nāgarā mallā yā(vat kuśina)garī yāvan nadī hiraṇyavatī yāvad yama(kaśā)lavanaṃ yāvan mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ (caityam atrāntarā dvādaśa yojanāni sāma)ntakena yad ga(n)dh(aṃ mālyaṃ puṣpaṃ) dhūpaṃ vādyaṃ tat sarvaṃ s(amudānayanti || vihatāni karpāsāny ayodroṇīṃ sarvagandhakāṣṭhaṃ sauvarṇakuṃbhaṃ sauvarṇaśivikāṃ ta)c ca samudānayant(i || bhaga)vataḥ śarīraṃ satkurvanti guruku(rvanti mānayanti pūjayanti ||)
47.5 (athānyata)raḥ kauśināgaro m(allaḥ kauśināgarān mallān idam a)vocat ||
body.translated_text:
47.3 "So be it," — thus they heard from the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
47.4 During that week, at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> lion-couch, the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> gathered all the perfume, garlands, flowers, incense, and music from the entire area — as far as <s>Kuśinagara</s>, as far as the river <s>Hiraṇyavatī</s>, as far as the grove of twin <s>śāla</s> trees, as far as the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>, encompassing twelve <s>yojanas</s> in the surrounding region. They also gathered carded cotton, an iron trough, all kinds of fragrant wood, a golden urn, and a golden palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>). They honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body.
47.5 Then a certain <s>Malla</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> addressed the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> with these words:

body.text:
47.6 śṛṇvan(tu) bhavantaḥ kauś(ināgarā mallā gaṇā) vā pūgā vā pariṣ(ado vā || malli)k(āś ca ma)ll(aku)m(ā)r(i)k(ā)ś ca bhagavata(ś cailavitānaṃ vita)nvant(u ||) mallāś (ca ma)llakumārā(ś ca bhagavataḥ śivikāṃ pragṛhṇantu ||) gandhair mālyai(ḥ) puṣpair dhūpai(r vādyair bhagavataḥ śarīraṃ satkurvant)o gurukurvanto mānayantaḥ pūjayantaḥ p(aścimena naga)radvāreṇa kuśi(nagarīṃ praveśayitvā madhyamadhyenānvāhiṇḍayitvā pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa niṣkāsayi)tvā mallānāṃ makuṭabandh(ane) caitye dhyāp(ayantv iti ||)
47.7 tathā bhavatu kauśināgarā mallāḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text:
47.6 "Hear this, noble <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, whether you be guilds, corporations, or assemblies! Let the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> maidens spread the cloth canopy (<s>cailavitāna</s>) over the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Let the <s>Malla</s> men and <s>Malla</s> youths take up the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>). Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music, let them bring it into <s>Kuśinagara</s> through the western gate, convey it through the very center of the city, bring it out through the eastern gate, and cremate it at the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>."
47.7 "So be it!" — the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> assented.

body.text: 47.8 atha mall(i)k(āś ca mallakumārikāś ca bhagavataś cailavitānaṃ vita)nv(an)ti || mallāś ca mallakumā(rāś ca śivi)kāṃ pragrahītukāmā na śaknuvanti pragrahītum ||
body.translated_text: 47.8 Then the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> maidens spread the cloth canopy (<s>cailavitāna</s>) over the <s>Bhagavān</s>. But the <s>Malla</s> men and <s>Malla</s> youths, though wishing to lift the palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>), were unable to lift it.

body.text: 47.9 athāyuṣm(ān aniruddha āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avo)cat ||
body.translated_text: 47.9 Then the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> with these words:

body.text:
47.10 na śakṣyanty āyuṣman(n ānanda kauśināgarā ma)llā bhagavataḥ śivikāṃ pragrahītum || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || devatān(ām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
47.11 (kaś ca bhadantāniruddha de)vatānām abhi(prāyaḥ ||)
47.12 (devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||) mallikāś ca mallakumārikāś ca bhagavataś cailavitānaṃ vitanvant(u || mallāś ca mallakumārāś ca bhagavataḥ śivikāṃ pragṛhṇan)tu || te (vayaṃ gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyair bhagavataḥ śarīraṃ satku)rvanto gurukurvanto mānayantaḥ pūjayantaḥ paścimena nagaradvār(eṇa kuśinagarīṃ praveśayitvā madhyamadhyenānvāhiṇḍayitvā pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa) niṣkāsayitvā mallānāṃ makuṭabandhane caitye dhyāpayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
47.10 "The <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> will not be able to lift the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>), venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. For what reason? It is the wish of the <s>devatās</s> (deities)."
47.11 "And what, venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, is the wish of the <s>devatās</s>?"
47.12 "The wish of the <s>devatās</s> is this: Let the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> maidens spread the cloth canopy (<s>cailavitāna</s>) over the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Let the <s>Malla</s> men and <s>Malla</s> youths take up the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>). We ourselves, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music, shall bring it into <s>Kuśinagara</s> through the western gate, convey it through the very center of the city, bring it out through the eastern gate, and cremate it at the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>."

body.text:
47.13 (tathā bhavatu bhadantāniruddha yathā devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
47.14 athāyuṣm(ān ānandaḥ kauśināgarān mallān idam avocat ||)
47.15 (na śakṣyatha vāsiṣṭhā bhagavat)aḥ śivikāṃ pratigrahītum || tat kasmād dhet(o)ḥ || d(e)vatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
47.13 "So be it, venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, as is the wish of the <s>devatās</s>."
47.14 Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> with these words:
47.15 "You will not be able, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, to lift the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>). For what reason? It is the wish of the <s>devatās</s> (deities)."

body.text:
47.16 kaś ca bhadantānanda devatānā(m abhiprāyaḥ ||)
47.17 (devatānām abhiprāyaḥ || mallikāś ca mallakumārikā)ś ca bhagavata(ś c)ai(la)vi(tānaṃ vitanva)ntu mallāś ca mallakumārāś ca bhagavataḥ śivikāṃ pragṛhṇantu || te (vayaṃ gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyair bhagavataḥ śarī)raṃ satku(r)v(anto) gurukurv(an)to (mānayantaḥ pūjaya)ntaḥ paścimena nagaradvāreṇa kuśinagarīṃ praveśayitvā madhya(madhyenānvāhiṇḍayitvā pūrveṇa na)garadvāreṇa niṣkāsayitvā mallānāṃ makuṭabandhane caitye dhyāpayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
47.16 "And what, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, is the wish of the <s>devatās</s>?"
47.17 "The wish of the <s>devatās</s> is this: Let the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> maidens spread the cloth canopy (<s>cailavitāna</s>) over the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Let the <s>Malla</s> men and <s>Malla</s> youths take up the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>). We ourselves, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music, shall bring it into <s>Kuśinagara</s> through the western gate, convey it through the very center of the city, bring it out through the eastern gate, and cremate it at the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>."

body.text:
47.18 tathā bhavatu bhadantānanda yathā (devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
47.19 (atha mallikāś ca mallakumāri)kāś ca bhagavataś cailavitānaṃ vi(tanvanti || mallāś ca) mallakumārāś ca bhagavataḥ śivikāṃ pragṛhṇanti ||
body.translated_text:
47.18 "So be it, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, as is the wish of the <s>devatās</s>."
47.19 Then the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> maidens spread the cloth canopy (<s>cailavitāna</s>) over the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and the <s>Malla</s> men and <s>Malla</s> youths took up the <s>Bhagavān's</s> palanquin (<s>śivikā</s>).

body.text: 47.20 samana(n)t(arapragṛhītāyāṃ śivikāyāṃ devatā antar)ī(kṣād) d(i)vyāny utpalāni padmāni (kumudāni puṇḍarīkāny a)garucūrṇāni tagaracūrṇ(ā)ni candanacūrṇāni divyān(i) m(andārakap)uṣpāṇi kṣipanti divyāni ca vādyāni sa(ṃ)pravādayanti cailav(i)kṣ(e)paṃ cākārṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 47.20 As the bier was taken up, the deities from the sky cast down divine <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (white water-lilies), <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses), <s>agaru</s>-powder (aloe-wood powder), <s>tagara</s>-powder (rosebay powder), and sandalwood powder, as well as divine <s>Mandāraka</s> flowers; and they played divine music and made offerings of cloth.

body.text: 47.21 ath(ā)ny(ataraḥ kauśināgaro malla)ḥ kauśināgarā(n) mallān (i)dam avocat ||
body.translated_text: 47.21 Then a certain <s>Malla</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> said this to the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>:

body.text: 47.22 pr(atik)ṣ(ipāmo) vayaṃ mānuṣyakāṇi vādyāni divy(ai)r v(ādy)air (bha)gavataḥ śarīrapūjāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 47.22 'Let us set aside the human music! With divine music we shall perform the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body!'

body.text: 47.23 pratikṣipanti (kauśi)nāgarā m(allā mānu)ṣyakāṇi vādyāni divyair gandhair mālyai(ḥ) puṣpair dhūpair vādyair bhagavataḥ śarīraṃ satkurvanto gurukurvanto mānayantaḥ pūjayantaḥ paści(me)na nagaradv(āreṇa kuśi)nagarīṃ praveś(a)yitvā madhyamadhyenānvāhiṇḍayitvā pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa niṣkāsayitvā mallānāṃ makuṭabandhane caitye upanikṣipanti ||
body.translated_text: 47.23 The <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> set aside the human music. With divine fragrances, garlands, flowers, incense, and music, honoring, revering, esteeming, and worshipping the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body, they brought it into <s>Kuśinagarī</s> through the western city gate, carried it through the very center [of the city], brought it out through the eastern city gate, and placed it at the <s>Makuṭabandhana</s> shrine (<s>caitya</s>) of the <s>Mallas</s>.

body.text: 48.1 tena (khalu sama)yena kuśinagarī divyair mandārakaiḥ puṣpair jānumātreṇaughena sphuṭā babhūva ||
body.translated_text: 48.1 At that time, <s>Kuśinagarī</s> was covered with divine <s>Mandāraka</s> flowers up to knee-depth in a torrent.

body.text: 48.2 athānyatara ājīvikas tato divyāni mandārakāṇi puṣpāṇy ādāya pāpāṃ (p)ra(krāntaḥ kenaci)d eva karaṇīyena ||
body.translated_text: 48.2 Then a certain <s>Ājīvika</s> (ascetic of the Ājīvika sect), having taken some of those divine <s>Mandāraka</s> flowers, set out toward <s>Pāpā</s> on some errand.

body.text: 48.3 tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān mahākāś(yapaḥ) pañcaśataparivāro 'ntarā ca pāpām antarā ca kuśinagarīm atrāntarādhvapratipan(no bhagavato śarī)ram avigopitaṃ vanditukāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 48.3 At that time, the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, with a retinue of five hundred, was on the road between <s>Pāpā</s> and <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, wishing to pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body while it was still unobscured.

body.text: 48.4 adrāk(ṣ)īd āyuṣmā(n) mahākāśy(apa)s tam (ā)jīvika(ṃ) pratimārga(m) || dṛṣṭvā ca punar (e)vam āha ||
body.translated_text: 48.4 The Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> saw that <s>Ājīvika</s> coming from the opposite direction. Having seen him, he spoke thus:

body.text:
48.5 kutas tvam ājīvikaitarhy (ā)gacchasi || ku(tra tvaṃ gamiṣyasi ||)
48.6 (ku)ś(i)nagaryā aham etarhy āgacchāmi || p(ā)pāṃ gamiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: 48.5 'Where are you coming from now, <s>Ājīvika</s>? Where are you going?' 48.6 'I am coming now from <s>Kuśinagarī</s>. I am going to <s>Pāpā</s>.'

body.text: 48.7 jānīṣe tvam ājīvika mama śāstāram ||
body.translated_text: 48.7 'Do you know, <s>Ājīvika</s>, my Teacher?'

body.text: 48.8 jāne || śramaṇo gautamaḥ || parinirvṛtas te āyuṣmañ chāstā || adya (gate saptāhe va)rtate śarīre śarīrapūjā || imāni ca me tasmān mandārakapuṣpāṇy ānītāni ||
body.translated_text: 48.8 'I know him. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> — your Teacher, Venerable One, has attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. It is now seven days since his body [was placed] and the funeral worship is [being conducted]. These <s>Mandāraka</s> flowers were brought by me from there.'

body.text: 48.9 athānyataro mahallakas tasyāṃ velāyām idam evaṃrūpam ak(ālabhāṣyaṃ) utsṛṣṭavān ||
body.translated_text: 48.9 Then a certain elder monk, on that occasion, uttered this kind of untimely speech:

body.text: 48.10 muktāḥ smas tataḥ kaukṛtikān mahallāt || ya evam āha || idaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ karaṇīyam idam akaraṇīyam || idānīṃ vayaṃ yad eṣi(ṣyāmas tat ka)r(i)ṣyāma(ḥ) || yan naiṣiṣyāmas tan na kariṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 48.10 'We are freed from that troublesome elder, who used to say: "This, monks, should be done by you; this should not be done." Now we shall do whatever we wish, and whatever we do not wish, we shall not do.'

body.text: 48.11 tat khalv akālabhāṣyaṃ devatā antardhāpayanti yathā tasyāṃ pariṣady ekabhikṣur api nāśrauṣīt s(thā)payitvā(yuṣmantaṃ ma)hākāśyapam ||
body.translated_text: 48.11 The deities caused that untimely speech to vanish, so that not a single monk in that assembly heard it — except for the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>.

body.text:
48.12 tatraikatyā bhikṣavaḥ pṛthivyām ā(va)rt(a)nte parivartante || ekatyā b(ā)hūn pragṛhya prakrośanti || evam cāh(u)ḥ || atikṣipraṃ bhagavān (parini)rv(ṛtaḥ || atikṣipraṃ) sugataḥ parinirvṛtaḥ || atikṣip(r)aṃ cak(ṣu)r lokas(y)ā(ntarhitaḥ ||)
48.13 (athāyuṣmā)n m(a)h(ā)k(ā)śy(apas) t(a)sy(ā) vā(cāyā evamasaṃyatāyā vinodanāya mārgād avakramya bhikṣusaṃghasya madhye prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat || niṣadyāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo bhikṣūn āman)tr(a)y(ate ||)
48.14 (an)ityā āyuṣmantaḥ sarvasaṃskārā a(dhru)vā an(āśvasikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ sarvasaṃskārā yāvad alam eva sarvasaṃskārebhyo nirvettum alaṃ virak)tum alaṃ vimoktum ||
body.translated_text: 48.12 Thereupon some monks rolled and writhed on the ground; some, raising their arms, cried out loudly, and spoke thus: 'Too quickly the <s>Bhagavān</s> has attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the <s>Sugata</s> has attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>! Too quickly the eye of the world has vanished!' 48.13 Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, in order to dispel that unrestrained speech, stepped aside from the road, sat down in the very seat prepared in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, and, having sat down, addressed the monks: 48.14 'Impermanent, Venerable Ones, are all conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — unstable, unreliable, subject to change. All conditioned formations are such that one should be sufficiently wearied of them, sufficiently dispassionate toward them, sufficiently liberated from them.'

body.text: 48.15 tvarit(aṃ) tvaritam āyuṣmanto bhikṣavaḥ par(ākramantu || bhagavataḥ śarīram avigopitaṃ draṣṭuṃ gacchāmaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: 48.15 'Quickly, quickly, Venerable Monks, let us exert ourselves! Let us go to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body while it is still unobscured!'

body.text:
49.1 (atha kauśināgarā mallā bhagavataḥ śarīraṃ vihataiḥ karpāsair veṣṭayitvā pañcabhir yugaśatair veṣṭayitvā tailapūrṇāyām ayodroṇyāṃ prakṣipyānyayāyodroṇyā pracchādya sarvaga)ndhakāṣṭhaiś citāṃ citvā prajvālayitukāmā na ś(aknuvanti prajvālayitum ||)
49.2 (athāyuṣmān aniruddha āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat ||)
49.3 (na śakṣyanti kauśin)āgarā mallā bhagavataś citāṃ prajvālayit(um || tat kasmād dhetoḥ || devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
49.4 (kaś ca bhadantāniruddha devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
49.5 (devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||) āy(u)ṣmān mahākāśyapa(ḥ) pañcaśataparivār(o 'ntarā ca pāpām antarā ca kuśinagarīm atrāntarādhvapratipanno bhagavato śarīram avigopitaṃ vanditukāmaḥ ||)
49.6 (tathā bhavatu bhadantāniruddha yathā devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
49.7 (athāyuṣmān ā)nandaḥ kauśināgarān mallān i(dam avocat ||)
49.8 (na śakṣyatha vāsiṣṭhā bhagavataś citāṃ prajvālayitum || tad kasmād dhetoḥ || devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
49.9 (kaś ca bhadantānanda devatānām abhi)p(r)āyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 49.1 Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, having wrapped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body with unraveled cotton, having wrapped it in five hundred pairs [of cloth], having placed it in an iron oil-trough filled with oil, having covered it with another iron trough, having built a funeral pyre with all kinds of fragrant wood, wished to ignite it — [but] they were unable to ignite it. 49.2 Then the Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 49.3 'The <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> will not be able to ignite the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s funeral pyre. For what reason? Because of the deities' intention.' 49.4 'And what, Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, is the deities' intention?' 49.5 'The deities' intention is this: The Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, with a retinue of five hundred, is on the road between <s>Pāpā</s> and <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, wishing to pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body while it is still unobscured.' 49.6 'Let it be so, Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, as is the deities' intention.' 49.7 Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>: 49.8 'You will not be able, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, to ignite the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s funeral pyre. For what reason? Because of the deities' intention.' 49.9 'And what, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, is the deities' intention?'

body.text:
49.10 dev(a)t(ānām abhiprāyaḥ || āyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ pañcaśataparivāro 'ntarā ca pāpām antarā ca kuśinagarīm atrāntarādhvapratipanno bhagavato) ś(a)r(īram avigopitaṃ vanditukāmaḥ ||)
49.11 (tathā bhavatu bhadantānanda yathā devatānām abhiprāyaḥ ||)
49.12 (athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo 'nukrameṇa prāpya kuśinaga)r(īṃ) yena bhagavataś citā t(enopajagāma ||)
(adrākṣīt) pariṣad āyuṣma(n)ta(ṃ) mahā(kā)śyapa(ṃ) dūrata eva ||
body.translated_text: 49.10 'The deities' intention is this: The Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, with a retinue of five hundred, is on the road between <s>Pāpā</s> and <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, wishing to pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body while it is still unobscured.' 49.11 'Let it be so, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, as is the deities' intention.' 49.12 Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, arriving in due course at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s funeral pyre. The assembly saw the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> from afar.

body.text: 49.13 dṛṣṭvā ca punar y(enāyuṣmān mahā)kāśyapas ten(o)pasa(ṅ)krāntā || upetyāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapa(ṃ) pṛṣṭhata(ḥ) pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā ||
body.translated_text: 49.13 Having seen him, they approached the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> and followed behind him, one after another.

body.text:
49.14 athāyuṣmān ma(hā)kāśyapo yena bhagavataś citā te(nopajagāma ||)
49.15 (u)p(e)tya tailapūrṇām ayodroṇiṃ vigopa(ya)ti pañcayugaśatāni vigopayati vihatāni karpāsāni vigopayati vihatāni karpāsāni v(igopayitvā bha)gavataḥ śarīram avigopitaṃ vandate ||
body.translated_text: 49.14 Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s funeral pyre. 49.15 Having approached, he uncovered the oil-filled iron trough, uncovered the five hundred pairs [of cloth], uncovered the unraveled cotton — and having uncovered the unraveled cotton, he paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body, [now] unobscured.

body.text:
49.16 tena khalu samayena pṛthivy(āṃ) catvāro mahāsthavirā abhūvan tadyathāyuṣmān ājñātakauṇḍ(iṇya āyu)ṣmān mahācunda āyuṣmān daśabalakāśyapa āyuṣmān mahākāśya(paḥ ||)
49.17 teṣām āyuṣmān mahākāśyapo jñāto ma(hā)puṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayan(āsana)gl(ā)napratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām ||
body.translated_text: 49.16 At that time, there were four great elders (<s>mahāsthavira</s>) on earth — namely, the Venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍiṇya</s>, the Venerable <s>Mahācunda</s>, the Venerable <s>Daśabalakāśyapa</s>, and the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>. 49.17 Among them, the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> was known as one of great merit, a receiver of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick.

body.text: 49.18 athā(yu)ṣmato (ma)hākāśya(pa)syaitad abhavat ||
body.translated_text: 49.18 Then this thought arose in the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>:

body.text:
49.19 yannv ahaṃ svayam eva bhagavataḥ śarīrapūjāyām autsukyam āpedyey(a ||)
49.20 (athāyu)ṣmān mahākāśyapo 'nyāni vihatāni (ka)rpāsā(ny) anyāni pañcayugaśatāni samudānīya bhagavataḥ śarīraṃ vihataiḥ karp(ā)sair v(e)ṣṭa(yitvā pañca)bh(i)r yuga(śatair veṣṭayitvā tailapūrṇāyām ayodroṇyāṃ prakṣipyānya)yāyodroṇyā pracchādya sarvagandhakāṣṭhaiś citāṃ citvaikānte 'pakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 49.19 'Let me myself undertake the eagerness for the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body.' 49.20 Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having brought other unraveled cotton and other five hundred pairs [of cloth], wrapped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body with unraveled cotton, wrapped it in five hundred pairs [of cloth], placed it in the oil-filled iron trough, covered it with another iron trough, built a funeral pyre with all kinds of fragrant wood, and then withdrew to one side.

body.text: 49.21 atha sā ci(tā svaya)m eva prajvalitā (ya)thāpi (tad buddhasya buddhānubhāvena de)vatānāṃ (ca) d(e)v(a)tānubhāvena ||
body.translated_text: 49.21 Then that funeral pyre ignited of its own accord — as if by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power (<s>buddhānubhāva</s>) and by the power of the deities (<s>devatānubhāva</s>).

body.text: 49.22 athāyuṣmān ānandas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ citām anu(kramaṅ) gā(the) babhāṣe ||
body.translated_text: 49.22 Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, on that occasion, gazing upon the funeral pyre, spoke these verses:

body.text:
49.23 yena kāyaratn(e)n(a nā)yako
  brahmalokam agaman maharddhikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 49.23 'By means of that body-jewel, the Guide, of great supernatural power, went to the <s>Brahma</s>-world.'

body.text:
dīpyate svatanujena tejasā
  pañcabhir yugaśataiḥ sa veṣ(ṭ)i(taḥ |)
49.24 (sahasra)mātreṇa hi cīvarāṇāṃ
  buddhasya k(ā)yaḥ pariveṣṭito 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: 'He blazes with the radiance born of his own body, wrapped in five hundred pairs [of cloth].' 49.24 'With a full thousand garments was the <s>Buddha</s>'s body enshrouded.'

children.text: dve cīvare tatra tu naiva dagdhe
children.translated_text: 'Two garments there were not burned —
the innermost and the second, the outermost.'

children.text: 49.25 atha kauśināgarā ma(llā govatā kṣī)r(e)ṇa nirvāpayanti || tatra catvār(o) v(ṛ)kṣā(ḥ) prādurbhūtā(ḥ) kāñcanaḥ kapi(ttho 'śvattha) udumbaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 49.25 Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> extinguished [the pyre] with cow's milk. There, four trees appeared — a golden <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple), an <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), and an <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig).

body.text: 49.26 atha kauśinā(ga)rā mallās tāny asthīni sauvarṇe kuṃ(bhe) prakṣipya sauvarṇyāṃ śivikāyām āropya gandhai(r) m(ā)ly(ai)ḥ (p)uṣ(p)air dh(ū)pair vādyaiḥ satkurvanto (gurukurvanto mānayanto pūjayanto nagaraṃ praveśya ta)sm(i)n (a)grāgā(r)e (mahāma)ṇḍala upanik(ṣ)ip(ya gandh)ai(r mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayanti ||)
body.translated_text: 49.26 Then the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>, placing those bones in a golden vessel, mounting it upon a golden palanquin, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music, entered the city, placed it in that foremost hall upon a great platform, and continued to honor, revere, respect, and worship with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music.

body.text:
50.1 (aśrauṣuḥ pāpīyakā mallāḥ || parinirvṛtaḥ kuśinagaryāṃ buddho bhagavān || adya gate saptāhe vartate śarīre śarīrapūjā ||)
50.2 (śrutvā ca caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ yena kauśināgarā mallās tenopajagmuḥ ||)
50.3 (upetya kauśināgarān mallān idam avocan ||)
50.4 (śṛṇvantu bhadantaḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā || dīrgharātraṃ sa bhagavān asmākaṃ priyaś cābhū)n m(anāpaś ca ||) bhavatāṃ grāmakṣe(tre parinirvṛtaḥ ||)
50.5 (arhāmo vayaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu śarīrabhāgaṃ yena pāpāyāṃ bhavataḥ) śarīrast(ūpaṃ) pr(atiṣṭhāpa)yiṣyāmaś chatradhvajapatā(kāṃś cāropayiṣyāmo mahāṃś ca prasthāpayiṣyāmo gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ) s(at)kari(ṣ)yāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānay(iṣyā)ma(ḥ) pūjayiṣyā(maḥ ||)
50.6 (yat khalu vāsiṣṭhā jānīyāta || asmākam api sa bhagavān priyaś cābhūn ma)nāpaś ca || asmākaṃ gr(ā)makṣetre pari(ni)rvṛtaḥ || nārhāmo vayaṃ (p)r(adātuṃ bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu bhāgam ||)
50.7 (saced dattam evaṃ sādhu || yadi vā na dāsyatha senayāpahariṣyāmaḥ ||)
50.8 (ta)th(ā bhavatu) kauśināg(arā mallāḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ ||)
50.9 (aśrauṣuś ca calakalpakā bulakā viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā rāmagrāmīyakāḥ krauḍyā vaiśālakā licchavayaḥ kāpilavāstavyāḥ śākyāḥ ||)
50.10 (aśrauṣīc ca rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputraḥ || parinirvṛtaḥ kuśinagaryāṃ buddho bhagavān || pāpīyakā mallāś calakalpakā bulakā viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā rāmagr)āmīyakāḥ krauḍyā vai(śālakā licchavayaḥ kāpilavāstavyāḥ śākyāḥ kuśinagarīm upasaṃkrāntā yena śarīrapūjā śarīrabhāgasyāharaṇāya ||)
50.11 (śru)tvā ca punar varṣākāraṃ (brāhmaṇa)magadhamahām(āt)r(am idaṃ avocat ||)
50.12 (jānīṣe tvaṃ varṣākāra || aśrauṣam ahaṃ || parinirvṛtaḥ kuśinagaryāṃ buddho bhagavān || pāpīyakā mallāś calakalpakā bulakā viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā rāmagrāmīyakāḥ krauḍyā vaiśālakā licchavayaḥ kāpilavāstavyāḥ śākyāś caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya kuśinagarīm upasaṃkrāntā yena śarīrapūjā śarīrabhāgasyāharaṇāya || tasmād vayam api caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya bhagavataḥ śarīrabhāgam āhariṣyāmaḥ ||)
50.13 (sannāhayāmi deveti varṣākāraḥ pratiśrutya caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhayati ||)
50.14 (rājājātaśatrur hastyārūḍho bhagavato guṇam anusmaran mūrchitaḥ || hastino 'varopyāśvam āropya tatrāpi mūrchitaḥ || sa idam avocat ||)
50.15 (ahaṃ gantum asamarthaḥ || gaccha tvaṃ varṣākāra caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya) yena kauśināgarā (mallā)s tenopasaṃkram(a ||) u(petyāsmākaṃ vacanena kauśināgarān mallān alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchālpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca) yātrāñ ca balaṃ ca sukh(a)ṃ (cānava)dyatāṃ ca sparśa(vihāratāṃ ca || evaṃ ca vada ||)
50.16 (dīrgharātraṃ sa bhagavān asmākaṃ priyaś cābhūn manāpaś ca || bhavatāṃ grāmakṣetre parinirvṛtaḥ || ar)hāmo vayaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu śarīrabhāgaṃ ye(na rājagṛhe bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaś chatradhvajapatākāṃś cāropayiṣyāmo mahāṃś ca prasthāpayi)ṣyāmo gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair (dhūp)air (v)ā(dy)ai(ḥ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ ||)
50.17 (evaṃ deveti varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro rājño māgadhasyā)j(ā)taśatror vaid(e)h(īputrasya pratiśrutya caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pa)tt(i)kāyaṃ yena kauśin(ā)garā mallās tenopajāgama ||
body.translated_text:
50.1 The <s>Pāpīyaka</s> <s>Mallās</s> heard: "The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>. Now, seven days having passed, the worship of the bodily relics is taking place."
50.2 Having heard, they equipped their fourfold army — the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — and approached the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>.
50.3 Having approached, they said this to the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>:
50.4 "Let the honorable <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> hear — whether assemblies, groups, guilds, or congregations: for a long time the <s>Bhagavat</s> was dear and agreeable to us. He has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of your village."
50.5 "We are worthy of a share of the bodily relics of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, so that in <s>Pāpā</s> we may erect a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) for the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s relics, raise parasols, banners, and flags, dispatch great offerings, and honor, revere, respect, and worship with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music."
50.6 "Know this, O <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>: the <s>Bhagavat</s> was also dear and agreeable to us. He attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of our village. We are not willing to give away a share of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s bodily relics."
50.7 "If it is given, well and good. If you will not give, we shall seize it by force."
50.8 "So be it," the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> assented.
50.9 And the <s>Calakalpaka</s>, <s>Bulaka</s>, and <s>Viṣṇudvīpīya</s> <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Rāmagrāmīyas</s>, the <s>Krauḍyas</s>, the <s>Vaiśālaka</s> <s>Licchavis</s>, and the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> also heard.
50.10 And King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, also heard: "The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>. The <s>Pāpīyaka</s> <s>Mallās</s>, <s>Calakalpaka</s>, <s>Bulaka</s>, and <s>Viṣṇudvīpīya</s> <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Rāmagrāmīyas</s>, <s>Krauḍyas</s>, <s>Vaiśālaka</s> <s>Licchavis</s>, and the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> have approached <s>Kuśinagarī</s> for the worship of the relics and to claim a share of the bodily relics."
50.11 Having heard, he then said this to <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> great minister of <s>Magadha</s>:
50.12 "Do you know, <s>Varṣākāra</s>? I have heard that the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>. The <s>Pāpīyaka</s> <s>Mallās</s>, <s>Calakalpaka</s>, <s>Bulaka</s>, and <s>Viṣṇudvīpīya</s> <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Rāmagrāmīyas</s>, <s>Krauḍyas</s>, <s>Vaiśālaka</s> <s>Licchavis</s>, and the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, having equipped their fourfold armies, have approached <s>Kuśinagarī</s> for the worship of the relics and to claim a share of the bodily relics. Therefore, let us also equip our fourfold army and bring back a share of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s bodily relics."
50.13 "I shall equip it, Your Majesty," <s>Varṣākāra</s> assented, and equipped the fourfold army.
50.14 King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having mounted an elephant, recollecting the virtues of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, fainted. Having been taken down from the elephant and placed upon a horse, he fainted there too. He then said:
50.15 "I am unable to go. You go, <s>Varṣākāra</s>, equipping the fourfold army — elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — and approach the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>. Having approached, inquire in our name after the health of the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> — whether they have few ailments, few afflictions, are light in rising, have ease of travel, strength, happiness, blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling. And say thus:"
50.16 "'For a long time the <s>Bhagavat</s> was dear and agreeable to us. He has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of your village. We are worthy of a share of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s bodily relics, so that in <s>Rājagṛha</s> we may erect a <s>stūpa</s> for the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s relics, raise parasols, banners, and flags, dispatch great offerings, and honor, revere, respect, and worship with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music.'"
50.17 "So be it, Your Majesty," <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> great minister of <s>Magadha</s>, having assented to King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, equipped the fourfold army — elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — and approached the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>.

body.text:
50.18 u(pe)tya kauśināgarān m(allān idam avocat ||)
50.19 (śṛṇvantu bhadantaḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā || rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīpu)tro bhav(a)tāṃ a(lpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchaty alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāñ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca || evaṃ ca vadati ||)
50.20 dīrgharātraṃ sa bhagavā(n asmākaṃ) priyaś cābh(ūn manāpaś ca || bhavatāṃ grāmakṣetre parinirvṛtaḥ || arhāmo vayaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu śarīrabhāgaṃ yena rājagṛhe bha)gavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhā(payiṣ)y(ā)ma(ś cha)tradhvajapatā(kāṃś cāropayiṣyāmo mahāṃś ca prasthāpayiṣyāmo gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyā)maḥ ||
body.translated_text:
50.18 Having approached, he said this to the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>:
50.19 "Let the honorable <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> hear — whether assemblies, groups, guilds, or congregations: King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, inquires after your health — whether you have few ailments, few afflictions, are light in rising, have ease of travel, strength, happiness, blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling. And he says thus:"
50.20 "'For a long time the <s>Bhagavat</s> was dear and agreeable to us. He has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of your village. We are worthy of a share of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s bodily relics, so that in <s>Rājagṛha</s> we may erect a <s>stūpa</s> for the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s relics, raise parasols, banners, and flags, dispatch great offerings, and honor, revere, respect, and worship with perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, and music.'"

body.text:
50.21 yat khalu bhavā(n varṣākāro jānīyāt || asmākam api sa bhagavān priyaś cābhūn manāpaś ca ||) asmākaṃ (grāmakṣetre parinirvṛtaḥ || nārhāmo vayaṃ pradātuṃ bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu śarīrabhāgam ||)
50.22 (atha varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātraḥ kauśināgarān mallān idam avocat ||)
50.23 (saced dattam evaṃ sādhu || ya)di vā na (d)āsya(tha senayāpahariṣyāmaḥ ||)
50.24 (tathā bhavatu kauśināgarā mallāḥ pratiśrutya rājñāṃ saṃghaṃ gaṇaṃ pariṣadam avalokya mallikā mallakumārāṃś ca dhanurvidyām upadiśanti ||)
50.25 (yāvat pāpīyakā mallāś calakalpakā bulakā viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā rāmagrāmīyakāḥ krauḍyā vaiśālakā licchavayaḥ kāpilavāstavyāḥ śākyā varṣākāraś ca magadhamahāmātraś caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānāṃ purastāt saṃgrāmāya vyūḍhās)
50.26 (tāvat kauśināgarā mallā malllikā mallakumārāś ca caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ bahir nagaryāḥ śatroḥ saptakabalakāyasya purastāt saṃgrāmāyāpi vyūḍhāḥ ||)
body.translated_text:
50.21 "Know this, honorable <s>Varṣākāra</s>: the <s>Bhagavat</s> was also dear and agreeable to us. He attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the territory of our village. We are not willing to give away a share of the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s bodily relics."
50.22 Then <s>Varṣākāra</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> great minister of <s>Magadha</s>, said this to the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>:
50.23 "If it is given, well and good. If you will not give, we shall seize it by force."
50.24 "So be it," the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s> assented, and surveying the assembly, group, and congregation of kings, they instructed the <s>Malla</s> women and <s>Malla</s> princes in the art of archery.
50.25 Meanwhile, the <s>Pāpīyaka</s> <s>Mallās</s>, <s>Calakalpaka</s>, <s>Bulaka</s>, and <s>Viṣṇudvīpīya</s> <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Rāmagrāmīyas</s>, <s>Krauḍyas</s>, <s>Vaiśālaka</s> <s>Licchavis</s>, the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, and <s>Varṣākāra</s> the great minister of <s>Magadha</s>, having equipped their fourfold armies — elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — were drawn up for battle in front of the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>.
50.26 Thereupon the <s>Kauśināgara</s> <s>Mallās</s>, the <s>Malla</s> women, and the <s>Malla</s> princes, having equipped their fourfold army — elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry — were drawn up for battle outside the city, facing the seven-fold army of the enemy.

body.text:
51.1 (tena khalu samayena dhūmrasagotro brāhmaṇas tasyāṃ ca pariṣadi sanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt sanni)patitaḥ || atha dhūmrasagotro brāhmaṇa ubhayato vyūhag(e)ṣu s(aṃ)grāmānīk(e)ṣv (aciram anyonyavipraghātikāṃ kariṣyantīti vi)d(i)tvāj(i)n(aṃ daṇḍa)k(e ropa)yamāṇo yena kauśinā(ga)rā mallās tenopajagāma || upe(tya k)au(śinā)garān mall(ān idam avocat ||)
51.2 (śṛṇvantu) bhavantaḥ kauśināgarā mallāḥ s(a)ṃ(ghā vā ga)ṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado (vā ||)
(dīr)gh(a)rāt(r)aṃ sa bhagavān vīta(rā)gaḥ kṣemaś cā(bhūt kṣāntipraśaṃsī kṣāntivādī || yad vītarāgasya kṣemasya kṣāntipraśaṃsinaḥ kṣāntivādino vācaṃ vikurvanto bhavantas ta)sy(a) bhavato gautamasya śarīrakāraṇ(ād anyonyavipraghātikāṃ kartum udyuktā apratirūpam || ahaṃ bhavato gautamasya śarīrāṇy aṣṭadhā vibhaktum autsukyam āpatsye || yasmiṃs tu kuṃbhe tāny asthīni prakṣi)ptāni bhavanti sa (ku)ṃbho 'smāka(m anupradātuṃ yena) vayaṃ dro(ṇagrāmake bhagavataḥ kuṃbha)stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaś chatradhvajapatā(kāṃś cāropayiṣyāmo mahāṃś ca prasthāpayiṣyāmo gandhair) mālyai(ḥ) puṣ(p)ai(r dhūmai)r vādyaiḥ sat(kariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ ||)
51.3 t(athā) bhavatu kauśināgarā mallā (dhūmrasagotrasya brāhmaṇasya) pr(a)t(yaśrauṣuḥ ||)
51.4 (atha dhūmrasagotro brāhmaṇo yena pāpīyakā ma)llāś (ca)la(kalpa)kā (bulakā viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā rāmagrāmīyakāḥ) kr(au)ḍy(ā vai)śālakā l(i)cchavayaḥ kāpilav(āstavyāḥ śākyā varṣākāro brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātras te)nopajagāma ||
body.translated_text: 51.1 At that time, the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra was seated and gathered in that assembly. Then the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra, having served in battle formations arrayed on both sides, not long ago ...

body.text:
51.5 upe(tya varṣākāraṃ brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātram idam avocat ||)
51.6 yat khalu varṣākāra jānīyā(ḥ ||) dīrgharātraṃ s(a bhagavān vītarāgaḥ kṣemaś cābhūt kṣāntipraśaṃsī kṣāntivādī || yad vītarāgasya kṣemasya kṣāntipraśaṃsinaḥ kṣāntivādino vācaṃ vikurvan)to bhavantas tasya bhav(ato) gautamasya (śa)r(īrakāra)ṇād anyonyavipraghātikāṃ kartum udyu(kt)ā (apratirūpam || ahaṃ bhavato gautamasya śarīrāṇy aṣṭadhā vibhaktum autsukyam āpatsye || yasmiṃ)s tu kuṃbhe tāny asthīni prakṣiptāni bhavanti sa kuṃbho 'smā(kam anupradātuṃ ye)n(a) v(a)y(aṃ) droṇagrāmake (bha)gavataḥ kuṃbh(astūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpa)y(i)ṣyāma(ś chatradhvajapatākāṃś cāropayiṣyāmo mahāṃś ca prasthāpayiṣyāmo gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair(?) dhūmair vādyaiḥ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ p)ū(ja)yiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
51.5 Having approached, he said this to the Brahmin Varṣākāra, chief minister of Magadha:
51.6 'May the honorable Varṣākāra know this: for a long time that Bhagavān was free from passion, was peaceful, was a praiser of patience, an advocate of patience ...'

body.text:
51.7 tathā bhavatu varṣākār(o brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātro dhūmrasagotrasya brāhmaṇasya pratyaśrauṣīt ||)
51.8 (atha dhūmrasagotro brāhmaṇo bhagavataḥ śarīrāṇy aṣṭadhā bheje ||)
51.9 atha dhūmrasagotro brāhmaṇa ekaṃ bhāgaṃ kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānām anuprayaccha(ti yena kauśi)nāgarā mallā kuśinagaryāṃ bha(gavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhā)payanti cchatradhvajapatākāṃś cāropayanti mahāṃś ca prasthāpayanti gandhair mālyai(ḥ) puṣpair dhūpair (v)ād(y)ai(ḥ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pū)jayanti ||
body.translated_text:
51.7 'So be it' — the Brahmin Varṣākāra, chief minister of Magadha, assented to the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra.
51.8 Then the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra divided the Bhagavān's bodily relics into eight portions.
51.9 ...

body.text: 51.10 dvitīyaṃ bhāgaṃ pāpīyakānāṃ mallānām anuprayacchati yena pāpīyak(ā) m(a)llāḥ pāpāyā(ṃ) bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayan(ti) pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.10 He gives the second portion to the Mallas of Pāpīyaka, by which the Mallas of Pāpīyaka erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Pāpā, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.11 tṛitīyaṃ bhāgaṃ calakalpakānā(ṃ) bulakānām anuprayacchati yena calakalpakā bulakāś calakalpāyāṃ bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.11 He gives the third portion to the Bulakas of Calakalpaka, by which the Bulakas of Calakalpaka erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Calakalpā, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.12 caturthaṃ bhāgaṃ viṣṇudvīpīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇānām anuprayacchati yena viṣṇudvīpīyakā brāhmaṇā viṣṇudvīpe bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.12 He gives the fourth portion to the Brahmins of Viṣṇudvīpīyaka, by which the Brahmins of Viṣṇudvīpīyaka erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Viṣṇudvīpa, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.13 pañcamaṃ bhāgaṃ rāmagrāmīyakāṇāṃ krauḍyānām anuprayacchati yena rāmagrāmīyakāḥ krauḍyā rāmagrāmake bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.13 He gives the fifth portion to the Krauḍyas of Rāmagrāmīyaka, by which the Krauḍyas of Rāmagrāmīyaka erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Rāmagrāmaka, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.14 ṣaṣṭhaṃ bhāgaṃ vaiśālakānā(ṃ) licchavīnām anuprayacchati yena vaiśālakā licchavayo vaiśālyāṃ bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.14 He gives the sixth portion to the Licchavīs of Vaiśālī, by which the Licchavīs of Vaiśālī erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Vaiśālī, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.15 saptamaṃ bhāgaṃ kāpilavāstavyānāṃ śākyānām anuprayacchati yena kāpilavāstavyāḥ śākyāḥ kapilavastuni bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pūrvavad yāvat pūjayanti ||
body.translated_text: 51.15 He gives the seventh portion to the Śākyas of Kapilavastu, by which the Śākyas of Kapilavastu erect a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Kapilavastu, as before, up to: and worship it.

body.text: 51.15 aṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ varṣākārasya brāhmaṇamagadhamahāmātrasyānuprayacchati yena rājā māgadho 'jātaśatrur vaidehīputro rājagṛhe bhagavataḥ śarīrastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati cchatradhvajapatākāṃś cāropayati mahāṃś ca prasthāpayati gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkaroti gurukaro(t)i mā(na)yati pūjayati ||
body.translated_text: 51.15 He gives the eighth portion to the Brahmin Varṣākāra, chief minister of Magadha, by which King Ajātaśatru of Magadha, son of Vaidehī, erects a stūpa of the Bhagavān's relics at Rājagṛha, with parasols and banners ...

body.text: 51.17 yasmiṃs tu kuṃbhe tāny asthīni prakṣiptāni bhavanti taṃ kuṃbhaṃ dhūmrasagotrāya brāhmaṇāyānuprayacchanti yena dhūmrasagotro brāhm(aṇo droṇagrāmake kuṃ)bhastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati pūrvavad yāvat pūjayati ||
body.translated_text: 51.17 As for the vessel in which those bones were deposited — that vessel they give to the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra, by which the Brahmin Dhūmrasagotra erects a vessel-stūpa (<s>kumbhastūpa</s>) at Droṇagrāmaka, as before, up to: and worships it.

body.text:
51.18 tena (khalu samayena) p(i)ppalāyano māṇavas tasyāṃ ca pariṣadi s(anniṣaṇṇo 'hūt sannipatitaḥ ||)
51.19 (a)tha pippalāyano māṇavaḥ kauśināgarān mallān idam avoc(at ||)
51.20 (śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kauśināgarā ma)llāḥ saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā (pariṣado vā || dīrgharātraṃ sa bhavāṅ g)au(tamo 'smākaṃ pr)i(ya)ś (c)ābh(ū)n manāpaś (ca ||) bhavatāṃ g(r)āmakṣetre parinirvṛtaḥ || arhāmo v(ayaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ śarīreṣu śarīrabhāgam || idānīṃ vibhakteṣu śarīreṣu ye jvalanasyāṅgārās te) 'smākam anupradātuṃ yair aṅgā(rastūpaṃ bha)vat(o) g(au)tamasya (pippalavatyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyām)i cch(atra)dh(va)japatākāṃ(ś cāropayiṣyāmi mahāṃś ca prasthāpayiṣyā)m(i) gandhai(r) mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair vādyaiḥ satkariṣyāmi gurukariṣyā(mi mānayiṣyāmi pūjayiṣyāmi ||)
51.21 (anuprayacchanti) kauśināgarā (mal)l(āḥ pippalāya)nāya māṇavāy(a śarīrāṇām aṅgā)rān yaiḥ pippalāyano māṇava(ḥ p)ippalavatyāṃ aṅgarast(ūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpa)yati cchatradhvajapatākāṃś cāropayati mahāṃś ca prasthā(payati gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpair dhūpai)r vādyai(ḥ) satkaroti gurukaro(ti māna)yati pūjayiṣyati ||
body.translated_text:
51.18 At that time, the young Brahmin Pippalāyana was seated and gathered in that assembly.
51.19 Then the young Brahmin Pippalāyana said this to the Mallas of Kuśinagara:
51.20 ...

body.text: 51.22 tena kha(lu samayena jam)b(u)dvīpe bhagavato 'ṣṭau śarīrastūpā abhūvan n(avamaś ca kumbhastūpo daśamaś cā)ṅgārastūpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 51.22 At that time, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, there were eight relic-stūpas of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, a ninth vessel-stūpa (<s>kumbhastūpa</s>), and a tenth ember-stūpa (<s>aṅgārastūpa</s>).

body.text:
51.23 iyaṃ atra dharmatā || tasmād idam ucyate
  cakṣuṣmato 'ṣṭau droṇ(āḥ śarirāṇāṃ
  jambudvī)pe sapta pūjāṃ labhante ||

children.translated_text: and one measure of the Supreme Person's [relics]
is worshipped at <s>Rāmagrāma</s> by the <s>Nāga</s> king.'
51.24 'The four canine teeth of the Supreme Person —
one tooth is worshipped in the world of the Thirty-three (<s>Tridaśa</s>) gods;

body.text:
d(v)itīy(ā gandhārapure manora)me
  kaliṅgarājño vi(j)i(te tṛt)īyā ||
body.translated_text:
a second in the beautiful city of <s>Gandhāra</s>;
a third in the domain of the <s>Kaliṅga</s> king;'

body.text:
daṃṣ(ṭr)ā (caturthī puruṣottamasya
  rāmagrāme pūjyate nāgarājñā |)

body.translated_text:
'The fourth tooth of the Supreme Person
is worshipped at <s>Rāmagrāma</s> by the <s>Nāga</s> king.'
